543514|2026-06.headline: Veranda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR150 crore and PAT to INR34 crore, with commerce demerger listing guided for September 2026.
543514|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to about INR150 crore and enrollments rose 35% to about 1.03 lakh students. EBITDA was about INR54 crore with a margin near 36% as stated, but management acknowledged the reported EBITDA growth of 10% was flattered by a INR17 crore one-time other income in Q1 FY26; excluding it, EBITDA grew about 30%. PAT rose to INR34 crore from INR5.9 crore, helped by a INR7.35 crore tax reversal tied to an intra-group merger. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR670 crore revenue, INR260 crore EBITDA and INR144 crore PAT, and said the Commerce demerger NCLT order is expected shortly with listing before end-September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY reported; ~30% excluding Q1 FY26 one-time other income of INR17 crore
+472% YoY from INR5.9 crore; sixth consecutive PAT-positive quarter
+53% YoY; EBITDA INR42.7 crore (+58% YoY), margin ~40%
+41% YoY; EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven prior quarter
Post refinancing; debt cost ~9-9.5% vs 17.5% last year

financial_highlights.value: Commerce INR125 crore; non-commerce INR145 crore

segments.name: Commerce Test Prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR108.6 crore (+53% YoY), EBITDA INR42.7 crore (~40% margin). Offline revenue about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore annualised, offline margin ~35% and online ~45-48%. Managed commerce colleges at about 17 now, to add 15 more this year.

segments.name: Government test prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven last quarter. Target of INR95-100 crore EBITDA over four to five years; Karnataka expansion planned in FY27.

segments.name: Academic / K-12
segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.2 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR9.2 crore (+53% YoY). Manages six schools with over 5,400 students; preschool managed operations to be entered in FY27.

segments.name: SNVA Veranda (associate stake)
segments.commentary: Vocational/higher-ed businesses (Edureka, Six Phrase) were moved into SNVA Veranda; management expects value unlock, with the stake to sit in the non-commerce entity post demerger. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: revenue about INR670 crore (FY26: INR482 crore), EBITDA about INR260 crore (FY26: INR204 crore), PAT about INR144 crore (FY26: INR130 crore).
Commerce FY27: revenue about INR450 crore, EBITDA about INR215 crore, PAT about INR110 crore.
Non-commerce FY27: revenue about INR220 crore, EBITDA INR46 crore, PAT INR34 crore.
Management cited EBITDA margin of about 38.8% for FY27 (per analyst reading of guidance); expects margins to recover in Q2 and Q3 as college and marketing spends mature.

Commerce demerger: NCLT order expected imminently after July 20 hearing (orders reserved); next NCLT hearing 17 August 2026; listing targeted by end-September 2026. Shareholders receive 1 JK Shah Commerce Education share per Veranda share.
Commerce long-term aspiration: revenue above INR1,000 crore by FY30.
capex_capacity: Offline commerce network at over 105 centres; 50 new commerce colleges under management in pipeline; plan to add 15 managed commerce colleges in FY27 (doubling from about 17).
Commerce Virtuals (live and recorded digital format for Class 11-12) recently launched for pan-India reach without physical infrastructure.
Government test prep: Group 1 offline programmes, junior IAS, subscription magazines; expansion into Karnataka in FY27.
Planned offline presence in UP, Bihar, Rajasthan and Gujarat to reduce regional concentration.
Managed schools: six schools, 5,400+ students; preschool managed operations to start in FY27.
demand_pricing: Enrollments +35% YoY vs collections +27%; management attributed gap to subject-wise commerce classes, which raise enrollment counts with lower per-enrollment billing.
Q1 collections INR165 crore vs revenue INR150 crore; about INR15 crore of advances deferred under Ind AS 11 to later quarters.
Managed school revenue jump attributed to ~10% student growth plus start-of-year book and service sales (~20% uplift in Q1).
Guided ARPU increase of 7-8% a year and 10% student growth in FY27 as EBITDA drivers, plus 15 new colleges.
Commerce positioned as number one across CA, CS, CMA, ACCA; management claims undisputed leadership in pedigree, alumni, centres and ranks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable quarterly finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohasin Khan guided INR7.5-8 crore per quarter after refinancing; EBITDA excludes finance cost, so no finance savings sit in the EBITDA bridge.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tax swing to a credit of about INR3 crore from about INR8 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Following an intra-group merger of a subsidiary into the parent, management reversed INR7.35 crore of tax related to earlier years; described as current tax, not a DTA write-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline QoQ and how will FY27 38.8% margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited doubled college expansion spend, pre-demerger advertising for the commerce brand, and initial work on 15 new colleges, all expensed in Q1; expects benefit in next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timing of the NCLT approval and listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders were reserved at the 20 July hearing; affidavit filed on the appointed date query; next hearing 17 August. Management expects order within about a week, then ROC filing in 3-4 days, a record date one week later, and listing before end-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-commerce be valued lower because it carries all the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the commerce entity to command the highest sector multiple as the leader; government test prep should earn a good multiple, K-12 less so. No numbers provided on valuation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offline/online split and margins in commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore (roughly 3:1 offline to online per management); offline margin ~35%, online ~45-48%.

risks_watch: Commerce demerger timing: NCLT order is pending after the 20 July hearing and the next hearing is 17 August; management's chain of ROC filing, record date and listing all hinges on this, with listing guided before end-September 2026.

FY27 margin ramp: Q1 EBITDA margin ~36% (reported), and the analyst-computed ex-other-income margin fell QoQ; guidance implies ~38.8% for FY27, which depends on college expansion spend and marketing costs maturing in Q2-Q3.
Cash conversion: Q1 collections INR165 crore vs revenue INR150 crore, with ~INR15 crore of advances deferred under Ind AS 11; collections grew 27% vs enrollments 35% and revenue 42%.

Tax line normalisation: Q1 tax was a credit of about INR3 crore after a INR7.35 crore reversal tied to an intra-group merger; PAT of INR34 crore is not a clean run-rate, and tax was earlier about INR8 crore a quarter.
Post-demerger valuation: non-commerce entity carries all debt (INR145 crore vs commerce INR125 crore); management expects commerce to get the highest sector multiple, but gave no valuation figures.

Expansion execution: 15 new managed commerce colleges in FY27 (from ~17), Karnataka government test prep launch, preschool managed operations, and UP/Bihar/Rajasthan/Gujarat offline entry; no capex or investment quantum given.
key_quotes: we expect the entire process to be completed by possibly the first half of September 2026, which is next month.
So it will be yet to be listed and traded but you should see the shares credited in the individual Demat accounts.
So the commerce business will be all businesses, except our government test prep, K-12 and the shareholding in SNVA.

So those spends have also been expensed during this quarter. You should see the impact of this -- positive impact of this in the growth that we will have in the commerce business in the subsequent three quarters of this year itself.
543514|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the commerce demerger timeline and the FY27 guidance, repeatedly stating orders are "pretty much" imminent, but evasive on market recognition and valuation, declining to predict how the market will price the listed entities. Management was also defensive when pressed on the QoQ EBITDA margin decline, attributing it to one-off expansion and pre-demerger marketing spend rather than a structural issue.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Guidance implies ~38.8% FY27 EBITDA margin vs ~36% in Q1 (reported), with management expecting college and marketing spends to mature over the next three quarters; Q1 margin was flattered by nothing but was hit by doubled college expansion spend and pre-demerger advertising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plan to add 15 managed commerce colleges in FY27 (doubling from ~17) with 50 in the pipeline, plus Karnataka government test prep and preschool operations; no capex quantum given, so execution rather than capital spend is the driver.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Enrollments up 35% YoY to ~1.03 lakh and guided 10% student growth plus 7-8% ARPU growth in FY27, against FY27 revenue guidance of ~INR670 crore vs INR482 crore in FY26 (~39%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed and no capex quantum discussed; growth is asset-light managed colleges and Commerce Virtuals, so a formal capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR670 crore revenue, INR260 crore EBITDA and INR144 crore PAT without raising it, and Q1 PAT was lifted by a INR7.35 crore one-time tax reversal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA of INR260 crore needs margin ramp to ~38.8% from ~36% in Q1, and Q1 EBITDA growth ex one-time income was ~30% against a 10% reported figure; delay in the margin ramp or demerger slippage would pressure guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Commerce Virtuals (live and recorded digital format for Class 11-12) recently launched, preschool managed operations to start in FY27, and Karnataka government test prep expansion planned in FY27.

rows.label: Commerce demerger and listing by end-September 2026
rows.why: NCLT order expected after 20 July hearing, next hearing 17 Aug 2026; management chain of ROC filing, record date and listing points to listing before end-September, one JK Shah Commerce Education share per Veranda share.

rows.label: Cash conversion catch-up on deferred advances
rows.why: Q1 collections INR165 crore vs revenue INR150 crore, with ~INR15 crore of advances deferred under Ind AS 11 to later quarters, though collections grew 27% vs revenue 42%.

rows.label: Finance cost reset after refinancing
rows.why: Debt cost ~9-9.5% vs 17.5% last year, with finance cost guided at INR7.5-8 crore per quarter on INR270 crore total debt (INR125 crore commerce, INR145 crore non-commerce).

tone.note: Management was confident on the demerger timeline and FY27 guidance, but defensive on the QoQ EBITDA margin decline and evasive on valuation; analysts pushed on margin ramp, tax credit normalisation and the sustainability of PAT.

543517|2026-03.headline: Hariom Pipe FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR1,667 crore and EBITDA 19% to INR209 crore at a 12.56% margin, with FY27 volume guided at 350,000-360,000 tonnes.
543517|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,667 crore (+23% YoY), EBITDA INR209 crore (+19%) and PAT INR76 crore (+23%), with EBITDA margin broadly stable at 12.56%. Q4 revenue was INR507 crore (+27% YoY), Q4 EBITDA INR64 crore (+31%) and Q4 PAT INR30 crore (+75%). FY26 volume growth fell short of the 30% guided last year, as management prioritised margin and cash over volume. Management said a Tamil Nadu (Perundurai) plant closure linked to a pollution board order had not yet hit volumes, citing stock and asset-light supply, and that reopening was expected within days.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to EBITDA / ROCE / ROE (FY26)

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Management stated value-added products were 98% of FY26 revenue (analyst cited about 90% earlier). Galvanised products were described as a meaningful contributor.

segments.name: B2B / OEM channel
segments.commentary: B2B share of sales rose to about 20% in Q4 FY26 from about 15% earlier, per management. Management said the target is to add more OEM and engineering clients.

segments.name: Renewable energy (Hariom Power & Energy, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: 60 MW AC solar project under MSEDCL PPA across 13 locations; 8 locations taken up, about 38 MW under work, and about 10 MW expected to start production next month. Investment to date INR9.56 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guided at about 350,000-360,000 tonnes, roughly 20-25% growth on FY26 (about 288,000 tonnes), subject to market conditions; management said 30% growth is possible on existing capacity but not at the cost of margins.
No firm EBITDA per tonne number for FY27; management said the current level (about INR7,200-7,800 blended) is the minimum to sustain, with no percentage growth target given.
Management called 12.5-12.6% EBITDA margin sustainable.

Solar: 60 MW project to be completed within FY27; project cost about INR241-245 crore, bank term loan about INR195 crore, equity from Hariom Pipes about INR25-30 crore, balance expected from central capital subsidy; FY27 solar revenue to be quantified at Q1 results.
Backward integration rising from about 40% to about 80% depends on an environmental clearance from the Government of India; management said 3-4 months after approval, with no assured timeline.
Q1 FY27 current trading described as good; management declined to give a specific Q1 YoY volume growth number.
capex_capacity: 60 MW AC solar project (subsidiary Hariom Power & Energy) under MSEDCL PPA; 13 locations, 8 taken up, 2 yet to commence, rest targeted in FY27; land of about 123 acres acquired at 8 locations and work started at 6.
Solar tariff about INR3.21 per unit plus central capital subsidy; fixed-tenure revenue.
Tamil Nadu (Perundurai) plant closed on a pollution board order; management said pile was moved, compliances completed, and reopening order awaited within 2-3 working days.
Backward integration at about 40%; expansion to about 80% requires a pending EC order.
Metal Mart Private Limited incorporated for metals trading, still at initial setup; GST registrations in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana in progress.
demand_pricing: Management said the market is competitive and steel prices are volatile; EBITDA per tonne is driven by market demand and supply, not MRP.
Scaffolding demand weak in FY26 because the business is credit-based; management said it is not extending the credit needed to push volume.

Management said dealer losses from the Perundurai closure were nil, with some dealers buying from competitors for a short period; the company supplied commercial products to Kerala from stock and other facilities.
Gas supply disruption: management said there was no impact in Q4, with own suppliers and storage in place.
Analyst's view: EBITDA per tonne can mislead when prices rise; management did not commit to a per-tonne target.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company still stand by 30% FY27 volume growth guidance, and what EBITDA per tonne is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capacity for about 30% growth on about 288,000 tonnes, subject to market conditions and no compromise on margins. Blended EBITDA is about INR7,200 per tonne, and management said it is confident of maintaining that level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tamil Nadu plant open, and what revenue was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant awaits a reopening order within 2-3 working days, and April 2026 turnover matched April 2025 because of stock and asset-light supply. It said no non-compliance was found and that the closure followed election-period actions by the authorities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar capex, debt and revenue roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Total project cost is about INR241 crore with INR195 crore bank debt and an equity component of INR25-30 crore; INR9.56 crore is invested so far. Management said the remainder is backed by central capital subsidy and that solar revenue will be quantified at Q1 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per tonne or margin be the better guidance metric?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins of about 12.5-12.6% are sustainable and it focuses on profitability rather than volume. It said the EBITDA per tonne figure is not price-dependent in a fixed way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B share and the FY27 product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B was about 20% of sales in Q4, up from 15%. Management said the mix is coils across MS and GI, the focus is B2B plus dealers, and dealer addition is continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Metal Mart subsidiary have a start date?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supplier tie-ups are done and GST registrations are pending in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, with operations to start once registrations are received.

risks_watch: Tamil Nadu plant reopening timing and any Q1 volume impact; the stated April turnover parity relies on stock and third-party supply.
Volume delivery against the 350,000-360,000 tonne guide, given FY26 undershot the earlier 30% growth guide and scaffolding demand is weak.
Steel price volatility and input cost swings (gas, power, logistics) that management said can affect EBITDA per tonne.
Solar project execution: remaining 2 locations to start, FY27 completion, subsidy realisation and ~INR160 crore net debt rising in FY27 with depreciation and interest impact.
EC clearance for backward integration (40% to 80%), with no assured timing.
Management commentary on the Tamil Nadu closure cause was not fully clear and drew follow-up questions.

key_quotes: Our area is not the volume, our area is always the profitability.
We will continue to focus on profitable growth rather than only volume-led growth.
EBITDA margins are sustainable, basically, whatever is being shown in the numbers are there.

rows.why: Guide of 350,000-360,000 t is about 20-25% growth on about 288,000 t, but FY26 undershot the earlier 30% guide, scaffolding demand is weak with credit tightly held, and the Tamil Nadu plant closure is unresolved.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Backward integration expansion from 40% to 80% is pending an EC order (3-4 months after approval, no assured timeline) and no new pipe capacity was announced, so a new capex announcement depends on that clearance.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to reaffirm the 30% growth guide, gave no firm per-tonne target, and avoided Q1 volume numbers, so no upward revision signalled despite Q4 PAT +75%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tamil Nadu (Perundurai) plant closed pending a reopening order within 2-3 working days, April turnover only matched April 2025 via stock, and steel price volatility can move EBITDA per tonne (blended about INR7,200).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch discussed; Metal Mart trading subsidiary is still at setup with GST registrations pending, and the mix remains MS and GI coils.

rows.why: Perundurai reopening order awaited within 2-3 working days and April turnover matched April 2025 only via stock; EC order for 40% to 80% backward integration is pending with 3-4 months lag after approval and no assured timeline.

rows.label: B2B/OEM share gain
rows.why: B2B share rose to about 20% of Q4 FY26 sales from about 15% earlier, and management said the target is to add more OEM and engineering clients with dealer addition continuing.

rows.label: Solar debt rise and net debt
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA at 1.65x with about INR160 crore net debt rising in FY27 as the INR195 crore bank loan funds the solar project, adding depreciation and interest costs.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins (12.5-12.6% sustainable), cash conversion (92%) and B2B growth, but evasive on the 30% volume guide, Q1 volume numbers and the Tamil Nadu closure cause; analysts pressed on volume and the closure.

543517|2026-09.headline: Hariom Pipe Q2 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR 554 crore and PAT to INR 29 crore, with EBITDA per tonne at INR 8,140.
543517|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 65% YoY to INR 554 crore, EBITDA rose 58% to INR 68 crore and PAT rose to INR 29 crore from INR 10 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.21%. Management attributed the recovery to the Perundurai unit restarting on July 13 after a roughly 110-day closure in Q1. H1 revenue was INR 983 crore (up 23%), EBITDA INR 118 crore (up 17%) and PAT INR 46 crore (up 35%). Management guided to 10-15% growth for H2 FY27 and FY28 and a 25% volume growth base case, while the solar portfolio and Andhra Pradesh steel MOU remain early-stage.

segments.name: Steel (standalone) volumes
segments.commentary: Q2 sales volume was 83,117 tonnes, up 32% QoQ; H1 volume was about 1.46 lakh tonnes, up 6% YoY. Q2 split: integrated steel plant ~29,000 t, Mahbubnagar galvanised ~29,600 t, Perundurai ~23,400-24,000 t, Anantapur sponge iron ~1,000 t.

segments.name: Hariom Power and Energy (solar)
segments.commentary: 15 MWac is operational across three locations after 5 MWac in July and two 5 MWac projects in October (the latter after the half-year end). Portfolio is 60 MW across 13 locations in Maharashtra; target is 52 MW across 11 locations by January 2027.

segments.name: Metal Mart (trading subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Completed documentation and obtained GST registration in H1; fuller operations are planned for the current quarter. No revenue contribution was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27: minimum 10-15% growth from current run-rate, per Managing Director.
FY28: management expects 10-15% growth again, with acquisitions and brownfield expansion under evaluation; projections may rise from the next or the quarter after.
Volume growth: management's stated target is not less than 25% a year (earlier 30%); 25% was described as the base case for FY28, with acquisitions as upside.
EBITDA margin: management said it is consistently above 12%; if the proposed HR coil/integrated capacity is built, EBITDA could rise to 13-15%.
Long-term vision: INR 10,000 crore top line within 5-6 years, per the MD.

Solar: 52 MW across 11 locations targeted by January 2027. Management expects roughly INR 28-30 crore revenue and INR 3-4 crore net surplus after debt, depreciation and interest once 52 MW is operational, over 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Total steel capacity is 5,21,000 tonnes of finished goods. Breakdown: Perundurai 1,80,000 t; Mahbubnagar galvanised 1,20,000 t; the remaining ~2,21,000 t is integrated steel plant output.

Maharashtra capex announced for a large steel expansion; the MOU is about 1.5 years old and still facing issues. Management expects execution over 3-4 years and plans an HR coil unit with backward integration, but gave no timeline or quantum.
Andhra Pradesh integrated steel plant MOU is non-binding, subject to due diligence, approvals and land allocation. It would be built within existing land at the current facility.
Perundurai: 4 MW DC of solar power under an MOU, which management said will lower power costs. Operations resumed July 13, 2026 after the Q1 closure.
Solar: 52 MW out of 60 MW awarded is targeted. Two sites face land scarcity and the alternative substation request is pending; if not granted, the build is capped at 52 MW.
demand_pricing: Management said about 20% of Q2 volume (~83,000 t) came from OEM customers. Focus is on OEM and value-added products, which carry better margins than standard galvanised or cold-rolled pipe.
Management said a single customer is no more than 5-6% of revenue, and about 80% of sales go through dealers with the balance direct B2B. The company has more than 800 SKUs.
Q2 EBITDA per tonne rise was attributed to lower fixed cost at Perundurai after full operation, higher integrated-steel margins, better market absorption and power and opex efficiency.
Power consumption per tonne fell to about 98 units in Q2 from about 135 units in Q1, per management.

Power and fuel expense rose to about INR 25 crore in Q2 from about INR 18 crore in Q1. Management cited restart costs, higher Mahbubnagar galvanised utilisation, and higher tariffs and additional charges. Electricity is the major component of power cost.
Management said peak revenue at the 5.21 lakh t capacity could be about INR 2,500-2,800 crore at present steel prices, depending on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: What are H2 FY27 and FY28 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: MD guided minimum 10-15% growth for H2 FY27 and 10-15% again for FY28. The CFO declined to give a specific number at first, and management said EBITDA per tonne and margins should hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth target and is 25% a base case?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the target is at least 25% volume growth (earlier 30%). Management said 25% is the base case for FY28, with acquisitions as upside.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned steel capex be funded and what margin impact is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Maharashtra project will take 3-4 years, with an HR coil unit planned for backward integration. EBITDA margin could rise from 12% to 13-15% if it is built. No funding plan was specified.

qa_highlights.question: Is GP pipe and coil dependence a concentration risk and what is the water-security position?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said GP segment growth reflects new customers and geographies. The company is not affected by the Hyderabad water situation.

qa_highlights.question: Solar subsidiary revenue and surplus from the 60 MW portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said 52 MW would generate about INR 28-30 crore of top line and INR 3-4 crore net surplus over 4-5 years after debt, depreciation and interest. Power from Maharashtra plants goes to MSEDCL under PM-KUSUM and cannot be used for manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the power cost increase and what is the Tamil Nadu power arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher production, Perundurai running on units rather than minimum demand charges, and extra tariff charges. A 25-year PPA-style MOU with a solar company supplies about 4 MW DC for Perundurai. Electricity is the main power cost component.

qa_highlights.question: What is the vision and expansion strategy beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD set a goal of INR 10,000 crore top line in 5-6 years and said acquisitions, franchising models and brownfield expansion are under evaluation. Management said there are no finalised deals, and the Andhra Pradesh MOU is non-binding.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the Maharashtra steel expansion and the Andhra Pradesh MOU, which is non-binding and subject to approvals and land allocation.
Solar: two sites are short of land and the substation approval is pending, which may cap capacity at 52 MW out of 60 MW awarded.
Power cost pressure: power and fuel costs rose to about INR 25 crore in Q2 from INR 18 crore in Q1, and management attributed this partly to tariff additions.
Concentration: GP pipes and coils dependence is rising, per an analyst. Single-customer exposure is capped at 5-6%.
Working capital and inventory rise from holding more than 800 SKUs, with 8-9 SKUs per dealer lot.
Tamil Nadu pollution-control issue: management said operations are normal, but no detail on cost or permit timing was provided.
Promoter warrant issue at INR 333 per warrant, with 25% margin money received. Management said the funds are for expansion and capital needs.
Management did not quantify the H2 volume target, the FY28 volume target or the HR coil capex amount, and gave no funding plan for the expansion.
543517|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the Q2 recovery and near-term growth, but noticeably vague on specific numbers. Management repeatedly declined to quantify FY28, capex, the funding plan and the Andhra Pradesh project, and cited factors "not in our hands". Tone was defensive on the solar investment and the Tamil Nadu shutdown.

For this second half, we can expect minimum 10% to 15% from here.
It is clearly in the stock exchange information also. We have clearly mentioned that it is a non -binding.
So, whatever we are talking about 25 %, 30% of growth will be consistent as we've seen, depending on multiple parameters which are not in our hands which we are working on.

543523|2026-03.headline: Campus Activewear Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, EBITDA margin 19.2%, FY26 PAT margin 8.4%.
543523|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, led by online (around 19%) and distribution (around 5.5%). EBITDA was INR 88.5 crore at a 19.2% margin (up 50 bps) and PAT was INR 44.1 crore at a 9.6% margin (up 100 bps). For FY26, revenue grew 11.4% to INR 1,774 crore, EBITDA margin rose 145 bps to 17.5%, and PAT margin rose 80 bps to 8.4%. Management said the mid-year raw material and minimum wage inflation was passed on via MRP hikes taken in early April, and that demand held up in April.

segments.name: Online (marketplace)
segments.commentary: Online grew about 19% in Q4 and 9.8% in FY26; management said all online business is pure marketplace except Flipkart, with Amazon, Snapdeal and brand.com growing faster. Online salience rose in Q4, though GT charges dilute gross margin and billing changed from 16 June to net of freight (INR 82 billed against INR 100 earlier).

segments.name: Distribution (general trade and franchise)
segments.commentary: Distribution grew about 5.5% in Q4 and 10.5% in FY26. Management said the annual distribution meet produced strong four-month forward orders, with AOP alignments with partners closed at over 100% of the target till September.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Sneaker portfolio grew about 100% YoY in FY26 and more than 50% in quarterly terms; the Paonta Sahib and Pant Nagar units are producing about 2 lakh pairs per month, targeted to double by end FY27. Management did not disclose sneaker revenue or volume share.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated its EBITDA margin aspiration band of 17% to 19% for FY27 but gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
Management said pricing taken in early April covers the inflation impact and that raw material prices have peaked and are starting to ease; no further price hikes expected.
Plan to open 60 to 80 new EBO stores in FY27 (about 40% COCO and 60% FOFO), after closing 9 to 10 and opening 13 to 14 stores in FY26; store count stood at about 300.
Marketing budget for FY27 set to be aggressive, focused on brand building rather than performance marketing.

Capex in FY27 expected to return to normal maintenance, mold, EBO and IT levels; Pant Nagar expansion including assembly lines is planned over the next three years, after first optimising the upper facility.
Full BIS compliance expected by 31 July 2026, with very little BIS stock remaining.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share of shoes priced below INR 1,000 rise versus Q4 FY25, and is the pricing MRP or realised price?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the figures are realised ASP; the shift reflects MRP corrections after GST on footwear was revised from 12% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What size of price hike was taken and will it suffice against inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO declined to give the percentage, said hikes were taken proportionately across the range and are enough to cover raw material and minimum wage inflation; peak RM seen, prices to ease in about a quarter, with no price reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses (ex-ad spend) rise only about 5% despite online growth of 19%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited dynamic online commission negotiations and event-based waivers, plus flat store count meaning no new EBO costs; other costs grew in the 5-6% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lease cash outflow rise sharply, nearly 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Pant Nagar land is a 71-year state government lease treated as lease liability payment; normalised FY26 rent excluding INR 65.4 crore is the base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise 5-6 days in FY26 and where will they go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FG inventory was at a very minimal level last year and was rebuilt to the right level by March 2026, which will be maintained going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for sneaker growth, and what is the path to 2 lakh pairs a month?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said capacity is not a constraint now; Pant Nagar can reach 6 lakh pairs per month after two phases and HRD2 can reach 2 lakh (already running), targeting 8-9 lakh pairs per month in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins reach the 17-19% band or slip to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; CEO said the company will endeavour to stay within the 17-19% range guided earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBO expansion plan and capex for stores and facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said 60-70 or about 80 new stores are planned after closing 9-10 and opening 13-14 in FY26; CFO said FY27 capex reverts to normal maintenance, mould, EBO and IT levels, with Pant Nagar expansion over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What were the distribution meet outcomes and demand trend?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said order bookings were strong on a four-month forward basis, numbers not shared; COO said AOP alignments with distributors were closed at over 100% till September.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the low Q4 ASP growth of 1.5% when D2C/online realisations should be higher?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to online billing change from 16 June (INR 82 billed against INR 100) with freight of INR 18 billed directly by portals, which is not in last year's Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the BIS compliance position?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the company is hardly left with any non-BIS stock and expects full compliance by 31 July 2026; the reported BIS rethink is only chatter with no official communication.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company gaining share in competitive affordable athleisure, and what are its moats?
qa_highlights.answer: COO cited an integrated supply chain, strongest distribution network, R&D, 20-year brand loyalty; CEO estimated replicating the supply chain would need about INR 2,000 crore.

543523|2026-06.headline: Campus Activewear Q1 FY27: revenue up 12.2%, volume up 11.7%, EBITDA margin 15.9%, PAT up 17.7%, with ASP drag from temporary accounting and mix effects.
543523|2026-06.overview: Campus reported 12.2% revenue growth, 11.7% volume growth, 15.9% EBITDA margin and 17.7% PAT growth in Q1 FY27. Reported ASP growth was held back by a Walmart (Flipkart/Myntra) GT-charge netting change (about 2.5%) and a school-shoe mix shift (about 2%), both described as Q1-only effects. An 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 gave underlying core-category ASP growth of about 5%. Management guided to mid-double-digit FY27 growth, split between ASP and volume, and reiterated a 17-19% EBITDA margin aspiration. Record Q1 production and record distributor orders were highlighted ahead of the festive season.

financial_highlights.change: Management says about 4.5-5% was temporary (GT netting ~2%, franchise SOR transition ~2.5%); normalised growth about 4%-plus ex these factors per management's framing
Analyst-cited figure; management did not dispute it

financial_highlights.metric: ASP impact from Walmart GT netting
Underlying ASP increase, core Stuck-On category
Additional depreciation from Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants
Minimum wage cost in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: about Rs. 5 crore for the quarter

financial_highlights.change: About 10% annualisation and increments, about 5% new hiring

segments.name: Stuck-On (core)
segments.commentary: Underlying ASP up about 5% after ~8% MRP increase; school shoes moved from DIP into Stuck-On, which management says has higher ASP and margin than DIP.

segments.name: School shoes
segments.commentary: Revenue up nearly 50% YoY; about 40% of Q1 volume growth came from this category, expected to normalise from Q2.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Q1 contributed about 12-13% of volume; management targets about 30% growth for the category in FY27, down from near-100% historically.

segments.name: Open footwear (sandals/slippers)
segments.commentary: Slower growth, about 4-5% below rest of category, attributed to CNG/LPG supply constraints affecting hot-and-cold machines during the war-related period.

segments.name: Franchise (FOFO/SOR)
segments.commentary: Management cited about 25% de-growth in franchise revenue in Q1 from the outright-to-SOR model transition across 158 stores (about 2.5% revenue impact); 18 EBOs opened in Q1, the highest in 6-8 quarters.

segments.name: Marketplace and brand.com
segments.commentary: Marketplace operations up mid-double digits; brand.com up over 100% YoY; company-owned stores SSG about 20%.

segments.name: General trade Gujarat
segments.commentary: GT grew at least 20-25% faster than rest of country over the period; Maharashtra now second-largest GT state after UP.

segments.name: Elan by Campus
segments.commentary: Neo-casual launch about 60 days old, priced Rs. 1,899-2,599, selling in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com; next set planned for festive season.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: mid-double-digit overall revenue growth, split between ASP and volume; management said volume is expected to be high single digit and ASP growth of at least 6-7% from Q2 onwards.
Management is '100% confident' of delivering the 17-19% EBITDA margin band for FY27.
Store additions target: about 90-100 stores by end FY27 (guidance range 80-120).
Employee cost as % of sales expected to be proportionate to FY26; no further incremental wage cost expected beyond what is already baked in.
Festive timing: Diwali in November 2026; BBD shifts to October from September, so some marketplace revenue may move from Q2 to Q3.
Management does not plan further MRP increases; expects raw material cost relief to flow into P&L as volatility subsides.
capex_capacity: Record Q1 production, with July 2026 the highest-ever production month, to build festive inventory.
Installed annual capacity cited at about 31 million pairs, down from 36 million two years ago, due to shutdown of about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity.
New manufacturing facilities at Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar commissioned and ramping up; sneakers production also from Haridwar and Pantnagar.
Franchise EBO ROI cited at 18-30% depending on store economics; franchisees pay deposit on inventory, company controls inventory, discounting and replenishment.
Franchise master partners to rise from about 8-9 to about 16; about 8 new partners added this year.
demand_pricing: 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 across key categories; management says volumes grew despite it and resistance has been limited. No further hikes planned.
Management said some demand tapering was seen in the last quarter, citing geopolitical factors and floods in Maharashtra and Gujarat, but its demand reading remains positive.
Record orders at the distributor meet held in May 2026, giving visibility on festive demand.
Management sees some constraints at smaller organised and unorganised competitors due to working-capital stress, though impact on festive supply is unclear.

Price-point mix: management said Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core shoe segment; analyst pointed to about 7% two-year CAGR decline in sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue, which management attributed to the 8% price hike shifting products above Rs. 1,500 and reporting changes.

qa_highlights.question: Vidisha Seth (Ambit): Is the 8% MRP hike, above industry levels, risking volume or share given elasticity in economy key products, and will there be another hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8% is a fair hike, accepted with limited resistance, and volumes grew despite it; RM inflation has been fully absorbed and no further MRP hikes will be taken. Raw-material relief is expected to flow back into P&L as markets stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash (Motilal Oswal): Why did sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue decline about 7% on a two-year CAGR basis, and is the company exiting price points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not exiting price points and Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core; the decline reflects products moving above Rs. 1,500 after the 8% hike, a change in reporting, and faster closed-shoe growth versus open footwear. Gaps at economy price points are being filled over the next couple of months before the season.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash: Why did installed capacity fall from 36 million to 31 million pairs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity were shut as uneconomic; school shoes were moved from DIP into Stuck-On, which has higher ASP and margin. Stuck-On capacity is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta (Kotak): How much did school shoes contribute to volume growth, and is the margin 17-19% band still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: School shoes contributed about 40% of Q1 volume growth and will normalise from Q2. Management targets FY27 mid-double-digit growth split between ASP (at least 6-7% from Q2) and volume, and said it is 100% confident of the 17-19% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta: What drove the faster growth in other expenses excluding A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gupta said about Rs. 5 crore was minimum-wage cost, about Rs. 2.5 crore was advertising and marketing (distributor meet and logo launch), and about Rs. 2.5 crore was depreciation/indirect cost from the new Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (Emkay): Why is EBITDA growth 11% when revenue growth is about 15-16% ex-accounting changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Walmart GT netting is an accounting change with no absolute EBITDA impact. Employee cost rose about 15% (10% annualisation and increments, 5% new hiring) plus higher SG&A, which drove the gap. FY27 employee cost as % of sales is expected to be in line with FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Shraddha Kapadia (SMFS): Can volume growth stay double-digit for FY27, and what is the Elan by Campus traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not promise double-digit volume but said volume will be high single digit, with ASP and volume together delivering mid-double-digit revenue growth. Elan, about 60 days old at Rs. 1,899-2,599, sells in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com, with a second set planned for festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Prerna Jhunjhunwala (Elara): What is the store opening plan, and how do franchise economics work under the SOR model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 90-100 openings in FY27 (range 80-120), with master franchise partners rising from about 8-9 to about 16. Under SOR, the company controls inventory and discounting, franchisees pay an inventory deposit and bear rent, and EBO ROI is about 18-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Ajay Nandavar (individual investor): Why is open footwear growing slower, and how does Gujarat franchise growth coexist with trade growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandals use hot-and-cold machines dependent on CNG/LPG, which were constrained during the war period, so growth is about 4-5% below the rest of the category. Management said franchise stores have not cannibalised GT, which grew at least 20-25% faster than the rest of the country in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (follow-up): Is the 8% hike in line with industry, and what signs show consumer acceptance and lower competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers took similar or slightly lower hikes; the May distributor meet recorded record orders after the hike. Management cited marketplace growth in the mid-double digits, company-owned store SSG of about 20% and brand.com growth above 100%, and said some smaller and unorganised players faced production constraints due to working-capital stress.

risks_watch: Sustainability of ASP recovery to 6-7% from Q2: the 2.5% Walmart GT netting and 2% school-shoe mix effects must reverse as stated, and the 8% hike must hold without volume loss.
Volume normalisation after school shoes (about 40% of Q1 volume growth) taper, against a high-single-digit FY27 volume target.
EBITDA growth (11%) lagging revenue growth; the 17-19% margin band depends on employee cost (about 15% growth) and SG&A staying in line with FY26 and on raw-material relief.
Demand tapering noted in the last quarter (geopolitics, Maharashtra and Gujarat floods); record festive inventory built in Q1 and July raises inventory-risk exposure if festive demand disappoints.
Franchise transition: about 25% franchise de-growth in Q1 across 158 stores; the SOR model's accounting and store-opening pace (90-100 target) need to be tracked.
Sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue two-year CAGR decline of about 7%; management says economy price-point gaps will be filled before the season.
Elan by Campus and sneaker growth (about 30% target) are early-stage; the Diwali and Big Billion Day shift (October) may move some marketplace revenue from Q2 to Q3.
key_quotes: So, we are, yes, we will be close to double-digit. We cannot promise a double-digit volume growth, but it will be high single digits for sure, right?
Absolutely, Umang. Yes, we are 100% confident of delivering that. There is no reason not to deliver the margin.
RM inflation has been fully absorbed.
So, it is just a recalibration of the DIP.

543523|2026-09.headline: Campus Activewear Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.9% YoY to Rs 452 crore on 10.2% volume growth, while EBITDA margin fell to 13.5%; FY27 17% EBITDA margin guided.

EBITDA rose 12.5% to Rs 62 crore but margin slipped about 50 bps to 13.5%, with gross margin at 51.4% versus 53.9% a year earlier due to material inflation. PAT grew 21.3% to Rs 24 crore (5.3% margin). Management expects a sharp H2 margin recovery and reiterated a full-year FY27 EBITDA margin of 17% and mid-teens revenue growth.

Occupancy was 45.3% group-wide in Q4, with mature hospitals at about 52%.

543526|2026-03.headline: LIC FY26 net VNB rose 41.63% to ₹14,179 crore, with VNB margin up 360 bps to 21.2% on non-par mix and economic assumptions.
543526|2026-03.overview: LIC reported record FY26 PAT of ₹57,419 crore (up 19.25% YoY) and net VNB of ₹14,179 crore (up 41.63%), with margin at 21.2% versus 17.6%. Non-par share of individual APE rose to 35.11% from 27.69% a year earlier, and the solvency ratio improved to 2.35 from 2.11. Embedded value grew only 1.58% to ₹7,89,185 crore because of ₹1.00 lakh crore-plus of equity and debt MTM declines in the year. Management flagged upcoming risk-based capital (RBC) rules as the reason it is cautious on dividend payout, even after raising the final dividend to ₹20 per share pre-bonus.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual APE ₹43,335 crore; non-par APE rose 43.78% to ₹15,214 crore, 35.11% of individual APE. Individual market share fell to 36.6% from 37.46%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group premium ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%); group APE ₹23,626 crore. Group market share 70.11% vs 71.19%. Group contributed about 19% of VNB per the Appointed Actuary's breakdown.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Share of individual NBP 7.51% vs 5.59%. Policy count fell sharply, which management attributed to a microfinance corporate agency issue.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Agency sourced 91.75% of new business premium and 98.42% of policies. Individual agents fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851.

guidance_outlook: No formal numeric guidance. Management expects VNB margin to keep improving, driven by higher ticket size and better persistency, but said further expansion will be gradual and slower from here.
Management said it is not looking for major changes in the business mix from here and aims to consolidate, with VNB growth coming from either margin or volume.
Management said maturity outgo will stay high through January 2027 from 25-year-old Jeevan Shree-type assured-benefit policies.
Dividend payout policy will be finalised only after RBC outcomes are clear; management expects the increased payout to be sustained.
April 2026 sales were described as good, ahead of the prior year, across participating and non-participating products.
risks_watch: RBC framework timing and calibration, which is likely to be equity-sensitive and could constrain capital and payout.
Equity and debt MTM volatility: ₹53,698 crore equity and ₹46,853 crore debt fall in FY26 hit EV growth (only +1.58%).

Margin sustainability: the GST charge, RFR tailwind and mix benefit may not recur, and management said margin could be challenged in the next three years.
Agent count down to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851, and bancassurance policy count down about 36%.
Upcoming Ind AS/IFRS transition and its effect on VIF-to-CSM translation, which is still being worked on.
Heavy maturity outgo through January 2027 from high sum assured legacy policies.

qa_highlights.question: Which products drove the non-par individual savings growth in Q4, and how much of that momentum continues into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Uthup Joseph said savings bucket grew about 48.40%, led by Jeevan Utsav on ticket size; Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium. No FY27 momentum figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin bridge from 17.6% to 21.2%, and what were the operating assumption and EV walk items?
qa_highlights.answer: A.K. Srivastava: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes including GST -2.8%. EV walk: unwind ₹74,748 crore, operating assumption changes -₹1,663 crore, operating experience variance +₹92,639 crore, equity MTM -₹53,698 crore, debt MTM -₹46,853 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the operating variance positive for several years, and what is the persistency variance breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency variance +₹3,509 crore, largely from participating and group business; par 13th-month persistency improved (+₹2,463 crore). Group persistency assumption was strengthened. Expense variance positive net of GST; mortality roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the solvency-driven dividend payout cautious even with solvency at 2.35, and how should the payout ratio be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Pant said the company wants clarity on RBC because equity exposure is high, and it does not want to create expectations it cannot sustain; growth also consumes capital. Doraiswamy said the payout will depend on regulation, with the increased payout (₹20 per share pre-bonus) expected to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par IRRs or offering rates be revised in FY27, and why did bancassurance policy count fall about 36%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said IRRs depend on investment opportunities, competition and margin balance; hedging for long-duration non-par is limited. Hemant Buch attributed the bancassurance policy decline to one microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move to bigger tickets; Q4 sales count rose about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the next year and the building blocks for expansion from here?

capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussion on the call; the call covered insurance sales, margins, capital and dividend.
Capital position: solvency ratio 2.35 at 31 March 2026 vs 2.11 a year earlier; management said it wants to build reserves ahead of risk-based capital (RBC) and that growth will also consume capital.

demand_pricing: Market share by first-year premium 56.6% in FY26 vs 57.05% in FY25; individual market share 36.6% (vs 37.46%); group 70.11% (vs 71.19%).

Non-par individual APE ₹15,214 crore (+43.78%), 35.11% of individual APE vs 27.69%. Jeevan Utsav was the main contributor to savings growth (management cited ~48.40% savings bucket growth); Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium.

VNB margin bridge 17.6% to 21.2%: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes (expense and persistency realignment plus GST) -2.8%. Individual par ~42% of APE contributes ~28% of VNB; individual non-par ~22.7% of APE contributes ~53% of VNB; remainder group (~19%).

Operating experience variance of ₹92,639 crore; persistency variance +₹3,509 crore (group line strengthened, par 13th-month persistency improved, +₹2,463 crore); mortality roughly flat; expense variance positive, net of GST.

Economic variance: equity MTM fall ₹53,698 crore and debt MTM fall ₹46,853 crore. Bond-amortisation accounting change impact of about ₹11,000 crore gross, of which ~₹9,000 crore sits in participating business (no direct PAT impact per management).

Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Policy count via bancassurance fell about 36%; management attributed this to a microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move away from login-based low-ticket sales; Q4 policy count reportedly up ~10%.

Agency: individual agents 14,57,045 vs 14,86,851 (down ~30,000); agency sourced 98.42% of policies and 91.75% of new business premium. Management said recruitment, training and younger-age agent focus will follow.

April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of FY26 pace across participating and non-participating products; management said it is too early to judge the effect of recent market volatility on ULIP and guaranteed demand.
Pricing: management said non-par IRRs depend on investment opportunities and competition and are balanced against margins; long-duration hedges are limited. Expense ratio 11.91% (-51 bps).

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussed; solvency rose to 2.35 from 2.11 and management is building reserves ahead of RBC, so capital is being retained rather than deployed into new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.why: Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP rose 45.19% to ₹5,076 crore, with alternate channels up 109.36%, though bancassurance policy count fell about 36% and Q4 policy count was up about 10%.

543526|2026-06.headline: LIC Q1 FY27 net VNB margin rose 750 bps YoY to 22.9% and VNB grew 61.32% to ₹3,136 crore; profit after tax up 22.81% to ₹13,492 crore.

543527|2026-03.headline: Prudent Q4 FY26: record ₹4,300 crore quarterly equity net sales offset MTM hit; AUM rebounded to ₹1.33 trillion by 5 May 2026.

543528|2026-06.headline: Venus Pipes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR320.5 crore and EBITDA hit a record INR51.5 crore, with margin flat at 16.1%.

543529|2026-03.headline: Delhivery FY26 revenue reached ~10,486 crore with 7.3% service EBITDA and first full-year FCF positive at ~89 crore, a year ahead of plan.

FY26 was the first year of the Ecom Express integration, with over a billion express packages and about 2 million MT of PTL freight. Supply chain services (SCS) reached breakeven on adjusted EBITDA after a service EBITDA turnaround to 10.9%. Management said the company turned FCF positive, one year ahead of plan, despite integration costs; cash stood above 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Express
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~1,832 crore, up 46% YoY, with volumes of 306 million (up ~72-73% YoY, sequentially up on Q3). FY26 revenue ~6,685 crore and about a billion parcels; service EBITDA at upper end of 16-18% normative range.

segments.name: Part Truck Load (PTL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~622 crore and 549 thousand MT, both up ~20% YoY. FY26 about 2 million MT and ~2,254 crore revenue; management cited gross margin rising from 14% to 28% over roughly 2.5-3 years.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ~729 crore with service EBITDA of 10.9% (~79 crore), up ~4x; segment at breakeven on adjusted EBITDA. Two mandates signed and activated in Q4.

segments.name: Delhivery Direct (intracity and intercity)
segments.commentary: Intracity on-demand service live in six cities; FY26 investment about 76 crore, with FY27 investment guided at 130-160 crore toward a 200+ crore external GMV run-rate.

guidance_outlook: Long-term transport ROIC target of 25%+, with adjusted EBITDA rising from ~6.3% toward at least 10%, and PTL service EBITDA moving toward ~18% and corporate overheads falling to ~7% of revenue.
Capital intensity (capex plus working-capital items) of ~21.5% of revenue could fall by 2-3 percentage points.
Capex to reach the 4% of revenue target from 4.7%; AGV and automation spend not expected to materially change capex guidance.
Net working capital at 11 days seen as sustainable; further reduction possible via faster billing and prepaid mix, though with limits.
FY27 new-business investment of 130-160 crore guided in the shareholder letter.
Management expects e-commerce industry to grow 15-20% in the medium term.
Management said the company does not plan a broad price increase now, though diesel pass-through clauses apply to PTL and some customers.
capex_capacity: Capex fell to 4.7% of revenue (from 7.8% in FY23); management reiterated a 4% target and said it is moving slightly ahead of plan.
Fleet metric: the 20,000 daily average fleet figure covers only contracted monthly vehicles; the decline reflects a shift to per-kilo variable fleet, while tractor-trailer count rose QoQ.
AGV pilots in Mumbai (Bombay) to be expanded to other mega gateways within FY27.
Delhivery Labs launched about a year ago; AI and automation deployed in claims, documentation and customer communication.
Company is the first in India to get a road train, after a 46-foot tractor trailer launch.
demand_pricing: Management said market structure is more settled after the Ecom Express deal, with less short-term price gouging than in the two years before FY26.
Share of 1P (first-party) logistics declined over the last year, per a listed marketplace; management expects a gradual shift towards 3P.
Long-tail D2C/SME share described as stable to slightly up YoY; heavy shipping share described as dominant.
Single largest customer was ~16% of revenue last year; management said it is well below its informal 35% concern threshold.

Diesel price hikes of about Rs 3/litre at pumps: prices indexed for PTL; express pass-through is via DPH clauses assessed customer by customer. Rs 1-2 price increases seen in some air-network pockets via surcharges.
Management dismissed Amazon's reopening of its 3PL offering as an old product with limited strategic value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising fuel prices on consumption and costs, and has Delhivery raised prices?
qa_highlights.answer: PTL prices are diesel-indexed; express uses DPH clauses. Pump prices rose about Rs 3, and no broad price hike is planned. Q4 margins rose over Q3 despite fuel, and a volatile environment is seen as favourable to the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Is Amazon's 3PL push a competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an old product in a new wrapper; first-party orders get priority at last mile and first-party logistics costs more than 3PL when fully loaded.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers included faster and more accurate billing, client selection (declining some RFQs), and more-than-monthly billing for preferential pricing. NWC was 11 days versus 38 three years ago; management called it sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will SCS pipeline remain margin accretive, and how much of new initiatives' investment is opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Each SCS project must clear an internal hurdle rate and the pipeline is in focus sectors. Short-term start-up costs can weigh on P&L. Management did not give a split of the 130-160 crore FY27 spend between opex and capex in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex intensity rise with express growth, and will the industry overbuild?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex intensity is expected to stay around the 4% target; growth is mainly PTL and heavy, and management does not expect irrational pricing like three or four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Delhivery Direct opportunity and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Intracity service live in six cities; FY26 spend ~76 crore; FY27 guided at 130-160 crore toward 200+ crore external GMV run-rate. Management described the TAM as very large without quantifying it.

543529|2026-09.headline: Delhivery Q2 FY27 revenue crossed Rs 3,066 Cr (+20% YoY) with adjusted PAT of Rs 41 Cr; management says volume guidance of 20-30% is tracking toward the lower end.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at Rs 123 Cr (4% of revenue) and PAT at Rs 41 Cr, with cash of Rs 4,676 Cr on the balance sheet. Management said October volumes were strong and that the company is not revising its 20-30% volume growth estimate, which it now sees at the lower end of the range. Newer businesses (Local LCV rental, Direct consumer, International, Saver) were reported ahead of prior expectations, while Express margin is guided to be roughly flat with FY26 and the management said that a 17% full-year margin looks achievable.

rows.why: H1 sales volume fell about 10% to 2 MMT on a 10-15% monsoon hit, and management expects to recoup part of the shortfall in Rabi with Q3 a favourable DAP window, but gave no volume number and Q4 mix awaits the NBS revision.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR 4,000-4,700 crore is already planned through 2029 and the second 1 MMT phase is awaiting clearance, so a formal new announcement is conditional on environmental approval and is not a fresh trigger.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management repeatedly refused forward guidance on volume and debt and the Rabi NBS and sulphur notifications are still pending, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Subsidy receivable of INR 6,700 crore, debt above last year's INR 6,900 crore level, a INR 60 crore inventory write-down and high DAP/NPK trade stock (DAP +20%, NPK +29%) all carry downside if NBS is delayed or rates fall.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch was discussed; the focus is on DAP/NPK/TSP mix and de-emphasising SSP.

rows.label: Debt reduction after subsidy collections
rows.why: Subsidy receivable of INR 6,700 crore includes INR 1,200 crore received in October and management expects a substantial debt reduction by end-December, with gross debt guided near but slightly above last year's INR 6,900 crore.

rows.label: Inventory write-down reversal on NBS notification
rows.why: About INR 60 crore write-down under cost-or-NRV because NBS and sulphur notifications are pending, with reversal expected once announced, likely in H2.

rows.label: Rabi NBS revision and price correction
rows.why: Management said it expects a Rabi NBS revision and will correct farmer prices if raw material costs permit; sulphur prices already fell more than $200/t, though the NBS is not yet declared.

tone.note: Management was confident on market share, Rabi demand and the phosphoric acid backward integration timeline but guarded on volume, debt and forward guidance, blaming monsoon and policy; analysts probed debt, subsidy collections and the weak H1 volume.

543533|2026-03.headline: eMudhra FY26 total income rose 35.1% to INR 7,132 million and PAT 26.2% to INR 1,100 million; FY27 guided to 18% top-line and 27-28% PAT growth.

For FY26, Enterprise Solutions and Services revenue was INR 5,616 million and Trust Services INR 1,400 million, with EBITDA up 32.6% to INR 1,654 million. Management guided FY27 organic top-line growth of about 18% and PAT growth of 25-30%, with an ambition to double PAT in three years. Q4 India enterprise revenue declined QoQ, which management attributed to a larger Q3 defence deal.

financial_highlights.change: Enterprise Solutions grew 55% YoY (23% organic, 32% acquisitive)

segments.name: Enterprise Solutions
segments.commentary: 59% of revenue; grew 55% YoY in FY26 (23% organic, 32% acquisitive). CertiNext (CLM) and SecurePass (IAM) added accounts across financial services, government, energy and education. India enterprise grew 27.6% for FY26 despite a Q4 dip.

segments.name: Trust Services
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue; grew 32% YoY in FY26, mainly India, driven by combo certificates, tokens sold via portal, and eSign. Management expects about 20% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Pure Services
segments.commentary: About 21% of revenue; flat YoY. Management expects no growth in FY27, in line with industry trends.

segments.name: US Products
segments.commentary: Product revenue rose from about USD 6.5-7 million to more than USD 9.5 million. Management expects 25-30% growth next year, aided by a large TLS order from the InCommon university consortium (about 700 universities).

FY27 PAT growth of about 25-30%, with a point estimate of 27-28%; ambition to double PAT over three years.

Order book projected at 2.2x-2.3x the prior-year level, with some Middle East orders delayed by the conflict that began in February.
Cryptas expected to contribute over USD 1 million of profit in FY27, dependent on replacing the incumbent US CLM vendor.

Google root certificate transition: existing roots remain trusted until new roots are accepted. Management sees no current impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will Enterprise and Services growth meet the guidance given the cybersecurity tailwinds?

qa_highlights.question: Why did India enterprise revenue fall in Q4, and what is driving trust services growth?
qa_highlights.answer: India enterprise grew 27.6% for FY26; Q3 had a larger defence deal, so Q4 looks lower. Trust Services growth came from partner-led combo certificates, token sales, retail, and eSign.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3i Infotech dispute?

qa_highlights.question: What is Cryptas' FY26 contribution and profitability outlook?

543533|2026-06.headline: eMudhra Q1 FY27 total income rose 28% YoY to INR 1,925 million, with EBITDA up 40% to INR 504 million at a 26.2% margin.
543533|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 27.8% YoY to INR 1,925 million, of which about 13 points came from the Cryptas acquisition (about INR 200 million revenue). Enterprise Solutions grew about 50% YoY and made up 65% of income, while Trust Services declined temporarily as legacy token demand fell ahead of a September security-standard transition. PAT rose 28% to INR 320 million (16.6% margin), and management kept its FY27 guidance of 18% organic growth and 25% PAT growth unchanged.

segments.name: Enterprise Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,623 million, about 50% YoY growth and 65% of total income; organic product growth about 25% after Cryptas contribution, per management. Management cited higher margin mix from lower token sales.

segments.name: Trust Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 284 million with a temporary decline as partners destocked legacy tokens before a September transition. Management estimated INR 5-7 crore of token volume was lost; token gross margin is about 10%.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Growth of about 5% YoY, supported by new US customers; margins are roughly 18-20%, similar to historical levels.

segments.name: Cryptas (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 20 crore in a seasonally weak quarter; first CertiNext sale to a German data center operator and first mSigner/PrimeSign deployment for an Austrian municipality. Management expects Cryptas to turn profitable in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 18% organic growth in total income and 25% PAT growth.
Management expects EBITDA margin around 25% and PAT margin around 16-16.5% going forward, as added sales hires weigh on costs.
Trust Service revenue likely stays lower in Q2 FY27 as legacy token demand remains weak; bottom-line impact described as limited given low token margins.
Three-year target (FY27-FY29) of doubling PAT, with about 18-20% organic revenue growth per year; Enterprise Solutions expected at 20-25% growth per year and Trust Services 15-20%.
UAE Trust Service (QTSP) licence expected around end of Q1 or start of Q2 FY27, after which launch is planned.
Expects the Cryptas loss to end in FY27 and the European subsidiary (BV) to be profitable this year; ROE expected to be maintained at about 14.5-15%.
capex_capacity: Token supply constrained: ePass token recertification by CCA submitted and largely complete, pending CCA action; management expects ePass certification by about September, after which volumes should recover.
New Innate token is certified but volumes are low because capacity is limited.

Cryptas integration of eMudhra's own CA and CLM IP replacing third-party products (such as Keyfactor) developed over the last six to seven months; this is intended to reduce cost and shift transfer pricing to India.
Added senior sales hires across geographies (USD 200,000-300,000 per person), which will weigh on near-term margins.
No capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Trust Services: partners destocked legacy tokens ahead of the September global transition to FIPS 140-3, which reduced volumes.

SecurePass in India: large bank or government deals typically start at INR 4-6 crore and can exceed INR 10 crore per bank for full PIM/PAM suites; compliance mandates from RBI-type regulators and SEBI-type regulators are cited as drivers.
US products: university federation (Common) onboarding is live, with about 1,000-1,500 certificates issued daily; IoT/PKI and SSL-expiry (47-day) demand are cited as pipeline drivers.
Agentic AI identity and signing is described as an early-stage opportunity; management said quantification is not possible yet and pilots are expected within about a year.
PrivaTrust consent-management modules are being piloted; a broader data discovery and classification suite is planned, with focus on India under the DPDP Act.

financial_highlights.change: About 13 points of 28% total income growth

qa_highlights.question: PrivaTrust cloud platform: is it live and what deployment opportunity exists in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Consent management is live with pilots and proofs of concept, with first wins expected soon. Additional data discovery and classification modules are to launch soon, with India the immediate focus because of the DPDP Act; management expects a clearer sizing in a quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: UAE QTSP licence timing and what the product is?
qa_highlights.answer: Final licence steps are underway, with completion expected around end of Q1 or start of Q2 FY27, after which launch follows. Management described it as an Aadhaar-eSign-type service, enterprise-oriented (sold mainly to banks and regulated entities) and complementary to emSigner in the UAE.

qa_highlights.question: Has the token supply issue been resolved and will Trust Services recover from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: ePass token recertification has been submitted and is largely done but pending CCA action; ePass certification is expected by about September. The new Innate token is certified but volumes are low due to limited capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Cryptas revenue for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 20 crore (INR 200 million).

qa_highlights.question: Will Trust Services be hit in Q2 and is competition a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to partners not stocking legacy tokens ahead of the September expiry, with about INR 5-7 crore of volume lost against roughly INR 8-9 crore of normal token volume. Token gross margin is about 10%, so Q2 top-line stays lower but bottom-line impact is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why are international segment margins lower than India, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Services carry 18-20% margins versus 70-75% product gross margins; Cryptas (about INR 100 crore business) was unprofitable but is expected to turn profitable this year; senior sales hires cost USD 200,000-300,000 each. Management did not give a separate international margin target, guiding instead to 25% PAT growth and 18% top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated subsidiary loss of about INR 4 crore: what is it and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the European BV entity, which incurred legal expenses; Cryptas sits under BV. Management does not expect the loss to continue this year, with a senior salesperson in Rome chasing leads that could make BV profitable.

qa_highlights.question: US products outlook, pipeline and SecurePass growth drivers in India?
qa_highlights.answer: University federation (Common) onboarding is live with about 1,000-1,500 certificates issued daily. Management said enterprise growth of about 25% is being maintained. SecurePass wins are driven by RBI/SEBI-type authentication mandates; large bank or government deals start at INR 4-6 crore and can exceed INR 10 crore with full PIM/PAM suites.

qa_highlights.question: Cryptas integration: has in-sourcing cut losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Cryptas integration of eMudhra's own CA and CLM IP replacing third-party products like Keyfactor took about six to seven months. First wins (German data center CertiNext, Austrian municipality emSigner) validate the stack, and the cost saving comes through lower third-party cost and transfer pricing to India.

qa_highlights.question: Enterprise organic growth and Cryptas data-center opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Cryptas contributed about 25% of product growth, with about 25% organic growth in the product segment. Cryptas has marquee banking, insurance and oil and gas customers now treated as prospects for eMudhra products; data-center access security is seen as a large addressable market, not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Agentic AI opportunity and revenue today?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage: conversations on agent risk, pilots expected within about a year, and no quantification yet. Agents would need digital signature certificate identities; no separate product, with CertiNext and SecurePass being strengthened instead.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin bridge and sustainable range?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin rose on lower low-margin token sales and higher Enterprise mix. Management expects margins to hold around 25% EBITDA and 16-16.5% PAT as new senior sales hires add cost.

qa_highlights.question: FY30 vision and KPIs to track for doubling profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-year target (FY27-FY29) is to double PAT, with 18-20% organic revenue growth, Enterprise Solutions 20-25% and Trust Services 15-20%. The main tracked KPI is the order book multiple disclosed in the annual investor presentation.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't the shift to Enterprise lifted ROE/ROCE and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROE was about 14.5-15% last year and could be maintained at that level; reserves build up equity over time. It argued peers rarely exceed 25% EBITDA or 16% PAT margin and that the company keeps low borrowing by strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Service revenue share and Cryptas turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Services were about 19-20% of quarterly revenue, with historical margin profile maintained. Cryptas turnaround is attributed to first wins using eMudhra products instead of third-party products.

Margin sustainability: senior sales hires at USD 200,000-300,000 each are expected to hold EBITDA near 25% and PAT near 16-16.5%.
Cryptas and BV: Cryptas expected to turn profitable in FY27; the European BV subsidiary had a consolidated loss of about INR 4 crore this quarter, linked to legal costs.
UAE QTSP licence: expected around end Q1/start Q2 FY27; launch timing and the enterprise go-to-market ramp remain unproven.
PrivaTrust and Agentic AI are early-stage with no revenue quantification; management said sizing may be possible in a quarter or two (PrivaTrust) or about a year (Agentic AI).
Legal matter with TI Infotech: no update; police have taken the company's statement. Management said the matter is in police hands with no timeline.

Our Trust Service business saw a temporary decline during the quarter following the transition to a new global security standard for digital signature tokens, which comes into effect in September.
We are not expecting the loss to continue in the current year.
