543533|2026-09.headline: eMudhra Q2 FY27 total income rose 19.6% to INR 209 crore and PAT rose 26.3% to INR 33.4 crore, but FY27 guidance was cut after a TLS certificate incident.
543533|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed strong core growth: total income INR 209 crore (+19.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 51.3 crore at 24.5% margin, and PAT INR 33.4 crore (+26.3%). H1 total income was INR 402 crore (+23.4%) and PAT INR 65.4 crore (+27%). In October, weak keys were found in eight intermediate certificates in the publicly trusted TLS hierarchy; management revoked them, exited public TLS issuance, and cut FY27 revenue guidance from about INR 825 crore to about INR 800 crore and PAT from about INR 137 crore to about INR 125 crore. Operating cash flow was weighed by lower creditors after timely payments.

segments.name: Enterprise solutions (own five-product platform)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% and now makes up about two-thirds of revenue, per the Chairman. Management said the core grew 23% in H1.

segments.name: Digital trust services (DSC, eSign)
segments.commentary: Conventional digital signatures expected flat to 8-10% growth; token revenue hit by FIPS 140-3 requirement until September. eSign is growing, now 7-8 lakh transactions per day versus 1-2 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Publicly trusted TLS
segments.commentary: About 1% of revenue; management decided to exit public TLS certificate sales. US TLS business was about INR 4 crore out of about INR 8 crore total TLS business.

segments.name: CRYPTAS (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue run-rate about INR 30 crore in the quarter; management expects about $1 million EBITDA for the year, through December.

segments.name: India vs international
segments.commentary: Total business about INR 800 crore: about INR 275 crore India and about INR 520-525 crore international. International is about two-thirds of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total income cut by about INR 20-23 crore to about INR 800 crore (from about INR 825 crore), per the call.
FY27 PAT cut by about INR 10-12 crore to about INR 125 crore (from about INR 137 crore, about 25% growth originally); impact mainly in H2.
Management expects the incident impact to last about two quarters, then return to business as usual.
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 25% going forward, with focus on higher-margin solutions business.
Incremental FY27 capex about INR 23 crore, mainly completing the data privacy (DPDP) stack, emSigner AI capabilities and ID verification for Google digital signature operations.
Investor meet planned at Trident Hotel, Mumbai, on December 2.
capex_capacity: Incremental planned capex for FY27 about INR 23 crore, directed to completing the DPDP data privacy stack, emSigner AI features and ID verification for digital signature operations.
Management did not disclose capacity or utilisation figures.
eSign volume is about 7-8 lakh per day, up from 1-2 lakh a year earlier.
demand_pricing: Customers face fixed deadlines for post-quantum migration (PQC adoption around 2029), machine and AI agent identity, and data privacy (DPDP); management says these are now board-level topics in banking.
First DPDP deal won in Q2 from an NBFC; DPDP deal sizes INR 40-50 lakh to INR 1 crore for mid-sized entities, INR 2 crore for larger ones.
Post-quantum: several POCs ongoing, one has converted into an order.

Wins: national PKI for Nigeria's certifying authority regulator; first Kazakhstan win with a defence entity; new clients in Indonesia, Philippines, Germany, Qatar and Abu Dhabi; three large enterprise clients in Europe via cross-selling with CRYPTAS.
Trust services pipeline in the UAE is building while the company awaits its trust services licence.
Management says the TLS line faces structural decline: 90-day certificates, free Google DV certificates, ACME auto-renewal, and lower EV demand.

qa_highlights.question: How large is US private PKI as a share of the enterprise business, and what is the 3-5 year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: US TLS was about INR 4 crore of the INR 8 crore TLS total; the US solutions business was about $6-9 million. Management sees private PKI for IoT and devices as a large opportunity, with a healthy pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DPDP opportunity materialising, and what are deal sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: One NBFC deal won in Q2 with more momentum in Q3. Deal sizes INR 40-50 lakh to INR 1 crore for mid-sized entities, INR 2 crore for larger ones.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Trust services trajectory for FY27, and what about CRYPTAS?
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional digital signatures are expected flat to 8-10%; eSign is growing. CRYPTAS revenue run-rate about INR 30 crore in the quarter, with about $1 million EBITDA expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Are there existing-client pushbacks or RBI contract ramp-up delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no effect on existing contracts and no terminations. The only affected party was one US university federation, which is continuing with CertiNext and has asked for subcontracted TLS. Some new TLS deals were withdrawn and other deals are slightly delayed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact on CertiNext and the broader enterprise business?
qa_highlights.answer: CertiNext is independent of TLS and is sold standalone in most cases. Management says the impact is limited to the US and a little of the Middle East; Europe, Africa and Far East are largely unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin profile hold beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin is expected at around 25%, driven by the solutions mix.

risks_watch: Reputational spillover from the TLS incident beyond the US TLS customer, especially in the US and Middle East; management expects it to wane over about two quarters.
External review by KPMG and the full ceremony-procedure review are underway; findings are to be shared.
Operating cash flow weakness in H1 from lower creditors after timely payments; receivable days flat.
Trust services (DSC) growth limited to flat to 8-10% with no new government use cases; token margins are lower.
UAE trust services licence still pending.
PQC and DPDP timelines drive the next-year pipeline; conversion of these deals is not yet proven at scale.
Management said the audit and review outcome will be shared; watch for it at the December 2 investor meet.

543539|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 84% to INR189 crore and PAT 26% to INR29.14 crore, but margins compressed on construction-cost inflation and new-project start-up costs.
543539|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of about INR189 crore (up ~84% from INR102 crore) and EBITDA of INR38.46 crore (up 35%), with PAT of INR29.14 crore (up 26%). Margins moderated on project mix, war-related construction input inflation, and early-stage costs on newly started projects. Two projects (Rashmi Vasudev and Rashmi Celestia) received OC and were handed over during the year, and the company remains debt-free. Management guided that margins will return to prior levels in FY27 and that Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature are the key cash-generating projects.

INR25,000 to INR27,000 per sq ft

segments.name: Rashmi Delight and Rashmi Manorath

segments.name: Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenu

No new land acquisitions planned in FY27 for now; township projects outside Mumbai are being explored but no suitable land found.
No dividend under consideration; board focused on project execution.
capex_capacity: Portfolio of 24 residential and commercial projects; 12.5 lakh sq ft under construction and 9 lakh sq ft in pipeline; about 7.25 lakh sq ft delivered to date.
Six ongoing projects after Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenu were started in FY26.
Total portfolio of 7.5 lakh sq ft: 4.92 lakh sq ft booked and 2.40 lakh sq ft available inventory.
Rashmi Square expected delivery FY27; Rashmi Signature Q1 FY27; Rashmi Delight and Rashmi Manorath completion next year.
Company stated it is asset-light and funds internal project cash flows from high-margin Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature; no structured debt planned for Icon or Avenu.
demand_pricing: Management reports healthy demand in Borivali, Kandivali and Dahisar with no slowdown; buyers returning from abroad and NRIs buying in India are cited as drivers.
Q3 seasonality (Shraadh period Dec to mid-Jan) cited as a slow period; management expects Q1 FY27 bookings to reflect better footfall and conversion.
Raw material cost inflation affecting only Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature, where materials are being procured at higher prices; management said impact is limited.
Supply rising in Mumbai; management says buyers are choosier and amenity-rich projects (open play areas, children's play area) are the company's advantage.
Management said the company is targeting South Bombay (Dadar talks) and Khar and Parla in western suburbs.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material inflation hit the company and was it passed through to realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature were hit minorly; other projects are unaffected and the overall impact is limited at the current execution stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended realisation and will it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 realisation was about INR25,000 to 27,000 per sq ft; management said it will not fall and Rashmi Square is targeted at INR27,000 to 28,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited construction cost inflation from the war and early-stage costs of two new projects, expecting margins to return to prior levels in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for structured debt for Icon or Avenu?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; funding will come from internal cash flows of Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature, and borrowings are minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and capital employed?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend under consideration for now as the board prioritises projects; capital employed estimated at INR80 to 90 crore as on 31 March.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery to prior levels in FY27 is management's expectation; FY26 margins fell and the cost drivers (war-related input inflation) remain open.
Rashmi Manorath has weak sales traction; company is shifting to channel partners and internal sales policies.
Rashmi Signature booking conversion (about 50% per management, analyst cited 57% of carpet area) needs to rise to the targeted ~75%.
Q4 FY26 revenue growth (analyst cited 158% YoY) and Q1 FY27 bookings are key checkpoints.
Limited new land pipeline for FY27 and difficulty finding clear-title land for township projects.
543539|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, delivery timelines and the debt-free model, but noticeably loose on specifics: several figures were corrected or left vague (realisation, carpet-area booking, capital employed), and margin recovery was asserted without numbers.
key_quotes: We don't build walls, we build homes that creates a long-term value for families and stakeholders alike.
We are still debt-free despite rapid growth.
Our profitability growth continues to be backed by actual project execution and sales conversion, not financial engineering.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Portfolio of 7.5 lakh sq ft with 2.40 lakh sq ft available inventory and 4.92 lakh sq ft booked; Rashmi Signature handover in Q1 FY27 and Rashmi Square delivery in FY27 should lift deliveries, though no FY27 volume target was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with no new land acquisitions planned in FY27 and no structured debt for Icon or Avenu; utilisation is not disclosed, so there is no capacity-pressure trigger for a capex announcement.

rows.why: Management says blended realisation will not fall and Rashmi Square is targeted at INR27,000 to 28,000 per sq ft vs about INR25,000 to 27,000 blended in FY26, but no quantified FY27 revenue target was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margins fell in FY26 (EBITDA up 35% to INR38.46 crore on revenue up ~84% to INR189 crore, so margin compressed) and war-related input inflation on Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature remains open; Rashmi Manorath has weak traction and Rashmi Signature is at ~50% booked vs a ~75% target.

rows.why: Rashmi Paradigm expected to start execution in Q2 FY27, with Rashmi Icon and Avenu already started in Feb-Mar 2026 (4,500 and 4,000 sq m layouts).

rows.why: Management set the target, and a Parla bid is in progress, but no timing or booking data was given.

rows.why: Borrowings are minimal (analyst figure INR5 to 6 crore, management says debt-free), and Icon and Avenu are to be funded from Rashmi Square and Signature cash flows.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand in Borivali, Kandivali and Dahisar, on the debt-free model and on handover timelines, but margin recovery was asserted without numbers and several figures were corrected or left vague; analysts pushed on the Q4 revenue read, carpet-area booking and capital employed

543539|2026-06.headline: Modis Navnirman Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore; PAT up 25.81% to INR8.54 crore, though EBITDA margin fell to about 20%.
543539|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore and 13.15% QoQ, with EBITDA up 14.25% YoY to INR11.65 crore and PAT up 25.81% YoY to INR8.54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to war-related material and labour cost spikes in April-May, which it said have since stabilised. The company added Khar (Rashmi Icon/redevelopment) to its Mumbai footprint, bringing the portfolio to 25 projects (six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming). Management gave no quantified FY27 project-addition target, only that two to three projects are likely in FY27.

segments.name: Mumbai redevelopment projects
segments.commentary: Six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming; 25 projects in total across Malad, Kandivali, Borivali, Dahisar, Goregaon, Khar. Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion (Ind AS 115).

segments.name: Rashmi Square / Rashmi Signature
segments.commentary: Together about 60% of Q1 revenue per analyst's question, which management did not dispute. Square at 22 slabs and roughly 80% of inventory booked; Signature at 20th slab and roughly 50-70% booked (figures varied within the call).

guidance_outlook: Management expects two to three new redevelopment projects in FY27, with no guarantee given tender uncertainty.

Four pipeline projects with aggregate GDV above INR800 crore: Rashmi Paradise to start in Q1 FY27 (this quarter), Rashmi Gold and Shectal in Q3, Khar in Q4; Govind Dalvi on hold due to a government stay on a 500-metre area.
Management cited healthy margins of around 20-30% expected per project, and 19-20% margins on upcoming projects.
Square and Signature margins are slightly below underwriting due to war-time material purchases, but not expected to be majorly hit over a two to two-and-a-half year timeline.
Management has not yet set a leverage ceiling or capital-employed framework per project.
capex_capacity: Under construction: about 12.11 lakh sq ft; upcoming pipeline about 10.5 lakh sq ft (per analyst's question, not disputed).
Rashmi Square completed 22 slabs; Rashmi Signature 20th slab; Rashmi Delight 14th slab; Rashmi Manorath 13th slab; Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue at plinth stage.
Rashmi Signature and Square expected to be handed over with occupancy certificate in Q3 FY27.
Asset-light redevelopment model: partners with societies rather than buying open-market land.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing trends are similar to before, with no significant volatility; pricing is micro-market and project specific.
Management views Mumbai demand as stable with no decline expected over the next few years, though supply has risen due to government moves on MHADA and SRA land.
Demand exists for both luxury and affordable segments; product positioning varies by micro-market (larger homes in Kandivali/Borivali).
Labour availability and cost were described as not an issue at any project now, after war-time shortages in April-May.
Expansion limited to Bombay; Parle in tender, Ghatkopar under discussion, nothing finalised. Other Indian cities open in principle.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 22.3% to about 19.8% despite 28% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the hit mainly to the war, which raised material and labour costs and caused panic buying and shortages; it said costs have stabilised and Q1 is expected to track the company's stated margin levels going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How many new projects in FY27 and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No guaranteed count; two to three development stages where the company is in the top three bidders, plus further tenders. Four pipeline projects with GDV above INR800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are Square and Signature margins tracking underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Slightly below, because materials were procured during the war; management said the impact should be minor over the remaining two to two-and-a-half year timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory status of ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Square about 80% sold; Signature about 50% (later 63-70%); Delight about 40%; Manorath 20-25%; Avenue and Icon only recently launched.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital employed and leverage be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: No leverage ceiling or capital-per-project framework set yet, as each project has different economics.

risks_watch: Margin recovery: Q1 EBITDA margin compression from war-related costs; watch whether Q2 margins return to the 20-30% range management cited.
Pipeline conversion: tenders are uncertain; Govind Dalvi is on hold due to a government stay on a 500-metre area.
Supply increase in Mumbai from MHADA and SRA land releases could pressure pricing or absorption.
Working capital and leverage: no framework yet for capital per project or leverage ceiling as project size rises.
Sales velocity: Manorath at 20-25% sold and Icon/Avenue only just launched; Square and Signature inventory is largely booked.
Thin stock liquidity noted by an analyst; management attributed it to market conditions.

543539|2026-09.headline: Modis Navnirman Q2 FY27 revenue rose to INR69.38 crore (QoQ up ~19%) with PAT of INR10.54 crore; H1 revenue up 53% YoY to INR127.64 crore.
543539|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR69.38 crore versus INR58.26 crore in Q1, with EBITDA up 25% QoQ to INR14.5 crore and PAT of INR10.54 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 53% YoY to INR127.64 crore, EBITDA 63% to INR26.19 crore and PAT to INR19.08 crore. Management cited H1 sales of about 78,560 sq ft worth INR202 crore at an average realisation of INR25,724 per sq ft. Management said H1 operating cash flow was negative (about INR16.51 crore, per an analyst's figure), which it attributed to inventory build-up and project costs, with cash-flow positivity expected around FY28.

543547|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 13% and PAT reached INR202 crore (+9%); FY27 guidance is 2.31 lakh tonnes volume at 73% utilisation, with BESS excluded.
543547|2026-03.overview: Ddev Plastiks reported FY26 revenue up 13% YoY, EBITDA up 12% at an 11% margin, and PAT of INR202 crore (+9%). Volumes were 2,01,370 tonnes at 77% capacity utilisation, with exports up 30% and export volumes up 23%. Management said the Israel-Iran conflict from 28 February 2026 raised raw material costs by 50%-plus and briefly hurt demand, but supply and pricing have stabilised since April. The company guided FY27 volume to 2.31 lakh tonnes, 13% revenue growth and ~11% EBITDA margin, and announced a foray into battery energy storage systems (BESS) targeting 5 GWh.

segments.name: Polymer compounding (cables and wires)

Installed capacity is 2,68,400 tpa, rising beyond 315,000 tpa with the Bhiwadi XLPE addition of 48,000 tpa (commercial operations from last week of April 2026).

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: New vertical; FY27 revenue expected at INR200-250 crore, with breakeven at roughly INR200-plus crore. FY28 target is 1 GWh and INR800-900 crore revenue at 10%-plus EBITDA margin (INR80-90 crore). Long-term aim is 5 GWh, or INR2,000-2,500 crore. Excluded from FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target 2,31,000 tpa at 73% capacity utilisation, with 13% revenue growth; BESS revenue excluded and additional.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at approximately 11%.

FY27 capex plan of ~INR175 crore, of which ~INR70 crore is for BESS and the rest mainly XLPE compound capacity.

FY27 capex ~INR175 crore, of which ~INR70 crore for BESS in the first phase.

BESS sourcing: lithium cells, enclosures, harness, DC cables, sensors and liquid cooling are sourced from identified suppliers; BMS is to be imported from China initially, with in-house BMS and EMS planned.
demand_pricing: Management said price pass-through is typically 7-15 days, becoming instant during sharp spikes such as March 2026; EBITDA is held at a fixed INR14-15 per kg.

Raw material prices rose 50%-plus during the conflict and have since stabilised. About 10-15% of raw material is imported, mainly from the Middle East and Europe; supply normalised by mid-April per management.
Export growth came from MENA and Europe; Latin America and North America showed no growth. Consignments stuck in March due to logistics moved in April.
Competition in XLPE is from Dow and Borealis; in HFFR from Shakun Polymer (now Orbia); in low-voltage fire-retardant from KLJ Polymers. Management said China import pressure is manageable.
Customers are mostly on contracts of up to ~90 days, with back-to-back import bookings; no open-ended annual contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 guidance imply NSR degrowth, given 13% revenue growth and 15% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is built on FY26 average realisation as a conservative base; Q1 NSR is expected to be much higher given the escalations.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BESS excluded from guidance and what is the breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: First-year ramp-up is the reason; breakeven is at roughly INR200-plus crore of revenue, and no FY27 loss is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government spending slowdown a risk to demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to private solar (Adani, Tata, JSW, Reliance), grid and peak-demand needs, and Middle East reconstruction demand, and said there is no expected impact on demand or cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 and BESS margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Total FY27 outlay is INR175 crore including BESS, of which ~INR70 crore goes to BESS; BESS margins are 5-8% lower than compounding in FY27, rising above 10% in the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS approval cycle and supplier base?
qa_highlights.answer: Developer approvals take 3-6 months, with certifications (ISO/IEC standards) in progress; suppliers are identified and locked for a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: Where does BESS IP sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial BMS will be imported from China; the company plans its own BMS and EMS IP in the coming months.

543547|2026-06.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q1 FY27 EBITDA crossed INR100 crore for the first time (INR101 cr, 10% margin), revenue up 29% YoY on export price gains.

Growth was driven mainly by export pricing (about INR300 crore export revenue, mostly MENA) rather than volume, with export volumes up only single digits and total volume up about 1% YoY. Capacity utilisation averaged about 66% as the new 48,000 t Bhiwadi XLPE plant, commissioned in April 2026, ramps up at roughly 20-25%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% volume growth and a 13-14% revenue target, and said it expects to beat it.

INR101 crore approx; first time above INR100 crore

qa_highlights.question: How much Q4 export revenue spilled into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 1,000 t moved from late-March shipments; value rose due to freight, so about INR300+ crore export revenue was reported in Q1, partly from Q4 volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA/t sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR19.6/t may not hold each quarter but could last a few months; the long-term target is INR16-17/t or 10-12% margin. The war-risk premium is about INR2.5-3/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS business model and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Starts as a supply model at 6-8% EBITDA margin, with EPC adding 2-5 points and system integrator another 2-3 points; long-term target 11-15%. BOO/BOOT not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance (13-14% revenue) below capacity growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance uses FY26 average prices, assumes about 50% Bhiwadi utilisation and 15% volume growth; management says it expects to beat guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will finance costs and cash conversion cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs rose from working-capital borrowing after the March raw material spike; they have eased since July. Cash conversion cycle expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company gain market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management cites the Bhiwadi plant and importers being displaced by supply-chain disruption. Bhiwadi will serve existing customers, mainly in Rajasthan and Delhi.

543573|2026-03.headline: Syrma SGS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR1,477 crore at 11.9% operating EBITDA margin; FY27 EBITDA guided to INR700 crore.
543573|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: consolidated revenue INR1,477 crore (+56% YoY, +16% QoQ), operating EBITDA INR174 crore (+51% YoY) at 11.9% margin, and PAT INR119 crore (+67% YoY). FY26 revenue reached INR4,857 crore (+27%), operating EBITDA INR545 crore (+68%, margin 11.3%), and the company moved to a net cash position of INR467 crore. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 30-35%, operating EBITDA margin of 10-10.5% (said to be conservative) and EBITDA of about INR700 crore, and is investing in a large PCB project. The Ksolare acquisition via the Premier Energies JV was dropped, and a greenfield renewable-inverter plan is being evaluated instead.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex profile for the PCB and other projects, and when do the government incentives start?
qa_highlights.answer: PCB phase 1 is INR400 crore (INR250 crore in FY27, INR100 crore in FY28). Organic capex is INR100-150 crore a year. Commissioning is expected towards the end of FY27 or the start of FY28, with incentives claimed in part and typically lagging by a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw-material and inflation outlook, and how are costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal prices, logistics and shipping routes are affected by the Middle East crisis. Contracts have pass-through clauses but recovery is negotiated and takes time. Management says better buying and efficiency can offset part of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 margin guided at 10.5-11% when Q4 was 11.9%?

qa_highlights.answer: Management says the project will be funded through debt, internal accruals and a 25% JV partner contribution, with subsidies of 50-60% expected. It says cash will not fall short over the project life. Balance-sheet cash is INR829 crore against a net cash position of INR470 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth comes from market share gains versus industry growth, and how does the PCB business affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the growth to market share and wallet-share gains, portfolio expansion (MedTech, defence) and larger customer contracts. PCB revenue is incremental, starting in FY28.

Management reaffirmed 10.5-11% full-year EBITDA margin guidance and said FY27 revenue growth would be 35%+, with a view to exceed guidance.

543591|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue fell to INR 660.6 crore from INR 1,291.9 crore and Q4 Gross Profit turned negative at INR -6.1 crore as domestic lounge model reset.
543591|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a transition year: domestic lounge volumes fell after banks shifted from unlimited to spend-based lounge access, cutting consolidated revenue roughly in half. Adjusted EBITDA fell to INR 25.0 crore from INR 102.1 crore and PAT to INR 11.6 crore from INR 65.1 crore. Q4 FY26 was loss-making at the gross profit, EBITDA and PAT level. Management pointed to global lounges (transaction volumes up 140% YoY), the Ten11 Hospitality railway lounge acquisition, the ongoing ETT acquisition and B2C membership (DreamFolks Club 2.0) as the growth drivers. Management said FY27 would be a transition year with breakeven possibly about a year later.

543596|2026-06.headline: TMB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 34.97% YoY to a record INR412 crores, with total business up 23% to INR1,21,715 crores.
543596|2026-06.overview: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank reported its strongest quarter on record: net profit of INR412 crores (up 34.97% YoY), NII up 32.01%, and operating profit of INR611 crores (up 48.22%). Total business grew 23%, driven by advances up 27.01% (gold-heavy, with agri at 40% of the book) and deposits up 19.71%, with term deposits up 20.73% and CASA down 2.95% QoQ as the bank prioritised resource mobilisation. Management raised FY27 guidance for deposits, advances and total business by 2 percentage points each, and cut its cost-to-income guidance, while stating that ECL transition provisioning (INR276 crores set aside so far) will be phased in. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 0.69% and NNPA at 0.17%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: 28% of advances; YoY growth of 20.09% (earlier cited 14.89%), adding about INR500 crores per quarter. Yield fell to about 10% from 10.5% as the bank widened its customer base with finer pricing.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 25% of advances. Home loans are declining but the decline is arrested; vehicle loans grew 25.7%. Retail shows a QoQ decline, which management partly attributes to migration from retail to agri gold loans.

segments.commentary: 5.62% of advances; grew 6.69% YoY. Unsecured exposure is 10 bps of the book, with NPA of about INR56 lakh.

543596|2026-09.headline: TMB posted record Q2 FY27 net profit of INR451 crore (+42.09% YoY) on 27.25% business growth, with net NPA at 0.14%.

543597|2026-06.headline: Virtuoso Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 85% YoY to INR 376.6 crore, with PAT up about 103% to INR 9 crore; FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth and 9-10% EBITDA margin maintained.

543597|2026-09.headline: Virtuoso Optoelectronics H1 FY27 standalone revenue up 78% YoY to about INR 534 crore; PAT up 213% to INR 10.22 crore.

segments.commentary: Running at about 65%-70% utilisation; capacity 1.5 lakh rising to 2.5 lakh around June-July 2027 ahead of next season. A large new customer added.

543599|2026-03.headline: Ksolves FY26 revenue rose 18.4% to INR 162.7 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 29.7% from 34.8%; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth.
543599|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR 162.7 crore (up 18.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR 48.3 crore at a 29.7% margin, and PAT of INR 34.3 crore, flat with FY25. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 43.03 crore (up 29.1% YoY, 1.7% QoQ) with a 29.3% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 9.7 crore. Margin compression was attributed to planned investments in ESOPs, leadership, travel and events, DFM product development, and a one-time INR 1.1 crore labour-code impact. For FY27, management guided to 18-20% revenue growth and a 25-30% EBITDA margin, and said it is shifting focus fully to IT services and winding down product spend.

segments.commentary: Core revenue and profit driver; services span ERP, cloud, data, AI, Salesforce and enterprise transformation. Management says 82% of revenue is recurring.

segments.name: Product (DFM)
segments.commentary: Small contributor. About INR 2 crore expensed on DFM development in FY26; two customers sold to, with two or three in pipeline now pushed to June/July. Management says no further big DFM development spend in FY27 and event spend to fall at least 60%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annual revenue growth guided at around 18% to 20%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 25% to 30%; management aspires to finish at the higher end.
FY26 expense increases (ESOPs, leadership pay, travel/events, DFM, labour-code one-time INR 1.1 crore) described as largely non-recurring.
Dividend payout to continue at 40% to 60% of profits, as no acquisitions are planned in the coming quarters.
Shift toward more fixed-price and outcome-based engagements and continued talent investment in FY27.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
DFM product development considered complete; no further large DFM investment planned in FY27.
Added ERPNext/Frappe partnership alongside Odoo to broaden ERP offering; installed-base metrics to be shared later by IR.
Multiple specialist data-science resources added for a US-based financial-crime client, supplied as dedicated people rather than employees.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth was held back by delayed POs from UAE customers due to the ongoing war; management said orders are now being released.
Management said deal conversions are strong and demand healthy, though some deals have been delayed.
Clients are migrating from SAP to Odoo to cut costs; a Tanzanian prospect was cited as a further example.
Management said pricing pressure from AI was not the reason for margin decline; no price-cut detail was given.
Management did not give a order-book or pipeline figure when asked.

qa_highlights.question: How much efficiency will AI agents bring to employee costs in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not measured it yet; agents are reducing time and raising output, and agents are being built for repetitive tasks.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover given the marketing and ESOP costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs are described as non-recurring, with some expenses continuing at lower scale; Q4 margin was at the upper end of the guided range and is expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why was DFM product spend not converting, and is there further hope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expectations were higher than customer acceptance; it sold to two customers, sees limited DFM opportunity, and will focus on services.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide to a wide 25-30% margin band and why slower growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative given geopolitical uncertainty, and that the larger revenue base means the same percentage adds more absolute revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are UAE war-related delays affecting orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; some UAE customers delayed orders, holding Q4 QoQ growth to 1.7%, and POs are now being released.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT grow faster than revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited heavy AI, insurance and IT security investment, so the 25-30% margin band is kept; the aspiration is to end at the higher end.

risks_watch: Margin band of 25-30% is wide; FY26 EBITDA margin fell about 5pp, and PAT was flat for several years.
DFM product has generated little revenue; watch whether pipeline deals close in June/July and whether product spend stays down.
Geopolitical disruption (UAE, war) is delaying customer POs; ~77% of revenue is overseas.
Concentration: top 5 clients 40% and top 10 clients 54% of FY26 revenue.
FX exposure: management said about 60% of revenue comes from North America, and the FX tailwind is currently small.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% (midpoint 19%) vs 18.4% in FY26, but Q4 QoQ growth was only 1.7% as UAE customers delayed POs and no order-book or pipeline figure was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity figures disclosed; DFM development considered complete with no large DFM investment planned in FY27, and the services model is people-based with dedicated resources rather than new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called FY27 guidance conservative given geopolitical uncertainty and said it aspires to finish at the higher end of the 25-30% margin band; Q4 EBITDA margin was 29.3%, and POs held back by UAE war are now being released.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: About 77% of revenue is overseas and UAE war-related PO delays held Q4 QoQ growth to 1.7%; top 5 clients are 40% and top 10 are 54% of FY26 revenue, so a single delayed account can move the numbers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two or three DFM deals in the pipeline are pushed to June/July, and two customers were sold to in FY26, but management sees limited DFM opportunity and is winding down product spend, with event spend to fall at least 60%.

rows.label: ERPNext/Frappe partnership alongside Odoo
rows.why: Added to broaden the ERP offering as clients migrate from SAP to Odoo to cut costs; installed-base metrics to be shared later by IR, with no numbers given on the call.

rows.label: UAE PO release and deal conversion
rows.why: Management said UAE orders are now being released after the war-related delays that held Q4 QoQ growth to 1.7%, and deal conversions are strong, though no order-book figure was provided.

rows.label: Dividend payout 40-60% of profits
rows.why: Management said the payout will continue at 40-60% of profits since no acquisitions are planned; FY26 PAT was INR 34.3 crore and the company is net debt-free with INR 6.9 crore cash.

tone.note: Management was confident on the AI-first services push and the 25-30% margin aspiration, and called guidance conservative given geopolitical risk; it was evasive on DFM revenue, pipeline size, order book and ERP installed base, which analysts pushed on.

543599|2026-06.headline: Ksolves Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 41.4 crore, but management withdrew FY27 revenue guidance while EBITDA margin hit 30.3%.
543599|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) was Rs 41.4 crore, up 10% YoY but down 3.7% QoQ, as two long-standing large clients cut work and some engagement ramp-downs landed late in the quarter. EBITDA was Rs 12.56 crore (up 26.2% YoY, flat QoQ) with margin at 30.3%, and PAT was Rs 9.21 crore (up 43.3% YoY, down 5% QoQ). Management said it would not reaffirm FY27 revenue guidance, now expecting flat-to-4-5% growth at most, and reiterated a 25-30% EBITDA margin range. The company remains debt-free and declared an interim dividend of Rs 4 per share.

segments.name: Core IT services
segments.commentary: Contributed 98.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue; management now describes the company as fully services-focused, with product business not a focus.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: 82% of revenue from overseas: North America 63%, India 18%, Europe 6%, Australia 3%, rest of world 10%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance not reaffirmed; management says FY27 revenue may be similar to FY26, with growth of up to 4-5% YoY if things go well.
EBITDA margin target maintained at 25-30% for full year and QoQ, with a move toward the upper end if revenue improves.
Softer revenue expected for the next two to three quarters as ramp-downs flow through; full impact seen over that period.
FY28 guidance to be revisited in March 2027.
Longer-term aspiration stated: about 20% growth after FY27 with roughly 30% margin, though management also said 'upper side of 30%' margins if things go well.
capex_capacity: Hiring is restricted to requirement basis; AI-driven productivity is cited as the lever to scale output with fewer new resources.
Developer efficiency reportedly up about 25% (four developers' work now done by about two); some senior developers reportedly up to 3x.
Management says the company will become an official Claude partner soon; all staff reportedly AI-certified and an enterprise Claude licence provided to everyone.
demand_pricing: Clients are tightening budgets and delaying decisions; two long-standing large T&M clients (3+ years) reduced work and headcount, citing a global headcount reduction, a management change at one, and losses at the other, not AI insourcing.
Management says most top-10 clients are stable or expanding; company added some new customers and revenue in the quarter.
Pipeline of about USD 1 million cited, with two deals of USD 300K and USD 250K; the rest undisclosed.
A major international bank (AI-hosted platform, principal vendor, roughly year-long project, still in discussion, more than 50 use cases) is in discussion; Salesforce is involved.
Middle East: no new business in the last quarter and none expected in the next few quarters; existing yearly contracts renewed. Focus shifted to Europe, Australia and the US.
More than 80% of revenue from repeat customers, per CFO.
Management says nearly every new proposal now asks for AI.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slowdown concentrated among a few large clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the top 10 are stable or growing; two clients with 3+ year relationships cut work and headcount, with one expected to ramp up next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two clients moving AI in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied this, saying the cuts were business decisions (global headcount reduction, management change, losses) and that the clients had been heavily using Ksolves on AI work.

qa_highlights.question: Will the current year look like FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue may be similar to FY26, with margins still improving and staying within 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Has AI improved efficiency and have token costs been factored into margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Developer efficiency is about 25% (senior developers up to 3x); management said token costs are below employee costs, and Claude licence spend is more than offset by benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Are layoffs happening due to AI efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: No layoffs; leavers are not being replaced unless exceptional, and hiring is on a requirement basis.

qa_highlights.question: Threat from larger players chasing smaller deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large players cannot economically serve small niche deals (for example, Big Data), so no material threat is seen.

qa_highlights.question: Deal pipeline size and five-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD 1 million of pipeline; management plans new verticals in cybersecurity and SAP, and a possible small acquisition within five years, with no current plan.

risks_watch: Revenue softness for two to three quarters as ramp-downs flow through; covering the two lost clients' revenue expected to be slow.
Concentration: top 10 clients are over half of revenue, and two large-client losses hit this quarter.
Middle East pipeline is empty for the next few quarters; growth relies on Europe, Australia and the US.
Token/AI tooling costs rising as a share of cost base; margin impact not quantified.
Monitor Q2 FY27 for revenue trend and whether the USD 300K and USD 250K deals and the bank AI project convert.
Revenue guidance withdrawn; FY28 guidance deferred to March 2027.
543599|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on revenue and explicitly conservative ("I do not want to give any false hope"), while confident on margins and AI-driven productivity. Management was candid about the two client losses but leaned on qualitative claims (pipeline, AI wins) that were not quantified.
key_quotes: I would like to be conservative. I do not want to give any false hope.
we are now moving one step forward, and we are already two steps back.
The developer efficiency, I would say, is almost 25%, so what four people were doing earlier is now being done by almost two people, at a very high level.
I have approximately 1 million US dollars of pipeline at this moment.

financial_highlights.change: +389 bps YoY (26.4% in Q1 FY26); vs 29.3% in Q4 FY26
vs Rs 2.71 in Q1 FY26 (+43% YoY)

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 30.3% in Q1 FY27 (up from 26.4% a year ago and 29.3% in Q4 FY26), and management targets 25-30% with a move to the upper end if revenue improves, but softer revenue and rising token/AI costs (not quantified) cap the upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hiring is on a requirement basis, leavers are not replaced unless exceptional, and AI productivity (developer efficiency up ~25%) is the lever to scale output with fewer people, so no new capacity is planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management says softer revenue for two to three quarters as ramp-downs flow through, FY27 revenue may be flat to up 4-5% at most (midpoint ~2.5%), and two long-standing T&M clients cut work; Q1 revenue fell 3.7% QoQ to Rs 41.4 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and capacity were not discussed as a plan; the company is asset-light with a debt-free balance sheet (Rs 17 crore cash) and hiring is restricted, so no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was withdrawn and capped at 4-5% growth, with the pipeline of about USD 1 million and two deals of USD 300K and USD 250K unconverted; only the bank AI project could change this.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance has already been cut and withdrawn, and management expects softer revenue for two to three quarters as ramp-downs flow through, with recovery from the two lost clients slow.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans new verticals in cybersecurity and SAP and says it will become an official Claude partner soon, but no product or date is firmly committed and the company has stepped back from product business.

rows.label: Large international bank AI platform project (roughly year-long, 50+ use cases,
rows.why: Project is still in discussion with no award yet, but it would be a sizable win against two lost clients, and a USD 300K and USD 250K deal are also in the roughly USD 1 million pipeline.

rows.label: Middle East exit, focus shifted to Europe, Australia and US
rows.why: No new Middle East business in the last quarter and none expected in the next few quarters, while Europe is 6% and Australia 3% of revenue, so geographic growth is limited.

rows.label: AI-led productivity with restricted hiring
rows.why: Developer efficiency up about 25% (four developers' work done by about two) and hiring restricted to requirement basis, supporting margin, though token costs are not quantified.

tone.note: Management was cautious on revenue and withdrew guidance, but confident on margins and AI productivity; analysts probed whether the two client losses were AI insourcing (management denied it) and the size of the pipeline, which was not quantified beyond about USD 1 million.

543599|2026-09.headline: Ksolves Q2 FY27 revenue fell 4.7% YoY to INR 37.8 crores on client ramp-downs; EBITDA margin 25.7%, within guided band.
543599|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 37.8 crores, down 4.7% YoY and 8.8% QoQ, driven by client-specific ramp-downs at a couple of large enterprise accounts and cautious client spending. EBITDA was INR 9.7 crores at a 25.7% margin (vs 30.3% in Q1 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26), which management attributed to lower revenue partly offset by cost actions and AI-led productivity. PAT was INR 7.25 crores (19.2% margin), and H1 revenue grew 2.5% YoY to INR 79.2 crores. Management guided FY27 revenue to trail FY26 and EBITDA margin to stay within 25-30%, with H2 focus on pipeline building, AI opportunities and enterprise account recovery.

financial_highlights.change: vs 30.3% in Q1 FY27 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26
broadly in line with H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1 per share second interim; H1 total INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT)

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Core business at 98.4% of Q2 revenue. Geography: North America 59%, India 20%, Europe 6%, Australia 4%, rest of world 11%; overseas 80%.

segments.name: BFSI / banking
segments.commentary: Three Q2 wins in banking (South America, UK, Europe). BFSI share of revenue rose from 7% to 8% (H1 FY26 vs H1 FY27 per analyst slide); management says the jump comes from H2. Company has about 11-12 BFSI clients.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 25% of revenue this year vs 27% last year per analyst reading of slides; one telecom client that was closing its business is now re-engaging.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to remain soft and trail FY26 levels; company did not reaffirm earlier guidance.
EBITDA margin expected within the 25%-30% guided range for FY27, with scope for improvement in Q4 as recent wins ramp up; management said margins would be at the upper end if sales traction holds.
Full-quarter benefit of Q2 cost actions expected from end of Q3.
Management said it is optimistic about returning to growth in FY28, with a 20%-plus growth aspiration conditional on geopolitical stability.
Dividend to be decided each year based on profitability and cash needs; shareholder returns remain a priority.
capex_capacity: Headcount fell about 10% from ~550 to ~495; hiring in FY27 limited to 5-10% of last year's level, and capacity is to be filled from the existing team before new hiring.
AI productivity: management says one person can now deliver 2x-3x prior output.

Built a low-code/no-code agent platform for a telecom client used by 500+ operations staff; migrated a US client's legacy codebase with 8 agents in about 7-8 months versus an estimated 1-1.5 years manually.
Opened a sales office in Australia for local bids; delivery team is based in India.
Being a Select Partner in Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI networks; 100% of engineers Claude certified.
demand_pricing: Client spending remains selective and discretionary spend under scrutiny; management said clients had put decisions on hold until around 10 September over AI wait-and-watch, and are now returning with AI-led requirements.
Customers now ask for Odoo, Salesforce or data engineering with agentic AI; management says the sales question has shifted from headcount to business outcome.
Two large enterprise accounts ramped down; management called these client-specific, not structural, and said the pipeline was not deep enough to offset them in the quarter.
Management said some clients tested building in-house AI tools but have since returned to outsourcing projects for features.
Top 10 clients contributed 50% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividends continue at around 100% of PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder returns remain a priority; the Board will decide each payout based on yearly profitability and cash needs. H1 interim dividend totalled INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT).

qa_highlights.question: Do you have constant-currency numbers given rupee weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company is not currently calculating revenue in constant currency.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the two clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it was large enough to be a big hit; new Q1 and Q2 wins absorbed much of it, though a deficit remained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the margin move with sales traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would be at the upper end of the guided range if revenue recovers; the INR 3.6 crore revenue drop was the main driver of the Q2 margin dip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the banking wins contribute meaningfully, and how big can BFSI become?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are underway and take months to quarters; the South American bank relationship is ongoing but expansion is not in writing. Management hopes other banks will follow.

qa_highlights.question: Are you entering cybersecurity?
qa_highlights.answer: Still exploring; management sees AI guardrails and security as a demand opportunity but has not defined the offering.

risks_watch: Revenue trend: FY27 guided soft, with dependence on recovery at re-engaged accounts and on H2 BFSI wins converting into revenue.
Margin: Q2 margin fell to 25.7% from 30.3% in Q1; watch whether cost actions hold the 25-30% band as revenue recovers.
Client concentration: top 10 clients are 50% of revenue, and two large accounts ramped down in Q2.
Currency: management does not track constant-currency revenue despite a weaker rupee, so FX effect on reported numbers is not visible.
Management did not reaffirm prior guidance; new cybersecurity vertical is still undefined.
543599|2026-09.management_tone: Candid but guarded: management called the quarter mixed and attributed the decline to client-specific ramp-downs, while staying confident about AI wins and a FY28 recovery. Answers on FY28 growth and client-level revenue were conditional or unquantified, and the company declined to give lost-revenue figures.
key_quotes: These are client -specific ramp -down, not a structural change in our business or our client relationship.
So simply put, this was a revenue -led dip.
We are now building a pipeline, even a strong pipeline enough that no client-specific decision can move our quarter the way this one did.
Ksolves is putting agentic AI into production for paying clients, not just running pilots.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 25.7% from 30.3% in Q1 on a INR 3.6 crore revenue drop; management says margins go to the upper end of the 25-30% band if revenue recovers, and full-quarter benefit of Q2 cost actions arrives from end of Q3.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Headcount fell about 10% from ~550 to ~495 and FY27 hiring is limited to 5-10% of last year's level, with existing team to be used first; no new plant, line or office capacity was guided beyond a sales office in Australia.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to trail FY26 after Q2 revenue fell 4.7% YoY to INR 37.8 crores, with two large enterprise accounts ramped down and the pipeline not deep enough to offset them; H1 growth of only 2.5% YoY is fading.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Headcount is being cut and hiring held to 5-10% of last year, with no utilisation figure disclosed and no capex plans discussed, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not reaffirm prior guidance and cut FY27 revenue to trail FY26, so an upgrade is not signalled in the next 2-4 quarters.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management did not reaffirm earlier guidance; FY27 revenue is guided soft and H2 BFSI wins and re-engaged accounts must convert, with top 10 clients at 50% of revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is exploring a cybersecurity vertical (AI guardrails and security) but has not defined the offering, and Odoo, Salesforce and agentic AI offerings are being sold without a stated launch date.

rows.label: BFSI and banking wins ramping
rows.why: Three Q2 banking wins (South America, UK, Europe) are underway but take months to quarters, and the BFSI share is 8% of revenue with about 11-12 BFSI clients; further bank expansion is not in writing.

rows.label: Return to growth in FY28
rows.why: Management is optimistic about FY28 growth with a 20%-plus aspiration, but this is conditional on geopolitical stability and the H2 recovery, and was not quantified.

rows.label: Full-quarter benefit of Q2 cost actions
rows.why: Headcount fell about 10% (550 to 495) and management guided the full-quarter benefit of the Q2 cost actions from end of Q3, supporting margin within the 25-30% band.

tone.note: Management was confident about AI wins, the BFSI pipeline and a FY28 recovery, but cautious on FY27 revenue, declined to quantify the lost client revenue, and did not reaffirm prior guidance; analysts pressed on the size of the client losses, constant-currency numbers and dividend payout.

543600|2026-03.headline: Harsha Engineers Q4 FY26 Engineering EBITDA rose to INR77 crore; FY26 Engineering revenue INR1,444 crore, guided to double-digit FY27 growth.
543600|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated Engineering revenue of INR382 crore and EBITDA of INR77 crore, versus adjusted EBITDA of INR64.3 crore in Q3 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25. For FY26, Engineering revenue grew to INR1,444 crore from INR1,269 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR264 crore (about INR270 crore adjusted for the new Labour Code impact). Solar revenue was INR183 crore with PAT of INR10.2 crore. Management guided to double-digit FY27 consolidated growth, with India Engineering in the mid-teens, and to maintaining current margins. The call also covered weak Romania profitability, the Advantek ramp-up, and the China steel-cage expansion.

financial_highlights.change: Engineering revenue growth of about 15.7% YoY excluding Solar; consolidated growth of about 27% including Solar
vs adjusted INR64.3 crore in Q3 FY26 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR264 crore reported; about INR270 crore adjusted for Labour Code impact

financial_highlights.change: PAT INR10.2 crore vs adjusted PAT INR5 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: Positive EBITDA INR4 crore; combined loss INR11.4 crore (management also cited INR11.5 crore)
Turnover about INR120 crore; PAT about INR5 crore profit; EBITDA about 11%
Turnover about INR247 crore; PAT loss about INR14 crore

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 combined loss of foreign subsidiaries
financial_highlights.value: INR9 crore (management correction from INR11 crore); prior year INR14 crore

financial_highlights.change: vs 134 days in previous quarter and 127 days in previous year

financial_highlights.value: INR120 crore consolidated; about INR20 crore in Q4

segments.name: Bearing cages (India Engineering)
segments.commentary: India-to-India cage business grew about 11% in FY26 per management. Large-size cages grew about 14% to about INR49 crore, with mid-teens to 15-20% growth expected.

segments.name: Bushings
segments.commentary: Revenue INR127 crore in FY26, up about 25%, driven by design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes from bearings to bushings. Management targets 25-30% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Stampings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR60 crore. Growth drivers are AC compressor components and white goods. Management expects at least 20% growth next year and 15-20% mid-term.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR183 crore with PAT INR10.2 crore. Q4 revenue about INR91 crore, roughly doubled YoY. Management expects more than 25% growth and Solar EBITDA margin to hold near the FY26 level.

segments.name: Advantek (India, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Still at low utilisation; FY26 EBITDA INR4 crore but net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest. Sales expected to grow at least 3x in FY27; current installed capacity seen generating INR250-300 crore turnover.

segments.name: China subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR120 crore, PAT about INR5 crore profit. Brownfield steel-cage expansion to be commissioned in H2 FY28; INR70 crore capex in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Romania subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Cage share of mix at about 22%, targeted to rise to 30-35%. Wind market in Europe not yet recovered.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected to be double-digit, with India Engineering in the mid-teens; India growth described as high-teens to mid-teens in the Q&A.
Management expects to at least maintain current margin profile in FY27, with an aim to improve it.
Over 2-3 years, management expects consolidated EBITDA to rise 100-200 basis points; India Engineering EBITDA has been consistently about 20%.
Maintenance capex in India of INR30-40 crore in FY27 and a similar amount in FY28; China expansion capex of about INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.
Advantek subsidiary expected to reach peak with current installed capacity in about two years; a second-phase capex plan is to be finalised in the next few weeks, with work starting this year.
Management indicated the India-level business could reach INR2,400-2,500 crore and consolidated INR2,700-3,000 crore on current capabilities, depending on capacity additions.
capex_capacity: Harsha has three facilities in India (the third, at Bhayla, commissioned in FY26), one in Romania and one in China.

Advantek is in its first year of operations and running at low utilisation; its sales are expected to grow at least 3x in FY27. Second-phase Advantek capex is being firmed up for additional capacity in key growth verticals.
China brownfield steel-cage expansion has begun; it will add steel cages to a predominantly brass-based portfolio, with commissioning in H2 FY28.
Management said the Advantek capex includes infrastructure that will not translate immediately into fixed-asset-to-revenue multiples.
Saket Kapoor noted PP&E closing balance of about INR615 crore.
demand_pricing: Export growth of about 17% in FY26 was attributed to improving European and US industrial markets; US import tariff on cages was cut to zero, aiding US picks-up.

Pass-through of raw-material costs (steel, brass, metal prices) to customers is contractual, with an average lag of about four months. Q4 growth was mainly volume-driven, as metal prices moved mainly from late December to February/March.

Europe demand is improving slowly, but management said there is no definitive recovery and that cost and pricing issues remain. Europe is about 30% of sales, China just over 10%, US 6-7% and Japan about 2%.
Domestic bearing makers are ramping capacity and are expected to invest further; management is bullish, though it flagged risks from the war and petroleum prices.
Cost pressure is building from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; logistics has not been impacted so far. Management is working to mitigate or pass through these costs.
Management said wallet share is about 70-90% in India but only 10-20% with large overseas customers and 2-3% with the Japan-based customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 revenue growth came from pricing versus volume, and was commodity inflation fully passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 27% consolidated growth was mainly Solar; Engineering grew 15.7% YoY. Growth was mostly volume-led, and pass-through is automatic with an average lag of about four months.

qa_highlights.question: What were the absolute FY26 revenue and PBT figures for the China and Romania subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: China: turnover about INR120 crore with PAT about INR5 crore profit. Romania: turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Combined subsidiary loss was INR9 crore after correction; management said losses would reduce significantly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Europe demand and restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is slowly improving, with no sharp recovery. Restructuring is ongoing, the cost structure is not yet right, and Romania still has negative margins. Management is evaluating how long it can sustain these margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: India maintenance capex of INR30-40 crore per year; China expansion INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28; further Advantek phase-two capex is being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is Advantek's ramp-up timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Current installed capacity expected to peak in about two years, with turnover of INR250-300 crore. Expansion beyond that is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What drives bushing growth and what is the stamping outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth comes from design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes away from bearings. Stampings (about INR60 crore in FY26) are driven by AC compressor and white goods components; management expects at least 20% growth next year.

risks_watch: Europe recovery is slow and unconfirmed; management has no clear customer read on demand, and Romania still runs negative EBITDA with restructuring incomplete.
Input cost pressure from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; pass-through lags about four months, so near-term margins could be squeezed.
Advantek: low utilisation, FY26 net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest; second-phase capex plan to be finalised in the next few weeks and its size not yet disclosed.
Subsidiary loss figures were corrected on the call (INR9 crore vs INR11 crore, Advantek INR11.4 crore vs INR11.5 crore); verify against the annual report.
Geographic mix and Solar growth (about 100% in Q4) drove the headline 27% growth; track Engineering-only growth (15.7%) against the mid-teens FY27 guidance.
Macro risks flagged by management: the war and petroleum prices could affect domestic bearing-maker demand in the short term.
key_quotes: And on your questions for the pass -through mechanism, yes, it is very well-established pass-through mechanism with the customer.
So, we are very bullish. There could be impact of, you know, current war and petroleum prices and all that.
So, last whole year, we are seeing demand has slowly improved over the year.
We are continuing to face massive inflationary pressure in Europe, which is also adding to this whole challenge.
543600|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on India Engineering, bushings, large-size cages and domestic bearing-maker demand, and gave specific FY27 growth targets. It was more cautious on Europe and Romania, saying the recovery is slow, there is no definitive turnaround, and restructuring is incomplete; on margins it said it would maintain them, with improvement as an aim rather than a firm target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects consolidated EBITDA up 100-200 bps over 2-3 years and at least maintain the current margin in FY27, though India EBITDA is steady at about 22% and Q4 Engineering EBITDA rose to INR77 crore from INR64.3 crore in Q3, while oil, lubricant and plastic cage cost pressure builds with a roughly four-month pass-through lag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: H2 FY28 for China; Advantek peak in about two years
rows.why: China brownfield steel-cage expansion with INR70 crore capex in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28 is due in H2 FY28, and Advantek's current installed capacity is expected to peak in about two years at INR250-300 crore turnover against FY26 sales that are small.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guided to double-digit growth, with India Engineering mid-teens (FY26 India up about 14%, exports up about 17%), Bushings 25-30%, Solar above 25%, and Advantek sales at least 3x; Q4 Engineering growth of 15.7% was mainly volume-led.

543600|2026-06.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.
543600|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Engineering supply rose to Rs 421 crore from Rs 382 crore QoQ and Rs 349 crore YoY, with India Engineering growing about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ. Consolidated Engineering EBITDA was Rs 69.8 crore versus Rs 77 crore QoQ and Rs 65.3 crore YoY, so margin fell QoQ. Management attributed the squeeze to an ~8% rise in average raw material cost (lagged pass-through of one to two quarters), about Rs 4 crore of FX hedge accounting loss, and about Rs 3 crore of higher indirect material costs after the West Asia conflict. Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

-9% QoQ vs Rs 77 crore; +7% YoY vs Rs 65.3 crore
Positive EBITDA of Rs 2.82 crore; down QoQ (Q4 seasonally strong)

segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ; EBITDA and PAT up YoY but margin down QoQ on material pass-through lag and FX loss. Management guides high-teens India growth for FY27.

segments.name: Harsha Advantek (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales about Rs 30 crore (+7% QoQ), EBITDA margin about 9%. FY27 target Rs 140 crore plus vs Rs 43 crore in FY26; expected PAT positive by end-FY27.

segments.name: Harsha China
segments.commentary: Stable and profitable; FY27 revenue growth about 10% on FY26 base of about Rs 120 crore, EBITDA margin 12-14%, PAT about 6%. Brownfield steel cage expansion to commission by Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Harsha Romania
segments.commentary: Still loss-making; slight top-line growth but one-time FX loss of about Rs 2 crore in Q1. Management expects some losses in FY27, aiming for break-even; new top management in place.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 36.3 crore, EBITDA Rs 2.82 crore; management guides about Rs 200 crore FY27 revenue at 7-8% EBITDA margin, project-driven and seasonal.

segments.name: Large-size cages
segments.commentary: Q1 sales only about Rs 10 crore on capacity ramp-up constraints at new facility; management still targets about 50% growth on FY26 base of Rs 49 crore (the call also cites about 30%, so the target is unclear).

guidance_outlook: India Engineering: high-teens growth in FY27 (volume-led, with some price pass-through); India Engineering EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%, with management noting the 24% Q1 standalone figure may be high due to lag cycles.
Consolidated FY27: low-to-mid-teens sales growth; management called 20% a very tough stretch.
Bushing: about 30% growth in FY27 vs Rs 127 crore in FY26.
Stamping: about 30% growth in FY27 vs Rs 60 crore in FY26.
Japanese customers: about 10% growth to about Rs 72-80 crore (management also said Rs 80 crore or thereabouts).
Consolidated EBITDA margin could recover to about 18% (FY26 level 18.7%) if metal prices stabilise; management had no view on RM price normalisation.
Subsidiaries: China plus Romania revenue growth below 10%; combined FY27 loss about Rs 2-3 crore, with Romania possibly profitable next year.
CapEx: Rs 50-80 crore per year, with Rs 180-200 crore combined over 1.5-2 years for Bhayla Phase-2 and China expansion.
capex_capacity: Bhayla (India) Phase-2 expansion: building construction delayed by heavy rain in Ahmedabad, expected to start this month; third building targeted for completion by end-2026 or Q4 FY27.
Bhayla total target: about Rs 300-400 crore revenue by year three across both phases; Phase-1 and Phase-2 demand visibility expected to absorb capacity within about one year.
China Brownfield steel cage expansion: funded with debt at attractive rate; construction under way; commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact from FY29.
Large-size cage capacity at new facility still ramping up, constraining Q1 volumes.
Advantek Phase-2 expansion (bushings, stampings, large cages) announced earlier; Advantek FY27 target Rs 140 crore plus.
demand_pricing: Cage demand strong in India from bearing majors and MNC customers' new plants; exports from India Rs 139 crore, +22% YoY.
Europe and US demand improving alongside industrial demand; management described growth as broad-based.
Raw material cost up about 8% in Q1 across brass, copper, zinc, steel and polymer; pass-through lag of one to two quarters (about four months per CFO).
Management estimated the raw material increase would lift prices by about 3-4% (CFO said 40-50% of a 6-7% increase), though the CEO declined to quantify the price impact.
Top 10 customers about 80% of revenue; top customers (SKF, Schaeffler, Timken, NBC, ZF, Flender) rank in a shifting order; management claims 80-90% wallet share with major Indian customers.
Management cited wind bushing upgrades, rail stampings and defence/aerospace stamping developments as future growth areas.

qa_highlights.question: Was the growth broad-based across segments, and was it driven by Europe or India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was broad-based, with industrial demand strengthening in India and European demand recovering. It called 20% FY27 consolidated growth a very tough stretch and expects mid-to-high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth.

qa_highlights.question: Which raw materials drove the cost increase, and how is foreign EBITDA margin trending?
qa_highlights.answer: The RM increase spans brass, copper, zinc, steel and polymer, not just brass as last year. On foreign subsidiaries, management said it is trying to shift to cages, while the raw material spike and FX offset the revenue gains. Management did not quantify the margin decline.

qa_highlights.question: How large are the Romania losses, and is the subsidiary restructuring on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Romania did not significantly improve ex-FX and copper prices hurt results. Sanjay Majmudar guided combined China and Romania loss of about Rs 2-3 crore for FY27 versus about Rs 10 crore last year, with Romania possibly profitable next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are bushing and stamping growth sustainable, and is large-cage growth credible after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth is driven by conversion and wallet share, with conversion expected to support growth for at least a couple of years. Stamping growth comes from new products maturing over about one year. Large-cage Q1 was about Rs 10 crore due to ramp-up constraints at the new facility, and management still expects about 30-50% growth, citing order book and pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CapEx outlook for FY27 and FY28, and what is the Bhayla status?
qa_highlights.answer: China Phase-2 is on track for Q3 FY28 commissioning. Bhayla building construction was delayed by heavy rain and expected to start this month, with the third building targeted for completion by end-2026 or Q4 FY27. Annual CapEx is guided at Rs 50-80 crore, with Rs 180-200 crore over 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India growth is volume versus price, and what price increase is being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is the focus and the price impact is not being predicted. Maulik Jasani estimated the 6-7% RM increase would lift selling prices by about 40-50% of that, roughly 3-4%. The Japanese customer was Rs 21 crore in Q1 versus Rs 16.5 crore a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Advantek EBITDA and margin expectations, and what is the normal India Engineering margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Advantek Q1 EBITDA margin was about 9%, and it is expected to be slightly below the India blended margin in FY27, matching it from FY28. Vishal Rangwala said the 24% Q1 standalone margin is high and a normal sustainable margin is 20-22%. Jason Soans's question on the 22-24% guidance was answered by Maulik Jasani, who said margin percentage will fall as pass-through lifts realisations.

risks_watch: Raw material pass-through lag of one to two quarters: Q1 margin compressed on an 8% RM rise, and recovery depends on metal prices stabilising (management had no view on normalisation).
Solar EPC volatility: Q1 revenue Rs 36.3 crore vs a Q4-heavy seasonal pattern; FY27 guide of about Rs 200 crore at 7-8% EBITDA margin.
Romania: still loss-making, one-time FX loss of about Rs 2 crore in Q1, no break-even timeline, and copper prices weighed on results.
Large-size cages: Q1 sales about Rs 10 crore and new facility still ramping; the FY27 growth target is stated as both about 50% and about 30%, so it needs clarification.
Bhayla Phase-2 construction delayed by monsoon rain, and China commissioning slipped to Q3 FY28 with revenue from FY29; watch construction milestones next quarter.
Advantek PAT-positive target by end-FY27, with FY27 sales target of about Rs 140 crore plus against Rs 43 crore in FY26.
key_quotes: As you would have seen on a consolidated basis, we have posted a 25% growth in Quarter 1 and year-over-year
However, there will be a lag of one or two quarters. Thus, we should be able to pass through this cost increase in the subsequent quarter.
I think 20% is a very tough stretch.
So, we expect that absolute value increase will continue, but definitely percentage will reduce because the material pass through will enhance the sales price recovery

543600|2026-09.headline: Harsha Engineers Q2 FY27: consolidated Engineering revenue INR428 crores (+18% YoY) and EBITDA INR81.1 crores; India growth above 24%, Romania being downsized.
543600|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 as business as usual and largely on track, with India Engineering revenue up over 24% YoY and H1 up about 23%. Consolidated Engineering revenue reached INR428 crores versus INR363 crores a year earlier, and consolidated EBITDA margin rose to about 18.6%, helped by metal pass-through, lower solar mix and operational efficiency. Management reaffirmed full-year FY27 guidance of mid-to-high teens India growth and 10-12% consolidated growth, but stressed it is conservative given metal-price inflation and a planned Romania downsizing. Romania downsizing details, capex timing and Advantek losses remained open items for next quarter.

Global volume growth target of 12-15% for the company; Q2 pass-through estimated at 4-5% of H1 growth.

Japan-based customer Cage growth: H1 up about 28%; management guides 10-15% annual growth.

Metal pass-through: copper and zinc (brass) increases over the last six months partly passed through; pass-through remains ongoing with lag per customer, and indirect cost inflation is not fully recovered.
Management estimates it captures a large share of incremental bearing-capex-driven Cage demand from Indian bearing makers; Cage TAM estimated at about 5% of bearing value.
Aerospace and defence stamping opportunity is small, about INR20-30 crores; a larger stamping opportunity is in other components.

qa_highlights.question: Romania: will operating profitability convert into net profit, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to confirm net profitability; it is working on cost structure and will update quarterly. Details of downsizing were deferred to about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18.6% margin driven by pass-through or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both: some metal pass-through, lower solar contribution, and operational efficiency. India margin was seen as steady around 22%, with consolidated margin of 17-18% for H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 consolidated guidance only 10-12% after 21% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited metal inflation, quantitative growth of 12-15%, and Romania downsizing reducing contribution. India guidance is conservative, not an implied slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and split between Advantek and China?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India capex is about INR110 crores over 1-1.5 years and China about INR100 crores; about INR70 crores spent in H1. Completion targeted by June 2027 with go-live later.

qa_highlights.question: Advantek peak interest and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined interest and depreciation around INR7.5-8 crores currently, rising to a maximum of about INR10 crores once fully running; Advantek capex loan about INR250 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Bushing contract delayed and what about large windmills?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bushing contract commercialisation is slightly delayed but still expected. It is supplying Bushings to a 16 MW windmill application and sees a continued opportunity.
