543619|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore with PAT INR 42.7 crore and executable order book of about INR 697 crore, 3.3x FY26 revenue.
543619|2026-03.overview: Management (Joint MD Gaurav Lath) framed Concord as evolving from a railway equipment maker into a full-stack railway technology and lifecycle platform, built on four pillars: green mobility, smart locomotive intelligence, railway safety (Kavach/MSDAC), and AI-driven diagnostics. FY26 figures stated were revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore, PAT INR 42.7 crore, EBITDA INR 62.1 crore, and an executable order book of about INR 697 crore at 31 March 2026. Working capital was the main analyst concern: receivables and short-term debt rose sharply, which management attributed to back-ended railway billing in Q4 and said will persist through the growth phase. Several questions on Fusion Electronics revenue, Kavach tender outcomes and loco-Kavach opportunity size got non-committal answers.

segments.name: Locomotive solutions
segments.commentary: Management said locomotive solutions are currently the larger contributor to growth, including DPWCS (distributed power wireless control systems). No segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Kavach / railway safety (via Progota)
segments.commentary: Field trials started; management hopes for a successful year. Trial completion and ISA approval are targeted within FY27. Kavach pillar is positioned as large and long-duration, with no revenue figure given.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Demonstrated India's first indigenous zero-emission diesel-to-battery locomotive retrofit. Also cited a recent NTPC order, with no value disclosed.

EBITDA margin guidance of 20% to 25%; management said guidance is realistic, not conservative.

Fusion Electronics expected to contribute revenue in the current financial year; no figure given.
Management aims to complete Kavach trial and ISA approvals within FY27, with geopolitical factors cited as a constraint.
Management did not give a peak debt or working capital estimate; said Q1 receivables will be high and working capital needs will persist.
capex_capacity: Fusion Electronics has installed flex PCB and box-build capacity; full-scale revenue potential about INR 200 crore with capacity doubling provision.
Management said it has been frugal on investment and will consider raising its Progota stake when returns justify it; no decision announced.
Field-level in-house engineering team on locomotives reportedly gives execution efficiency for loco Kavach installation.

Kavach: a tender for about 4,500 loco units closed 14 April 2026 with no outcome yet. Management said tender finalisation takes time and Concord has quoted several tenders.

No direct response on whether the LNG and geopolitical crisis could slow railway spending, beyond general references to uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise sharply, and will this working capital pattern continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to back-ended Q4 billing and customer acceptance cycles with railways. Said receivable cycles had improved by June versus last year, and confirmed similar working capital will recur.

qa_highlights.question: How should debt and balance sheet strength be seen over the next few years, given short-term debt rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 is always heavier and working capital will spike with the INR 697 crore order book, then ease. It declined to give peak debt estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% to 25% EBITDA guidance conservative given around 30% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for realistic guidance and that technology adoption is faster than expected, without accepting the conservatism framing.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and is there any liquidity challenge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said railway payments are streamlined and sovereign-backed with no penalty or bad-debt risk, and that cash flow will not deter growth. Confirmed that some money started coming in from April, but gave no timeline for positive operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company face penalties for delayed order execution, and will it grow execution faster than 40% to 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company executed similar growth last year and planned more structured execution for the large order book. No penalty figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can Fusion Electronics deliver this year, and why has it shown little revenue so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a turnaround with a typical 300-day integration cycle and said full-scale revenue could be about INR 200 crore. It expects revenue contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: How will Kavach orders be executed, and when will the 4,500-unit loco Kavach tender be decided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kavach orders have two to three phases (production, inspection, installation), with part of the invoice paid on delivery and the balance after installation. The tender outcome timing was not given; it said finalisation is a process.

Execution risk on a INR 697 crore order book with an 18 to 24 month cycle and possible penalties for delays (not addressed in detail).

543619|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose ~95% YoY to ~INR 159 crore, EBITDA ~INR 46.7 crore at 29.3% margin, unexecuted order book INR 846 crore.
543619|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue of ~INR 159 crore (up ~95% YoY), EBITDA of INR 46.7 crore (up ~110%) and PAT of INR 31.2 crore (up ~95%), with a 29.3% EBITDA margin. Debtor days fell from 210 to 178 and inventory days from 313 to 259 over six months. Management said the unexecuted order book stood at INR 846 crore as of 30 September 2026, against an opening INR 697 crore, and targeted a 40-50% revenue CAGR over three to five years. Key uncertainties remained on Kavach approved-vendor status, which is still in trials with no timeline given, and on the main board migration, which is awaiting eligibility.

financial_highlights.change: down from 210 days in six months
opening FY27 INR 697 crore; H1 inflow INR 308 crore

segments.name: Locomotive subsystems (ex-Advanced Rail, now merged)
segments.commentary: Management said more than 80% of current revenue and about 80% of the future order book (excluding Kavach) come from locomotive subsystems and green mobility. Advanced Rail is now a single unit with Concord.

segments.commentary: Progota is an associate, so only profit share is booked, not revenue consolidation. Management said Kavach is still in trials for approved-vendor status; no timeline given. Shareholder query on Kavach segment revenue was deferred to the IR team.

segments.name: Fusion (PCB / EMS, acquired)
segments.commentary: Backward integration into PCB, PCB assembly and SMT EMS has started. Management expects around INR 400 crore revenue at full scale; plant described as production ready, and first revenue hoped for in FY27.

segments.name: Green mobility / propulsion
segments.commentary: One battery locomotive delivered and running for over 12 months. A green hydrogen propulsion order is to be executed next year, and a 3100 HP hydrogen loco is in development. IGBT propulsion is in development.

guidance_outlook: Targeting a revenue CAGR of about 40-50% over the next three to five years, which management said implies roughly INR 1,000 crore revenue by FY30 when a shareholder raised it, without confirming that number.
H2 has historically been about 60% of the year's revenue versus 40% in H1; management expects the same pattern in FY27 and ex-Kavach growth of similar magnitude next year.
International markets expected to contribute one-fourth to one-half of revenue over three to five years; a few orders of a few million dollars possible in the current or next year.
Fusion expected to marginally improve profitability by some basis points in FY28.
Management said margins of 29-30% are sustainable, citing in-house technology.
capex_capacity: Fusion installed capacity exceeds 2 lakh sq m of flex PCB, plus additional rigid PCB capacity.
Management expects to use 30-40% of Fusion's SMT/PCBA capability for internal needs, with rigid PCB use only marginal.
Fusion plant described as production ready; Fusion exhibiting at Electronica Germany after Diwali.
Hydrogen propulsion system to be deployed by early next year per management.
No fundraise planned in the near term based on the current order book; working capital said to be adequately covered by banks.
demand_pricing: Kavach: management said roughly 10% of the Kavach opportunity is deployed so far and the programme runs over 10-15 years; new competition expected but seen as having long gestation.
Non-Kavach order book addition of INR 100-plus crore from locomotive subsystems and real-time monitoring and sensing applications.
Kavach orders carry a 12-month delivery period per management, though the company is not yet an approved vendor.
Price variation clauses in railway tenders differ; where unavailable, component cost rises from geopolitical issues are absorbed. Fusion work for third parties is a complete pass-through.
Discussions with 3 or 4 companies (e.g. HBL, Kernex named by analyst) to sell flex/rigid PCB and PCBA.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for Progota developer-to-approved-vendor status for Kavach.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trials are progressing and the outcome will come soon, but declined to give any date or number.

qa_highlights.question: Status of main board migration.
qa_highlights.answer: Eligibility to be completed very soon; applications to be filed immediately after.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue would a Kavach order add to Concord, given Progota is an associate?
qa_highlights.answer: Progota is 46.5% owned and is equity-accounted, so only profit share appears; no line-by-line revenue consolidation. Management said revenue is growing without Kavach.

qa_highlights.question: Share of H1 and backlog from Advanced Rail/locomotive versus legacy business.
qa_highlights.answer: Over 80% of current revenue and about 80% of future order book, ex-Kavach, is locomotive subsystems and green mobility.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins of 29-30% be the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are a focus and expects to sustain them with economies of scale and in-house technology; no numerical guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Best-guess FY27 and FY28 revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: No number given. Management reiterated H2 is typically about 60% of annual revenue and 40-50% CAGR target.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and fundraise plans before main board migration.
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital adequately covered by banks; no fundraise planned on the current order book, citing OpEx reasons.

543620|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% to INR2,146 crore and PAT 59% to INR201 crore; cell line guided to lift EBITDA margin toward 20%+ later.
543620|2026-03.overview: Insolation Energy listed on BSE and NSE Main Board on 9 March 2026. FY26 revenue from operations was INR2,146 crore (up 61%), EBITDA INR305 crore (up 79%, margin 14% vs 13%), and PAT INR201 crore (up 59%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR794 crore (up 100% YoY), with EBITDA INR111 crore and PAT INR70 crore, though management said utility-scale dispatches cluster in the last month of each quarter. Management is building a 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line and 4.5 GW aluminium frame plant at Narmadapuram, with cell COD targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27 and frames in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / ROCE / ROE

financial_highlights.value: INR835 crore (long-term INR468 crore; short-term INR300 crore)
financial_highlights.change: from INR108 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: FY26 sales mix was about 85% non-DCR and 15% DCR. Module capacity is 5.5 GW. Management targets about 2 GW production and sales from modules in FY27, with non-DCR at 2-2.5 GW and DCR cells sourced externally on top.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Very nascent; minimal revenue in Q4 FY26. A third-party order of over INR300 crore secured last year is expected to contribute revenue in FY27.

segments.name: IPP (KUSUM)
segments.commentary: Targeting about 325 MW AC / 400 MW DC, with 38-40 MW commissioned so far. FY27 IPP revenue guided at about INR135 crore; FY28 at about INR300 crore. Capex about INR1,000 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least equal to FY26 (about 50-60%), subject to market conditions; FY28 revenue target above INR5,000 crore.
EBITDA margin in FY27 expected at 14-15% including aluminium frame integration; management says 20%+ once the full cell line runs (FY28 framing).
FY27 capex about INR2,500 crore: about INR1,500 crore for the cell line (including working capital margin and contingency) and about INR1,000 crore for KUSUM IPP.
Positive free cash flow expected 6-8 months after cell plant goes live (Q4 FY27), per CFO.
Wafer/ingot plant (4.5 GW, CZ technology, about INR1,000-1,200 crore capex) to be funded mainly from internal accruals; DPR due in 2-3 months.
Peak debt expected near INR1,500 crore in FY27; IREDA loan of INR1,134 crore, 12-month moratorium then 7-year repayment, at 8.95% post-COD.
capex_capacity: Sawarda Unit 3 (INR320 crore) fully operational with all three lines running.

4.5 GW TOPCon cell line at Narmadapuram: INR340 crore drawn from IREDA by 31 March 2026; expected to start ramp-up in Q4 FY27, full ramp about 3-4 months later (management said full utilisation by Q1 FY28).
Aluminium frame plant (4.5 GW) expected to commission in Q1 FY27; mainly for internal use.
Next phase: 4.5 GW ingot and wafer on 70,000 sq m of land acquired in Narmadapuram; about 20 acres remain. ALMM Part 3 effective 1 June 2028 is the stated timing driver.
Cell line plant efficiency target above 80%; management says the cell capacity is used internally first, with any surplus sold in the open market.
demand_pricing: Current order book of about 1.6-1.8 GW for this year, per management; about 50% of FY27 capacity already booked, with the rest refilled monthly from distributors, OEM white-label and KUSUM partners.
Non-DCR module prices about INR13-14/W; DCR about INR20-22/W (Mono PERC INR20-21, TOPCon INR21-22, up to INR22.5 in some locations).
Sales mix by segment in FY26: utility about 65%, KUSUM about 15%, PM Surya Ghar about 5%, OEM about 5%, miscellaneous about 10%.

Raw-material cost pressure noted; management said it will pass through some increase and absorb some, relying on about 2-3 months of raw material held in inventory against orders. Escalation clauses are mostly USD-linked.
Management estimates about 30 GW of non-ALMM modules in the market, and said non-DCR cell demand remains for 1-1.5 years of tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility on FY27 volume and margin after the cell line comes on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 2 GW module production and sales in FY27 and 14-15% EBITDA margin, rising to 20%+ with the full cell line. Ravi said margins could be revised upward if market conditions allow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did December and March not sustain the run rate of Q4 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utility-scale dispatches are concentrated in the last month of each quarter, with about INR350 crore in December and about INR440 crore in March, and that this is an industry pattern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and debt picture after receivables rose 156%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said short-term borrowing rose because of capacity scale-up, and that orders are now on 45-day LCs, which lifts receivables. IREDA drawdown of INR340 crore is largely parked in FDs of about INR300 crore; the remaining drawdowns are expected within 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost on borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: IREDA loan sanctioned at 9.20% pre-COD and 8.95% post-COD. Working capital borrowings are close to 8%.

Cell line ramp timing (Q4 FY27 start, full utilisation by Q1 FY28); next two quarters' utilisation guided at only 60-70%.
Heavy reliance on Chinese equipment for the cell line; management cites a two-year on-site support contract with the supplier.
Quarter-end-loaded dispatches make quarterly revenue and receivables lumpy; receivables rose to INR280 crore.
Negative FCFF (CFO's FCF yield cited as -15.9%) until the cell plant is operating; peak debt near INR1,500 crore in FY27.
Wafer/ingot plant (INR1,000-1,200 crore) remains at DPR stage with no technology partner named; the CZ technology choice is still under consideration.

543626|2026-03.headline: Electronics Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% to INR1,913 crores and SSSG hit 12.2%, with EBITDA margin up to 6.7%.
543626|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15% YoY to INR1,913 crores, with EBITDA up 20% to INR129 crores and margin expanding to 6.7% from 5.6%. Same-store sales growth was 12.2% in the quarter, helped by GST rate cuts, festive demand and mobile launches, while FY26 SSSG was 5.3%. FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR7,183 crores with EBITDA of INR438 crores (6.1% margin) and PAT of INR107 crores. Management said working capital requirements have fallen and pre Ind AS operating cash flow reached INR299 crores for the year.

segments.name: South cluster (AP, Telangana, Hyderabad)
segments.commentary: Management cites a 6.5% EBITDA margin for the South cluster, with about INR6,000-6,500 crores of revenue from the region (69 AP stores, 46 Telangana, 72 Hyderabad city). Hyderabad city generated about INR4,122 crores in FY26; Hyderabad SSSG was double-digit in Q4.

segments.name: North cluster (NCR/Delhi)
segments.commentary: Delhi NCR operates 35 stores with about INR590 crores of revenue in FY26 and is now EBITDA positive on a full-year basis. Management guided to 25-30% growth in FY27 and a 2.5-3% EBITDA margin, versus about 0.2-0.3% now; Q4 Delhi like-to-like sales were reported at about 19%.

segments.name: Mature vs new stores
segments.commentary: Of 223 stores, 83 are over 4 years old (about 7.3% EBITDA margin) and 140 are under 4 years old (about 3.1% margin).

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Panels grew 13% and mobile phones 28% in Q4; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, refrigerators were stable, and large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%.

guidance_outlook: Organic store additions of about 20 in FY27 (12-15 in NCR and AP/Telangana per management, plus Delhi and South openings), with capex of about INR3-4 crores per store assumed for 8,000-10,000 sq ft stores.
New East entry starting with 5-7 stores in Kolkata by end-Q2 or start-Q3 FY27; FY27 real estate spend of about INR50 crores, up to INR100 crores over 12-14 months.

NCR revenue target of INR800+ crores in FY27 (vs INR585 crores in FY26), with 2-4% EBITDA margin; Andhra Pradesh (INR1,100+ crores) and Telangana (INR1,000 crores) expected to deliver higher single-digit SSSG.
North cluster margin to be 3-4% higher than now by FY28 (not stated as an exact level).
Management expects ASPs up at least 5-6% on average in FY26 with volume held; price hikes are passed through to customers; inventory to be bought 2-3% higher at newer prices for the next 20 days.
capex_capacity: Store count 223 (83 over 4 years old, 140 under 4 years); Q4 added 4 stores (NCR, Telangana, 2 in Andhra Pradesh).
Management plans 12-15 organic stores in NCR, AP and Telangana, with 4-5 Delhi stores getting ready, and 7-8 more stores in NCR; new Kolkata cluster to start with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.
Store size 8,000-10,000 sq ft typical, capex about INR3-4 crores per store, similar product mix in new regions.
Working capital requirement reduced; cash flow prioritised over expansion, with loans against property repaid organically.
Franchise model not in use; all stores company-operated, with franchising only to be explored if OEMs support it.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand robust across categories; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, panels 13%, mobile phones 28% (new launches in January and March).
ASPs rose at least 5-6% on average in FY26 for the same volume (bigger TV sizes after GST cut, higher-star ACs), and management says no category saw ASP decline.
Price hikes on RAC products of about INR1,500-2,000 per SKU are passed on to customers; additional inventory bought at 2-3% higher prices.
Entry-level mobile price hikes (below INR20,000) have limited impact, as the company's mobile ASP is about INR35,000-40,000.
Sourcing is essentially direct from OEMs/brands; distributor purchases are about INR50 crores a year, with margins unchanged.
Competition: NCR faces Croma, Reliance and Vijay Sales; South competes mostly with mom-and-pop stores, which drives the margin gap.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hyderabad SSSG double-digit in Q4 and how should FY27 be read?

543644|2026-09.headline: InfoBeans Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 165 crore and PAT grew 16% YoY, with 6% QoQ revenue growth, the seventh straight quarter of sequential growth.
543644|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 165 crore, up 28% YoY from Rs 129 crore, and up 6% QoQ; PAT rose 16% YoY and 21% QoQ to Rs 26 crore. Operating margin was about 24%, against a stated target of 24% and PAT margin of 14-15%. Excluding the prior-year H1 Employee Retention Credit (Rs 6.3 crore), H1 revenue grew 30% in INR and 22% in USD terms. The call also covered Claude Select Services partner status with Anthropic, a net addition of 43 employees on a base of about 1,800, and an M&A search with no deal announced.

PAT margin ~16% in H1 as stated

guidance_outlook: Long-run targets stated as 24% operating margin and 14-15% PAT margin; management said continued AI investment may pressure margins in future.
Net headcount addition guided at 10-15% for the year, with AI expected to improve efficiency and delivery optimisation.
Management does not give revenue forecasts but described a sustained momentum, healthy order pipeline and healthy demand.
M&A: active scouting for targets in AI and data and ServiceNow; leads received this quarter, no deal stage disclosed; acquisitions to be announced once a term sheet is signed.
Management stated the company is not focused on dividend yield; dividends and buybacks are made as and when needed.
capex_capacity: Capitalised about Rs 9 crore of intangible development cost for products Stanza and Beantrail; amortisation has started, per management.
Development centres in Indore, Pune, Chennai and Bengaluru; nearly 1,900 people in total, with fewer than 50 based outside India.
Investment in AI capability and in building out sales teams across geographies noted as a continuing cost item.
demand_pricing: Management reported no pricing pressure from clients and said the shift to outcome-based pricing has not reduced top-line; net headcount additions are lower than revenue growth.
Revenue growth was about 90% from existing clients and about 10% from new clients YoY; management said new-client relationships take 6-12 months to close large deals.
Claude Select Services partner status with Anthropic obtained two weeks before the call; a dozen certified cloud developers and a couple of deployed engineers; ISO 42001 certified for AI practices.
Core offerings are AI-led engineering, Salesforce and ServiceNow practices. Long client relationships cited: one client about 9 years, another 22-23 years, IQVIA 18 years.
Visa restrictions in the US: management said less than 50 of nearly 1,900 people are on US visas, so the impact is insignificant.
Management said it does not disclose individual deal sizes; two US and one India wins were mentioned via press release.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company devoting capacity to strong growth, and which industries are performing well?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is spread across BFSI, manufacturing, logistics and HR with no single industry standing out; healthcare compliance was the only softness.

qa_highlights.question: How much net hiring was done and what are the plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Net addition of 43 in the quarter on a base of 1,800+ (about 2-3%); the year-level guidance is 10-15% net addition, with AI used to raise efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing pressure seen from AI or outcome-based pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no pricing pressure and that outcome-based pricing has not hurt the top line; AI is also used internally to cut evaluation and appraisal cycles from weeks to days.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the Rs 9 crore capitalised intangibles and the director loan.
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 9 crore relates to products Stanza and Beantrail, now amortising. The loan was a US employee-policy loan of up to USD 1 million to a director, interest-bearing, given for 3-4 months and repaid.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of 22% constant-currency growth between existing and new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% from existing clients and about 10% from new clients; trust takes time and new deals typically take 6-12 months to close.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook, US concentration and visa risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to raise US share (49% now) and to expand the US sales team; visa restrictions have little impact since about 50 of nearly 1,900 people are on visas. Management declined to forecast.

qa_highlights.question: M&A update?
qa_highlights.answer: Scouting is active with strict criteria and several leads; no deal is at a closing stage, and the company will announce once a term sheet is signed.

543652|2026-09.headline: Fusion Finance Q2 FY27 net profit rose to INR86 crores and annualised ROA hit about 4%, while AUM growth guidance is being moderated.
543652|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 disbursements were INR1,726 crores, up 33% YoY but broadly flat QoQ, and AUM reached INR8,007 crores (+14% YoY) after floods disrupted July and August collections in five states. Gross NPA fell to 1.6% from 2.51% QoQ (2.28% including the INR54 crore ARC sale), and profit after tax reached INR86 crores versus a loss of INR22 crores a year earlier. Cost of borrowing fell for a fifth straight quarter, with marginal cost at 9.35%, and NII margin rose to 12.52%. Management said the INR10,000 crore AUM ambition will likely slip given the H1 disruption, while credit cost and ROA targets are unchanged.

segments.name: Core JLG microfinance
segments.commentary: Remains the majority of the business; average MFI AUM per branch rose to INR5.4 crores from INR5.1 crores, with about 102 branches being rationalised and 50 new branches planned.

segments.name: Premium JLG (income above INR3 lakhs)
segments.commentary: Vishwas product launched in Q2 accounted for about 20% of MFI disbursements in September and October; ticket size capped at INR1 lakh, and loans are reported as MFI JLG under bureau rules.

segments.name: Secured MSME
segments.commentary: About 10% of MSME disbursements now originate through MFI branches, with MFI branches acting as MSME spokes expanded from 50 to 100; MSME disbursements grew about 10% QoQ in October, with MSME ticket size cap raised to INR50 lakhs from INR25 lakhs.

segments.name: Maharashtra (about INR117 crore book)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency fell to 98.84% in October from 99.4%; net flow rate 0.57%, with the drought-affected sub-book of about INR26-27 crores at about 97.25% collection efficiency.

segments.name: Karnataka (about 1.25% of portfolio)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency 99.95% in October with negative net flow rate; management reports no stress in the market.

guidance_outlook: AUM ambition of INR10,000 crores is still a medium-term objective, but management said it may moderate and arrive later; no new year-end AUM number given.
Credit cost guided at 2% to 2.5% for the year: about 1.8% base (flows of about 15-16 bps per quarter) plus about 30 bps per quarter if a shock occurs.
Exit-quarter ROA target of 4% has already been achieved (annualised ~4% in Q2); medium-term ROA target is 4%+.
Management expects at least 15-20 bps NIM expansion next quarter and sustained margins thereafter; a further 12-15 bps per quarter of yield uplift is expected over the next two quarters.
Q3 disbursement momentum: October up about 10% over the prior-quarter monthly average (INR568-570 crores), across both MFI and MSME.
Medium-term AUM growth ambition of 20-25% per year, with a calibrated timeline for the INR10,000 crore target.
Management expects a possible 50-75 bps rise in marginal cost of borrowing over the next two quarters, which it says would have a muted impact; rate pass-through is 6-9 months away if needed.
Retention of repeat customers rose to 38-39% from 28-29%; target is 50% over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: MFI branch network: 950 branches now run on-ground credit assessment, up from about 200 branches.
Branch footprint: about 102 branches being rationalised and 50 new branches planned in markets with strong opportunity.

New LOS and LMS systems live in about 15% of branches, with broader transition targeted before financial year-end; AI capabilities in development for collections, customer service and credit assessment.
Recovery of 90+ DPD legacy portfolio brought in-house; recoveries exceeded INR30 crores in Q2, including INR21 crores from written-off accounts.
demand_pricing: Collection efficiency returned to 99.75% in Q2 with net flow rate below 0.10%; October gross collection efficiency 99.78% (September 99.77%).
Disbursements in October up about 10% over the prior quarter's monthly average of INR568-570 crores, with MFI and MSME each growing about 10%.
Yield rose about 24 bps QoQ from the rate hike taken at the start of FY27; cost of borrowing fell about 35 bps QoQ.
PTC raised INR320 crores at an all-in cost of about 8.5%, now about 10% of borrowings; management aims to raise the PTC share further.
CGSMFI2.0 scheme: accepted about INR468 crores of sanctions at about 9.23% all-in cost out of about INR1,100 crores available; the company declined sanctions with unfavourable terms.
Delinquent receivables on direct assignment fell to 12.65% of AUM from 13.75% QoQ; the company aims to reduce direct assignment reliance.

qa_highlights.question: What were October collection efficiency and disbursement numbers, including for Maharashtra and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross collection efficiency was 99.78% in October (September 99.77%). Maharashtra's INR117 crore book fell to 98.84% (from 99.4%) with a 0.57% net flow rate; Karnataka was at 99.95% with negative net flow.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company accelerate growth in H2 or wait for drought-affected areas to stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has moved almost all of Maharashtra and some bordering Karnataka branches to stricter guardrails with no new customers there, and is pressing growth elsewhere. Maharashtra is about 2% and Karnataka about 1.25% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress building in districts from rainfall deficit or drought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no carry-over of stress from September or October into the next month outside Maharashtra. The premium JLG product carries a 0.19% par in the third cycle and above over the past 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrower count falling and what is retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 4% of customers hold more than three lenders and will be exited. Repeat-loan retention rose from 28-29% to 38-39% since August, with a target of 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 credit cost guidance and how much H1 profit is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 2% to 2.5% for the year, with a base of about 1.8% and a further 30 bps per quarter if a shock occurs. Management said INR86.47 crores of profit is recurring with no exceptional items; net credit cost is about 1.2% annualised after recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise, and will rates be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 15-20 bps margin rise next quarter from yield and PTC-driven borrowing cost benefits, and sees a further 12-15 bps per quarter yield uplift. Any pass-through of rate increases is 6-9 months away and not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company give a year-end AUM number and a higher exit ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a new year-end AUM figure, citing many moving parts and a likely moderation of the INR10,000 crore target. It said the company enters November with no carry-over of stress and expects growth from individual loans, premium JLG and MSME.

risks_watch: Maharashtra drought: 60% of drought impact not yet seen per management; sub-book at 97.25% collection efficiency, with stricter guardrails and no new customers in the affected areas.
AUM growth: the INR10,000 crore target may slip; growth in the next 4-5 months depends on October's 10% momentum continuing.
Cost of funds: management expects 50-75 bps of rate increase over two quarters, and margin guidance depends on PTC share rising and the CGSMFI2.0 benefit.
Credit cost: 2-2.5% guidance includes a 30 bps per quarter shock allowance; the ARC sale of INR54 crores lifted Stage 3 coverage to 93.4%.
Premium JLG and MSME: higher-ticket products are a new risk; loans above INR3 lakhs income are non-qualified but reported as MFI JLG.
Tax: unrecognised DTA of INR271 crores as of September 30 could be used in future.

rows.why: Capex was not discussed; no utilisation figure was given to judge capacity needs.

Analysts pressed on drought

543653|2026-03.headline: Bikaji Q4 FY26 revenue grew close to 18% to about INR720 crores, with FY26 revenue of INR2,994 crores and 9.5% volume growth.
543653|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 top-line growth of close to 18%, with revenue from operations around INR720 crores, EBITDA about INR88 crores (roughly 12.2% margin) and PAT about INR56 crores. For FY26, revenue was about INR2,994 crores on 9.5% volume growth, with consolidated gross margin of 35.1% and EBITDA margin of 13.7%, up over 120 bps. Q4 EBITDA was pressured by a step-up in advertising linked to the Bhujia and Kya Baat Hai Ji campaigns, plus a Bengal-election labour exodus and a 2.5-day factory shutdown. Management took a price rise of about 3% in April 2026 to offset edible oil and packaging inflation.

financial_highlights.change: top line growth close to 18% YoY

financial_highlights.value: close to INR88 crores, about 12.2% margin
financial_highlights.change: H2 margin about 11% vs H1 about 13.5-14% per analyst calculation

financial_highlights.value: close to INR56 crores, PAT margin close to 8%

financial_highlights.change: down about 240 bps YoY, as PLI was included last year

from 2% last year; channel growth about 75-100%

segments.name: Ethnic snacks
segments.commentary: Q4 volume growth in line with overall volume growth of 16.1%; FY26 ethnic snacks growth stated at 11%. Bhujia (Bikaji brand) campaign drove strong H2 momentum.

segments.name: Western snacks
segments.commentary: Q4 growth about 8.5% YoY versus 25% in Q3; FY26 about 7%. Management targets 20%+ growth and lifting Western share of business from 8.5% to about 11% in 3 years.

segments.name: Sweets
segments.commentary: FY26 growth about 9% against a target of 11-12%; budgeted at about 12.5% for the year. A new Bikaner sweets factory is being built; capacity is constrained in festive months (about 80% of sweets sales fall in four months from Rakhi to Diwali).

segments.name: Family pack and impulse
segments.commentary: Family pack grew about 20% in Q4 and impulse about 14%. Family pack price was raised and impulse grammage cut.

segments.name: Packaged food and brand
segments.commentary: Bikaji brand revenue crossed INR100 crores in FY26, with a target of 50-60% growth annually for 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: core states growth about 13% plus or minus, focus states growth about 20%; management said 15% growth would not be sustainable.
Consolidated gross margin target is to maintain FY26 level (35.1%) in FY27; EBITDA expected to improve through fixed-cost leverage and CMU (co-manufacturing) output.
Advertising budget for FY27 held at about 2% of sales, same as last year.
Capex of close to INR100 crores planned in FY27, including a sweets factory in Bikaner.
THF plans to open 8-10 stores a year for 3 years and grow top line 50-55%; Bikaji retail to open 2 outlets in next 6 months.
Ariba (frozen) utilisation expected to rise to about 55-60% to make it EBITDA-neutral; export growth expected at 50-60%.
capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR100 crores planned this year, mainly a sweets factory in Bikaner; capacity added in FY26 was limited.
New warehouse adjacent to the plant: trials began about two weeks before the call, full operations from about 15 June 2026; storage rises from under 2 days of finished goods to 6-8 days.
Outlet reach reached 3.5 lakh direct outlets (about 1.2 lakh core, 1.7 lakh focus, 0.6 lakh other states); indirect reach about 8.2 lakh in core, 1.8 lakh in other states.
Production shift from Bikaner to co-manufacturing units (CMU) expected to add operational efficiency in FY27.
Sweets capacity at 100%+ utilisation in festive months but very low utilisation off-season.
demand_pricing: Price rise of about 3% taken in April 2026; management said it is enough to offset current raw material and packaging inflation and will decide on further hikes depending on the war.
Edible oil costs up about 12-14%; packaging material up about 25-30% at peak, then eased to INR220-225 from INR260-270 per unit cited.
Pulses and flour prices have not seen major increases.
Post-April demand momentum reported as continuing with no slowdown despite the price pass-through.

Bengal election-related migration of workers and a 2.5-day factory shutdown after the Chairman's death cost about 4-4.5 days of production in Q4 and Q1 to date; management said sales were partly lost but demand was not.
Delhi market underperforming; UP growing upwards of 20%, and UP's TAM equals the other five focus states combined.
Management expects regional and local brands to exit under GST rationalisation, with benefits to organised players over 2-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 EBITDA margin fall to about 11% from about 13.5-14% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to advertising, which was about 3.2-3.3% of sales in Q3/Q4 versus about 1% in H1, plus about 50 bps of one-time doubtful-debt provisions in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference between consolidated growth of 19% and standalone growth of 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is mainly THF retail, worth about 2.2 percentage points of growth, with Bikaji USA and Ariba also contributing; management confirmed there is no inorganic contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook and the price hike plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold consolidated gross margin at FY26 levels and says EBITDA will improve on fixed-cost leverage and CMU volumes; one price rise of about 3% was taken in April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sweets growth constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Sweets is capacity-constrained in festive months and under-utilised off-season; a new Bikaner factory and small all-season SKUs at INR5-10 are planned, with FY27 sweets budgeted at about 12.5% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlet split and the target for 5 lakh outlets?
qa_highlights.answer: Current direct reach is 3.5 lakh outlets; the next 1.5 lakh are expected mainly from focus states, with core states moving toward direct distribution rather than wholesalers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Western snacks slow in Q4 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Western snacks grew about 8.5% in Q4 after 25% in Q3; management attributed it to weaker family-pack traction and a soft category, and expects 20%+ growth going forward from a base of 1.1% national share.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: edible oil and packaging costs are volatile due to the war; further price increases may be needed to protect gross margin.
Advertising intensity: FY27 ad spend held at about 2%, but H2 margins were pressured by campaign spend, and campaigns must be refreshed each cycle.
Western snacks growth slowed to about 8.5% in Q4 and needs to recover to the 20%+ target.
Delhi underperformance and weaker focus-state execution; the 1.5x focus-market growth aspiration was not met in FY26.

543653|2026-09.headline: Bikaji Q2 FY27 top line grew close to 13% as Diwali shifted to Q3; management guides FY27 growth to about 17% and Q4 EBITDA to 13.5%.
543653|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew close to 13% in Q2 FY27, but the quarter was distorted by Diwali and sweets/gifting shifting into Q3 (October). Snacking carried the quarter, with value growth of about 22% and volume growth of about 15%, while total volume growth was about 5%. Gross margin was 34.4% in Q2, with standalone gross margin hit by about 1.7% from raw material inflation (pulses, edible oil, packaging, diesel), and consolidated EBITDA was about 12.6% in H1. Management says a roughly 3% MRP price increase takes effect from around 15 November, with full price impact in Q4, and expects Q3 to be margin-pressured and Q4 to normalise.

543654|2026-03.headline: Medanta FY26 total income rose 20% to INR 45,089 million and Q4 set a record, with Noida losses narrowing to INR 236 million in Q4.

Full-year PAT rose 15.1% to INR 5,541 million, while EBITDA including Noida was INR 10,560 million (24.2% margin). The newly inaugurated 550-bed Noida hospital ramped up, with its quarterly EBITDA loss narrowing from INR 320 million in Q3 to INR 236 million in Q4. Management guided to Noida breakeven in 2H FY27 and laid out a capex and bed-addition pipeline of roughly 2,700 beds over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Khetan (SMIFS): why are bromine realisations flat versus rising spot prices, and why is FY27 volume growth of 10-15% far below earlier FY26 guidance of 22,000-25,000 tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is driven by about 70% long-term contracts, so realisations lag spot; majority of contracts are now repriced upwards. On volume, it restated the 50-55 tons/day run-rate and a 15% higher FY27 target near 25,000 tons; the management team 'has expanded, not changed'.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Khetan: what drove the INR13 crore increase in inventory cost in COGS, and what is captive bromine consumption for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Unsold finished salt inventory built up in Q4 because deferred orders and logistics constraints prevented shipments; captive bromine consumption figure was not provided and will be emailed.

qa_highlights.question: Avnish Tiwari (Vaikarya): is the bromine supply gap still present and what are the spot versus long-term price levels; can management give EBITDA or breakeven guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply on trade routes still trails pre-conflict levels; spot has eased from RMB70,000-80,000 to about US$4-4.5/kg and short-term deal pricing tracks spot. Management declined forward EBITDA, revenue or breakeven guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj (360 ONE): bromine price range for next year, timeline to INR150 crore for Idealis, and salt pricing in USD vs INR?
qa_highlights.answer: No bromine price range given. Idealis: about 40-45% of the INR150 crore was expected from Mandvi bentonite, which awaits state approvals; the rest needs retooling; at least two of three plants expected at reasonable volume in H2 FY27. Salt pricing varies by geography: South Asia high-grade commands premiums, while China is more competitive.

capex_capacity: Bromine: management said production is back to historical daily rates of about 50-55 tons per day since mid-February; the 25,000-ton next milestone is about 15% above the current run-rate, with 40,000 tons as the longer-term anchor.

Idealis Mudchemie: three plants commissioned in the past 12 months; Gujarat (Mandvi) bentonite plant is production-ready but awaiting state approvals after NCLT-related interpretation issues; Nagri (Andhra Pradesh) plant being retooled for starch, PAC and Fibroseal products; at least two of three plants expected at reasonable volume in H2 FY27.
Acume Chemicals: capacity utilisation about 45% in Q4 during ramp-up; PBR 3 launched and zinc bromide volumes being scaled.
SOP: re-engineered product system and manufacturing process; plant trials expected in Q1 FY27 with higher production in H2 FY27.

SiCSem (Odisha semiconductor): fiscal support agreement signed with Government of India; substructure work targeted from July 2026, with roughly 27-30 months to completion per management's reconciliation.
demand_pricing: Industrial salt Q4 volume 1.1 million tons, down 7.2% YoY; about 120,000 tons deferred due to US-Iran conflict and about 250,000 tons of shipments not completed due to logistics issues.

Bromine Q4 volume about 3,731 tons, up 4% YoY and up 53% vs Q3 FY26; realisation up 14% YoY; management said majority of bromine long-term contracts have been renegotiated upwards, with no numbers given.

Logistics: Kutch road diversion roughly doubled effective distance; Q4 logistics cost increase of about INR200-220 per ton by March, with a Q4 weighted impact of about INR14-15 crore; global freight up 18-20%, industrial fuel up about 50%, coal, sulfur and propanol up 20-30%.

Acume (bromine derivatives) Q4 revenue INR23.8 crore on about 1,400 tons; FY26 revenue about INR81 crore on about 5,300 tons, up nearly 300%; Q4 sales up nearly 50% YoY; margins under pressure during ramp-up.
Idealis Mudchemie original INR150 crore revenue target now delayed; oil and gas demand muted due to Middle East conflict.
risks_watch: Kutch road works expected to run until early Q3 FY27; logistics cost and fleet turnaround remain elevated until then.

Salt pricing pressure in distant geographies such as China, with 10% YoY price decline in Q4 and rising competition from new capacity in Australia and the Middle East.
Idealis Mudchemie: Mandvi plant approvals pending with Gujarat authorities; original INR150 crore revenue target delayed with no new timeline.
Acume capacity utilisation about 45%; margin recovery depends on product ramp-up and bromine supply consistency from Hajipir.
Monitor Q1 FY27 SOP plant trials, H1 FY27 Idealis volumes, and the captive bromine consumption figure promised by email.

qa_highlights.question: Why was bromine volume 4,175 tons vs ~4,500 implied by 55 tpd run rate, and is the 20,000-ton FY27 target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 325 tons short: about 200 tons lost to grid power cuts (3-3.5 days) and about 150 tons to planned shutdowns; exit run rate of 20,000-25,000 tons still the target, with Q2 and Q3 the real test.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for bromine realisations over next 3-4 quarters given contract structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fairly confident of holding the weighted average blend; long-term contracts are 60-70% of volume, spot 30-35%, and some spot impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Salt shipments shortfall and whether demand or logistics is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand has not moved backwards; the shortfall reflects QVC deferrals and logistics issues including vessel slots and cut-offs; Kandla added as third port from Q2 to reduce blank sailings.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving if diesel and routes normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide numerically; said other expenses rose about INR40 crore YoY, ~60% from logistics (mainly distance) and ~40% from diesel, with normalisation expected to reflect from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why are derivative prices up only ~10% vs bromine ~25%, and status of Gujarat lease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the numbers quoted were not accurate, bromine is 40-50% of derivative cost so pass-through is fractional; lease closure expected in coming months, rents being paid and accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for zinc bromide and off-grid scale-up, and SiCSem timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-grid pilot needs several months to prove out; megawatt-plus plants in India not timed. SiCSem 24-27 months to commercial SOP from FSA; construction from late Aug/early Sep 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why has bromine volume been flat for five years versus capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited structural changes in brine feedstock needing recovery-system redesign, plus cyclonic rainfall in Kutch (average rainfall up to ~900 mm); 40,000-ton expansion timed to FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for oilfield chemicals and timing of volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian drilling demand is small and most demand is overseas; pack and starch (Nagri) volumes expected H2 FY27, bentonite and barite (Mandvi) by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Semicon capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Kumar said 15-20% of USD249 million already spent, 60-65% in FY27 and 40-45% in FY28.

543657|2026-09.headline: Archean Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 17.5% YoY to INR89.3 crore, but management withdrew SOP guidance and H1 EBITDA was flat.
543657|2026-09.overview: Standalone total income rose 32% YoY to INR305.4 crore and EBITDA rose 17.5% YoY to INR89.3 crore, with PAT of INR43.2 crore. Consolidated EBITDA for H1 fell 5.2% YoY to INR147.3 crore on a weak Q1. Bromine volumes and revenue grew strongly YoY, while industrial salt volumes fell 9% YoY and Acume posted a one-quarter EBITDA loss of about INR1 crore. Management cut the FY27 SOP volume outlook to 3,500-4,000 tons from 9,000-10,000 tons, and the Odisha semiconductor project (SiCSem) started civil works.

segments.name: Industrial salt
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR161 crore, up 9% YoY, with volumes down 9% YoY to about 812,000 tons because of customer deferrals tied to PVC and caustic soda. Management says H1 volume was about 1.8-1.9 million tons and it has high confidence in 4.2-4.3 million tons for FY27. Realisation was lifted by mix, and the cost per ton stayed flat QoQ.

segments.name: Bromine
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR127 crore, up 76% YoY. Volume was about 4,100 tons, up 29% YoY, and H1 volume was 8,300 tons, up 18% YoY. Realisation was up 36% YoY and stable QoQ. Unscheduled power cuts cost about 6-7% of output in the quarter.

segments.name: Acume (bromine derivatives)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR36 crore, up 81% YoY, with finished derivative volume of 2,115 tons, up 56% YoY. The quarter posted an EBITDA loss of about INR1 crore from adverse mix, one-time period costs and an inventory revaluation. H1 revenue was INR66 crore, up 51% YoY, and H1 was EBITDA positive. Capacity utilisation was about 40%.

segments.name: SOP (sulphate of potash)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume was 444 tons and value INR2.18 crore; H1 volume was about 2,400 tons. FY27 volume is now guided at 3,500-4,000 tons, versus the earlier 9,000-10,000 tons, because trials were delayed about a quarter and KTMS feedstock output was below plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bromine volume is expected at the lower end of the 18,000-20,000 ton guidance, with recovery of the 6-7% power-cut loss in H2.
FY27 salt volume is expected at 4.2-4.3 million tons, with an attempt to exceed 4.5 million tons. Management says the 4.5 million ton target has uncertainty.
Bromine average yield is expected to hold at about INR300/kg for the full year and at minimum each quarter.
SOP FY27 volume is cut to 3,500-4,000 tons. FY28 SOP throughput is expected to be significantly above this year, with pricing of USD 600-700/ton.
Management does not give earnings guidance. The Hajipir road re-routing (completed early October) is expected to mitigate most of the 15-30% increase in transport cost from Q3.
Bromine debottlenecking Phase 1 (25,000 tons run rate next year) is expected to finish in FY27. Flame retardant and the next bromine expansion are targeted for FY27-FY28 to FY28-FY29.

The Odisha semiconductor (SiCSem) project is about USD 240 million total, with a little under half funded by ISM. Management expects INR1,000-1,100 crore more investment, largely through debt, and 24 months of construction end to end.
Core chemical capex is to stay within the depreciation curve, with debt-to-equity of 0.6-0.7 (about 0.7 over three years).
capex_capacity: SiCSem project in Odisha: civil works started in Q2, environmental clearance received in mid-October, and first equipment consignments shipping. Construction is about 18-24 months; INR462.8 crore invested to date.

Brine field expansion: Phase 1 (4,000 hectares of an 8,000-hectare expansion, total 24,000 hectares) is in CWIP and expected to go live within about a quarter. Brine field expansion drives both salt and bromine volumes.
SOP plant modification is expected to be capitalised by end-FY27. Total CWIP is about INR120 crore, of which about INR80 crore is chemicals and about INR40 crore is SiCSem.
Bromine debottlenecking is on schedule, with some minor delays. Management expects completion in FY27.
Fleet: 100 new company-owned trailers were added in Q2 and a Kandla yard was commissioned. Electric trucks are at pilot stage, limited by charging downtime on about 300-400 km routes.
demand_pricing: Caustic soda and chlorine prices remain volatile. PVC demand is weak, with lower operating rates and deferrals from large salt customers; management expects a PVC price rebound this quarter.

Bromine exports are strong and pricing there is stable. Domestic bromine pricing is under pressure from agro and pharma slowdown and higher competitive intensity, which management says has not hit its own yields.

Industrial salt: about 80% of volume is on 18-24 month long-term contracts and about 10-20% is spot. Spot share has risen above 10% because of rescheduling. New export orders came from Vietnam and Oman.

Input inflation: industrial HSD rose from about INR87/litre in Q2 FY26 to about INR136 in Q2 FY27. Coal and propanol rose about 40% YoY, and sulphur more than doubled. Management expects cost pressure to continue through the rest of this year.
Oil and gas (oilfield specialty products at Oren Hydrocarbons): order traction is weak, with only campaign orders and no structured offtake. Management expects a ramp-up from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will bromine volume fall short of 18,000-20,000 tons, and will salt reach 4.5 million tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Bromine is expected at the lower end of guidance, with H2 recovery from power-cut losses of 6-7%. Salt is pegged at 4.2-4.3 million tons with an attempt to pass 4.5 million, and PVC-linked deferrals are the main uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Hajipir road completion lift H2 EBITDA, and is there a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transport costs rose 15-30% from the diversions and that most of this should be mitigated from Q3. Risks are fuel prices (Q2 averaged about INR130 per litre, with further upside), winter recovery issues, and bromine volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex and debt will SiCSem need, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD 240 million total, of which a little under half is ISM-funded. Another INR1,000-1,100 crore is needed, largely debt, front-loaded. Interim construction milestones will be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was SOP guidance cut and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 SOP volume was about 2,400 tons. FY27 is now 3,500-4,000 tons because of a one-quarter trial delay and feedstock (KTMS) shortfalls. FY28 pricing is expected at USD 600-700/ton.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q2 salt realisation high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to grade and geography mix, with more deferrals in lower-priced geographies. It said this was not a deliberate pricing change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Acume operating rate and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished production of 2,115 tons was about 40% of capacity. Management expects utilisation to rise over the next couple of quarters, though organic compound mix is weak.

risks_watch: Fuel and sulphur cost inflation, with management flagging that a further fuel increase could erode much of the logistics saving.
PVC-linked customer deferrals in salt, which could keep volumes below the 4.5 million ton target.
Power-cut downtime at bromine, and winter recovery issues.

SOP feedstock (KTMS) and trial execution; FY28 volume and pricing remain unconfirmed.
Funding and execution risk on the SiCSem project (INR1,000-1,100 crore of debt-led funding, instrument not finalised).

rows.why: Brine field expansion Phase 1 (4,000 of 8,000 hectares, total 24,000 ha) is in CWIP and expected live within about a quarter, bromine debottlenecking to 25,000 t/yr run rate is due in FY27, and the SOP plant modification is capitalised by end-FY27; SiCSem (USD 240 million, INR462.8 crore invested) runs 18-24 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Salt guided at 4.2-4.3 million t with a push past 4.5 million t, but PVC-linked deferrals cut Q2 volume 9% YoY to about 812,000 t; bromine at lower end of 18,000-20,000 t with H2 recovery of 6-7% power-cut loss; SOP cut to 3,500-4,000 t from 9,000-10,000 t.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it will look at investing another INR1,000-1,100 crore largely through debt for SiCSem, and utilisation is only about 40% at Acume, so the new capex is firm in intent while the instrument is not yet finalised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no earnings guidance and cut SOP volume by roughly 60% at the midpoint, with bromine only at the lower end and salt volume uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel rose to about INR130/litre in Q2 with more upside flagged, sulphur more than doubled, SOP FY27 already cut, and bromine power-cut losses of 6-7% of output could push volumes to the bottom of guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Flame retardant and the next bromine expansion are targeted for FY27-FY28 to FY28-FY29, but no firm dates are given and Offgrid commercialisation was deferred.

rows.label: SOP FY28 volume and pricing step-up
rows.why: Management expects FY28 SOP throughput well above FY27's 3,500-4,000 t at USD 600-700/ton, but trials and KTMS feedstock are unconfirmed and the FY28 volume question was deferred.

rows.label: Oil and gas ramp-up at Oren Hydrocarbons
rows.why: Order traction is weak with only campaign orders and no structured offtake, and management expects a ramp-up only from Q1 FY28.

rows.label: New salt export orders from Vietnam and Oman
rows.why: New export orders came in from Vietnam and Oman, and export share of revenue rose to 79% in Q2 from 75% a year earlier, though salt spot share above 10% limits pricing visibility.

tone.note: Management was confident on bromine exports, the Hajipir road logistics recovery and the brine expansion, but cautious on salt volumes, fuel and sulphur costs and SOP, where guidance was cut; analysts pressed on SOP, salt volume, SiCSem funding and capex, and management deferred several questions.

543663|2026-03.headline: Five-Star Q4 FY26: Q4 slippage fell to 0.7% from 1.9%, while FY27 AUM growth guided at ~20% and credit cost at 1.7-1.75%.
543663|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as the toughest year, with asset quality stress from MFI and unsecured overlap reaching the secured small-ticket LAP book. Q4 showed recovery: unique customer collection efficiency was 98.1%, x-bucket collections 99.3%, and slippage ratio fell to 0.7% from 1.9% in Q3. Disbursements rose 24% QoQ to INR1,213 crores and PAT was INR269 crores, down 3% QoQ on higher personnel expenses. Management guided to ~20% AUM growth in FY27 and a steady-state credit cost of 1.5-1.6% over FY28-30.

financial_highlights.change: management also cited 8.37% ROA on average AUM in the call
includes USD100mn ADB facility; USD50mn drawn

segments.name: South India (core)
segments.commentary: Around 85% or more of AUM is in the South, where over-leverage stress first appeared; management expects South to drive ~20% or more growth in FY27. Karnataka x-bucket collections were 99%.

segments.name: Non-South / new states
segments.commentary: Maharashtra operations started with branches in Nashik, Pune and Aurangabad, which lifted the Tier 1-2 share of AUM from ~1% to ~2%. Management plans to scale Maharashtra branches from ~40 to 70-80.

segments.name: Micro-LAP (INR3-5 lakh)
segments.commentary: Core product; management expects it to return to growth in a big way in FY27. Average ticket size rose from INR3.5 lakh to INR4.2 lakh YoY, and about 50%+ of AUM sits in INR3-5 lakh.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Introduced in some locations, targeting INR7-8 lakh tickets. Management says it is a secondary priority behind micro-LAP.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of around 20%, with a conservative range of 18-20%; management says close to 20% for the next two to three years.
FY27 disbursements of INR6,500-7,000 crores per the Q&A; another analyst's arithmetic used INR6,200-6,400 crores for 20% growth, which management said is achievable.
FY27 credit cost of 1.7-1.75% of average AUM; steady-state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30.
FY27 opex to average AUM of 7-7.25%, with limited scale benefit.
FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady-state ROA of 8-8.25%; spread around 13.5%.
Yield: about 30-40 bps further book-yield decline over the next 3-4 quarters; incremental lending at ~22.5%. Cost of funds: no major drop expected in FY27, with borrowing at ~8.5%.
Plan to open 60-75 branches in FY27, versus about 90-96 opened last year.
capex_capacity: Branch network: 60-75 new branches planned for FY27; 95% of branches opened last year have reached breakeven, per management.
Catchment area per branch of 25-30 km; new branches expected to break even in 9-12 months.
Business and collections teams separated and fully operational from April 1, 2026.
Write-offs for FY26 were about INR160-165 crores.
demand_pricing: April is seasonally weak; management says collections are in line with a typical April, and it expects no material deterioration.
Lead indicators are strong for disbursements; management expects Q1 FY27 disbursement growth.
Pricing was cut by 200 bps about 1.5 years ago; management sees no need to revise pricing in FY27 and expects no further cut.
Top-ups and repeat loans are 10-12% of disbursements. About 84% of Q4 collections were digital, up from 80% a year ago.
Management sees fintechs as a limited threat, given the INR4-5 lakh ticket size and roughly seven-year tenor against 6-12 months for fintech loans.
Exposure to small eateries and NRI remittance-linked borrowers is sub-1% of the portfolio, with no alarm signals so far.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost trajectory for FY27 and steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guided at 1.7-1.75% (Q4 was 1.88%); steady state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30, reflecting better buckets and a shift to slightly better-quality customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the steady-state credit cost higher than the earlier 0.8-1% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was on total assets (0.8-1%), roughly 1.3-1.35% on AUM. Management says it now expects to run at higher credit costs to avoid pressure on the field force while maintaining growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ROA outlook depend on margin given the steady-state credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady state of 8-8.25%. Leverage is currently low and will weigh on ROA but support ROE; spread is around 13.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 personal expense a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a combination of collections-vertical build-out and seasonal Q4 incentives. It said this is business as usual, not a one-off, and added that the April increment will also add cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth stay at ~20% beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for close to 20% for the next two to three years, with an 18-20% range. Growth is to be supported by pent-up demand and a low base; FY27 AUM is expected to reach about INR16,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How much yield is left to reprice on the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 30-40 bps more book-yield decline over 3-4 quarters. Incremental lending is at ~22.5%, book yield ~22-22.25%, and Q4 yield ~22.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost of funds and rating-upgrade expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding ADB, Q4 cost of funds was ~8.25-8.3%. Management expects FY27 borrowing at ~8.5% and no rating upgrade until the second half of the year, with about 30-40 bps more book-yield benefit over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Stage-2 provision coverage below the RBI 5% norm a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL framework for banks starts April 2027 and does not expect the 5% Stage-2 norm for NBFCs soon. It is being conservative on credit cost and may see benefit if DPDs improve.

risks_watch: Stage-2 coverage fell as the 61-90 DPD bucket dropped from 5.1% to 4.8%; management tracks overall coverage instead.
Geopolitical stress (West Asia conflict) and liquidity in the borrowing market; management expects no major cost-of-funds benefit in FY27.
Disbursement ramp needs to rise from INR1,213 crores in Q4 to INR1,400-1,500 crores per quarter; April borrowing was zero given strong liquidity.
Senior management exit during FY26; management says there is no impact on performance.
Opex to AUM is guided at 7-7.25%, above historical levels, with competition for talent.
Rating upgrade is not expected until the second half of FY27 at the earliest.

543663|2026-06.headline: Five-Star Q1 FY27 disbursements hit a record INR 1,496 crore (+23% QoQ, +16% YoY) while AUM grew 4% QoQ to INR 13,722 crore.
543663|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly disbursement of INR 1,496 crore and AUM of INR 13,722 crore, up 4% QoQ. Asset quality metrics improved modestly: 1+ current book rose to 83.30%, 30+ fell to 12.38%, and the 1.85% credit cost was slightly lower QoQ, while slippages were flat at 0.70%. Management guided to lower credit costs and NPLs in coming quarters, with opex staying flat in FY27 on an employee-cost reset. Q&A focused on yield compression, cost of borrowing, write-off run-rate, opex, and the timeline to higher leverage.

financial_highlights.change: Average cost of funds down ~15 bps, spread up 3 bps
Recoveries ~INR 35 crore incl. write-off and NPA settlements (vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4)

segments.name: Micro LAP (core product)
segments.commentary: Onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); management sees yield settling near 22.25% after 10-15 bps further compression over next couple of quarters. Average ticket size ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, targeting 25/50/25 mix across ~INR 3 lakh, ~INR 5 lakh and ~INR 10 lakh tickets.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Launched about two quarters ago; management said focus has been on restoring micro LAP before pushing housing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of ~20% reiterated; management expects FY27 disbursements of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%).
FY27 credit cost guided at 1.7%-1.9%; management said the trend is more likely toward 1.7%. Overall ECL coverage to be maintained at ~1.75%-1.8%.
Gross NPA to fall to sub-3% and a steady-state NPA of ~2.5%; steady-state Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%.
Write-offs for FY27 guided at INR 225-250 crore (~INR 55-60 crore per quarter).
Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% in FY27, moving to 5.25%-5.5% from FY28. Branch additions run-rate ~50-60 per year.
Incremental cost of borrowing guided at ~8.5%; spreads expected flat for next few quarters absent policy action. Repo rate increases are a downside risk.
FY28 credit cost expected at ~1.6%-1.7%. Debt-to-equity of 2x expected in 6-8 quarters; ROA steady state 6%-6.5% and ROE 18%-20% at ~3x leverage.
Management plans to launch one more product (beyond micro LAP and housing) within ~3-6 months, with details to be shared later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at ~856 after adding ~12 in Q1, mainly in Maharashtra and newer states; FY27 additions expected at ~50-60 branches.
Collections and business functions separated into different verticals; management says this lifted productivity without any change in credit filters.
Liquidity: ~INR 1,850 crore held on balance sheet at quarter end; ~INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and ~INR 450 crore raised in Q1.
Pending ADB tranche (ECB) to be raised, with hedging cost impact; timing to be managed.
demand_pricing: Management says demand was never the constraint; the slowdown over the past 3-4 quarters came from tighter approvals and deliberate disbursement pacing.
June disbursements were ~INR 670 crore; management expects a new normal of ~INR 600-650 crore per month on average, with intra-quarter seasonality being reduced.
Repeat-customer policy relaxed: top-up offered to best customers instead of requiring full prepayment, which management expects to reduce the repayment rate from ~30% toward 27-28%.
Microfinance overlap with Five-Star customers fell from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (per management, not measured for Q1).
Competition: management cited new competitors entering, requiring more competitive employee compensation.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI): Where will cost-to-assets settle and when does operating leverage kick in?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth due to competitive employee pay; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% this year, moving to 5.25%-5.5% in steady state from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: Has yield repricing largely finished, and what is the current lending rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Large part of contraction done; onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); a further 10-15 bps compression expected over next couple of quarters, settling near 22.25% after NPA interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah (IIFL): Further Stage 3 flow-through expected, any ARC sales, and rollback rates in early buckets?
qa_highlights.answer: No ARC sales. Slippages expected to trend down; recoveries ~INR 35 crore vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4. Rollbacks ~4-5% in 1-60 DPD buckets and ~2-3% in 61-90 DPD; management frames it as stabilisation, with unique customer collection efficiency key.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): How many more quarters until slippages decline and what is a normalised slippage rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in September, December and March quarters; credit cost trending toward 1.7%. Will wait 1-2 quarters of slippage trend before giving a steady-state slippage number.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What drives the disbursement acceleration (demand, approvals, productivity, geography)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand was never the constraint; earlier slowdown reflected tighter approvals and deliberate pacing. Vertical split of business and collections lifted productivity with no change in credit filters; login and sanction traction strong.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What is the outlook for cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing ~8.5%, leaving room for 20-30 bps further compression on the book; pending ADB ECB tranche carries hedging cost; assumes no repo hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Chandrasekhar Sridhar (Fidelity): Is gold loan growth masking underlying stress via repayments by overlapping customers? Also ticket size and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says gold loans are fully secured and repayments via gold loans are seasonal; microfinance overlap down from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (not measured for Q1). Ticket size mix target 25/50/25 across ~INR 3 lakh, 5 lakh, 10 lakh; one more product within 3-6 months. Spreads to stay flat for next few quarters absent policy action.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Why have repayment rates risen, and how does that reconcile with a rising 3-5 year duration share?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose on stronger collections and a policy change: top-up offered to best customers instead of full prepayment. Repayment rate currently ~30%, expected to trend to 27-28%; behavioural tenor ~4-4.5 years. Management said 85-90% of loans are disbursed on 7-year tenure; the vintage shift reflects seasoning and higher disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Rajiv Mehta (Yes Securities): Trajectory of write-offs, coverage build-back, and FY28 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 write-offs guided INR 225-250 crore, roughly flat at ~INR 55-60 crore per quarter; steady-state write-off view in 2-3 quarters. Overall ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%, whichever mix of Stage 1/2/3. FY28 credit cost ~1.6-1.7%. Growth achieved with no change in credit filters.

qa_highlights.question: Kunal Shah (Citi): Steady-state bucket mix and employee cost drivers, attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state: Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%, Stage 3 ~2.5%; current book to reach ~85% by end FY27 from 83.3%; 30+ below 12%. Employee cost rise is salary realignment and incentives for branch staff, not ESOPs. Attrition flat so far; trends in 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Expense growth this year and whether 20% loan growth guidance stands?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth ~20-21% YoY, similar to Q1; increments and appraisals already in Q1 base. ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%; write-offs INR 55-60 crore per quarter; 20% AUM growth guidance reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Divyansh Gupta (Latent PMS): Why did debt decline from March, cost of funds for levering up, and timing of D/E of 2x?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 borrowing was muted as banks awaited results; INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and INR 450 crore in Q1; INR 1,850 crore liquidity held. Guide 8.5% incremental cost. D/E of 2x in 6-8 quarters, as net worth adds ~INR 1,100-1,200 crore PAT annually.

qa_highlights.question: Chirag Fialoke (MS Capital): Are incremental disbursements averaging INR 5-7 lakh, and what is the 60-90 DPD bucket?
qa_highlights.answer: Average ticket ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, expected to hold around INR 5 lakh; mix guidance unchanged. Management deferred the 60-90 DPD figure to the IR team.

qa_highlights.question: Darshan Deora (Indvest): Steady-state ROE target, and will yields be raised back given higher collection costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROA ~8-8.5% on AUM (7-7.25% on total assets); steady-state ROA 6-6.5% and ROE 18-20% at ~3x leverage. Management says the cost increase will be recovered through lower credit cost, not higher lending rates; the 200 bps cut in Oct 2024 tracked borrowing costs falling from 11%+.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: What was June disbursement and is INR 600-650 crore a monthly run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: June disbursements ~INR 670 crore; management is working to reduce intra-quarter seasonality and agreed an average of ~INR 600-650 crore per month is a fair assumption for the rest of the year.

risks_watch: Yield compression: onboarding yields ~22.5% with a further 10-15 bps decline expected over the next couple of quarters, and NPA interest reversals weigh on yields.

Cost of borrowing: guidance of ~8.5% incremental assumes no repo hikes; a rate increase or ADB ECB hedging costs would hit spreads. Management flagged energy costs and possible regulatory liquidity moves.

Asset quality: slippages flat QoQ at 0.70%; credit cost guidance 1.7-1.9% and gross NPA sub-3% depend on slippages turning down in September, December and March quarters. Write-off run-rate ~INR 60 crore per quarter gives little relief in FY27.
Opex and employee cost: opex growth 20-21% YoY and cost-to-assets ~5.75-6% in FY27; attrition is flat and too early to call, with more competitors entering.
Disbursement sustainability: H1 run-rate of ~INR 600-650 crore per month and reliance on a new product within 3-6 months; leverage target of 2x D/E is 6-8 quarters away.

So our request is, can you please keep yourself mute so that the background noise is too much.
So it's not like we are completely removing the DNA of collections from the business people.

543667|2026-03.headline: Inox Green Q4 FY26 total income INR120 crore (+40% YoY), EBITDA INR57 crore (+93%), with INR40 crore of acquisition-linked other income flattering profit.
543667|2026-03.overview: Inox Green reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR120 crore, EBITDA of INR57 crore, PBT of INR46 crore and PAT of INR28 crore, with machine availability near 96.5%. Management said roughly INR40 crore of quarterly other income relates to the two pending O&M acquisitions (debt-linked income), with INR10 crore each from value-added services and treasury. Parent Inox Wind reported Q4 revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY) and PAT of INR106 crore, and FY26 revenue of about INR4,500–4,600 crore against a revised INR5,000 crore target. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% and Inox Green EBITDA of above INR600 crore, while the evacuation-infrastructure demerger has been approved by NCLT Ahmedabad.

EBITDA margin for Inox Wind guided at north of about 20%.

Inox Wind's 3.1 GW order book supports more than 24 months of execution visibility; most EPC jobs expected to be complete by H1 FY27 except one leading job.
