PSU contracts saw payment delays; management said the PSU project issue is now resolved.
Working capital: management said net working capital days target of about 200 was missed; supply disruption for a key imported component (ECS) by ship and commodity price rises were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin do the acquired O&M assets carry, and what is the FY27 Inox Green guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions have about 50% EBITDA margin as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems; FY27 Inox Green EBITDA guidance is above INR600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR600 crore FY27 EBITDA reached given acquisition timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Devansh Jain said entity one's order is due in about two weeks and entity two's within 60–90 days; revenues and profits from 1 April 2026 will be reflected in consolidated results. Management added about 1.5 GW of organic addition for Inox Wind plus value-added services.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 other income about INR61 crore, and how much is core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions' debt, INR10 crore to value-added services and INR10 crore to treasury; PAT impact about INR25–26 crore. Devansh Jain said ex-acquisition income the margin would be about 45%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall from INR78–82 crore in Q3 to INR69 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarter-on-quarter move to value-added service lumpiness of about INR8–9 crore and asked investors to look at the annualised run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Inox Wind moving from turnkey to equipment supply, and what happens to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Agarwal said turnkey caused the largest working capital blockage; order book moved from 100% turnkey to about 50:50, targeting 75–80% equipment supply. Management said margins stay above about 20% and equipment supply is more predictable.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 megawatt execution and status of working capital days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY26 megawatt execution, reiterating revenue-based guidance; it reported INR4,600 crore against a INR5,000 crore target and said INR400 crore would be made up in Q1–Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and use of INR600 crore cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Devansh Jain said the Board will set a dividend policy after consolidation; the INR600 crore is expected to be operating cash flow with no depreciation or finance cost and a tax shield up to INR700 crore; acquisitions may use 10–20% of free cash flow.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: Inox Wind working capital and receivables (PSU delays) are behind the INR400 crore shortfall versus target; watch Q1 FY27 collections.
Quality of Inox Green earnings: about INR40 crore of Q4 other income is acquisition-linked; ex-that, margin is about 45% on annual basis.
Acquisition closure timing and NCLT/administrative approvals for the two O&M entities and the demerger.
Execution risk from geopolitical supply disruption (ECS imports by ship, commodity prices) and the one remaining major EPC job.
Governance and minority-shareholder concerns raised on value destruction, megawatt-to-revenue guidance changes and refusal to disclose FY26 MW execution.

543667|2026-06.headline: INOX Green Q1 FY27 PAT rose 86% YoY to INR41 crore; Wind World India acquisition completion expected in Q2 FY27.
543667|2026-06.overview: INOX Green reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR101 crore (+17% YoY), EBITDA of INR57 crore (+19%), PBT of INR54 crore (+74%) and PAT of INR41 crore (+86%). Management said the power evacuation business was demerged into INOX Renewable Solutions effective August 1, 2026 (record date), leaving INOX Green as an asset-light O&M player. NCLT Ahmedabad approved the Wind World India acquisition, with completion expected in Q2 FY27. Management reiterated full-year guidance but declined to quantify quarterly trajectory, and the call was largely about the parent's (INOX Wind) revenue and receivables questions.

segments.name: INOX Green (O&M)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of approximately 13.3 GW peak as of June 2026: about 10.5 GW wind operating assets plus solar; revenue-generating base of about 4 GW own turbines, with about 6.5 GW acquired (Wind World India and one other) still classified as investments. Blended revenue of INR9-10 lakh per MW excluding GST on the about 4 GW base.

segments.name: Wind World India (acquisition pending)
segments.commentary: O&M portfolio of about 4.5 GW; FY26 revenue about INR580 crore with contracted annual price escalation of about 5%. Completion expected in Q2 FY27, after which line-by-line consolidation follows.

segments.name: INOX Wind (group parent, equipment/EPC)
segments.commentary: Equipment supply share of third-party order book about 59% (41% turnkey) as of July 2026; order book about 4.4 GW. Q1 revenue flat YoY per management.

segments.name: INOX Renewable Solutions (demerged EPC/power evacuation)
segments.commentary: Power evacuation infrastructure business demerged from INOX Green effective August 1, 2026; listing expected in about 2-3 months, subject to regulatory approvals.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% YoY maintained (INOX Wind, per management).
Full-year FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin of 20% to 22% maintained; H2 expected to carry about 70-75% of annual business.
INOX Green EBITDA guidance of INR600 crore on an annualised basis from Q3/Q4 FY27 post consolidation; management clarified it is an annual, not quarterly, figure.
INOX Green wind O&M EBITDA margin guidance of about 50% on the existing portfolio, excluding treasury income; management said one-off costs and life-extension spend cause quarterly variation.
Working capital guidance maintained on an annualised basis; receivable days expected to fall over the next 3-4 quarters.
4X wind turbine: prototype installation in August 2026, commercial launch about a month later; ALMM-driven indigenisation targeted near 100% by calendar year-end.
Wind World India acquisition formalities expected in Q2 FY27; other investments expected to be completed and consolidated in FY27.
capex_capacity: INOX Wind signed a 1.5 GW MOU with INOX Clean in June 2026; firm orders for 500 MW signed so far, balance 1 GW pending.
INOX Wind received a 200 MW LOA from NLC India in Q1 FY27 (repeat order); order book about 4.4 GW as of July 2026, visibility 24-36 months.

Expansion at INOX Renewable Solutions: transformer capacity to 4.9 MVA for 4X series, plans for 8-20 MVA and 100 MVA+ transformers, 4 cranes in operation with more this fiscal, unit substation (USS) commercial launch in FY27.
demand_pricing: Wind industry added 1.4 GW in India in Q1 FY27; cumulative installed wind capacity 57.4 GW; management expects 8-10 GW annual additions over the next few years.
Of 9.34 GW renewable capacity awarded through tenders in Q1, 2.35 GW (25%) was standalone wind.
Blended O&M realisation INR9-10 lakh per MW on the about 4 GW own base; acquired portfolios expected to be substantially higher per management.
INOX Clean plans 3 GW+ annual IPP capacity; management expects roughly 25-30% of that to flow to INOX Wind and the O&M portion to INOX Green.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise funds for the Wind World acquisition when prior preferential issue funded it, and why not debt against cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these were enabling resolutions and declined further comment citing the silent period.

qa_highlights.question: Is INOX Clean business on the same terms as third-party business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inter-entity contracts are arm's length, INOX Clean is treated as a customer, and there is no preferential pricing for any customer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INOX Green portfolio's revenue per MW and how much of the acquired portfolio is consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended INR9-10 lakh per MW excluding GST on about 4 GW own turbines; the two acquired portfolios (about 6.5 GW) remain investments and are not consolidated until shares are acquired.

qa_highlights.question: Why is legacy O&M EBITDA well below the 50% guided margin, and what about the deferred INR400 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to one-off, infrastructure and life-extension costs, plus value-added services previously not billed separately, which will be billed from this year. On the deferred revenue, management said part was recognised in Q1 and the rest would be covered over FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR600 crore EBITDA guidance for FY27 and does it start from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR600 crore is an annual figure on an annualised basis from Q3/Q4 post consolidation, not a quarterly target, and gave no FY28 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75% FY27 revenue growth guidance still achievable given flat Q1 at INOX Wind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 75% growth target, citing H2-weighting (70-75% of business) and a shift to equipment supply that it expects to show results from Q2-end and predominantly in Q3.

543669|2026-03.headline: Keystone Realtors FY26 presales rose 33% to INR4,022 crore, with FY27 presales guided at INR5,000 crore and a INR10,000 crore presales target by FY30.
543669|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 presales of INR1,346 crore (up 58% YoY) and full-year presales of INR4,022 crore (up 33%), about 1.74x its BD guidance. Revenue from operations was INR1,596 crore in Q4 and INR2,635 crore for FY26, with OCF of about INR715 crore. The company transitioned from completion method to percentage-of-completion accounting from 1 April 2025, and management says legacy low-margin projects are largely behind it. Gross debt was INR755 crore at March 2026 (gross D/E 0.26:1), and CRISIL assigned AA- with stable outlook.

segments.name: Residential sales and launches
segments.commentary: Seven projects launched in FY26 with GDV of INR9,813 crore (1.4x INR7,000 crore guidance); two launched in Q4 with GDV INR3,978 crore. Of FY26 presales, INR1,620 crore came from new launches and INR2,400 crore from the opening pipeline.

segments.name: Business development
segments.commentary: Five projects added in FY26 with GDV of INR10,400 crore (1.74x INR6,000 crore guidance). Since FY23, 25 projects worth over INR27,800 crore added, 21 of them redevelopment; each underwritten at about 35% gross margin with equity capped near 10% of GDV.

segments.name: Legacy projects (Crown, Virar affordable)
segments.commentary: Legacy projects were 62% of FY26 revenue and are guided to 12% in FY27. Crown has about INR180 crore inventory and about INR450 crore sold receivables, with exit expected by December 2026.

segments.name: Commercial annuity
segments.commentary: Target of about INR100 crore recurring rental income by 2030. Current assets are 33Fifteen (strata sales underway), a 2 million sq ft Thane project (phases of 4.5 lakh sq ft, expected next FY), and Dhuruwadi in Prabhadevi.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance INR5,000 crore (about 25% growth); FY27 project launches about INR8,000 crore; acquisitions about INR8,000-plus crore.
Target of INR10,000 crore presales by FY30, requiring about 26% CAGR from FY27.
FY27 OCF expected a little over INR1,000 crore (FY26: about INR700-715 crore).
Gross debt-to-equity to be capped at 0.75:1. Peak gross debt guided at INR1,300-1,400 crore in FY27 (excluding commercial); FY28 peak to be discussed later.
FY27 finance cost estimated at about INR95 crore (average debt about INR1,000 crore at 9.5%).
Revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion: about 40% completion method, 60% POCM in FY27; 100% POCM from FY28. Revenue acceleration expected from FY28.
Collection efficiency expected at 75-80% from this year onwards.
Blended gross margin of about 35% and EBITDA of about 20% on current projects; affordable/mid-size tends toward 30% gross margin and luxury toward 40%.
capex_capacity: Construction spend rose to INR997 crore in FY26 from INR829 crore in FY25.
Precast construction plant under way for captive use, technical support from Robin Village (Singapore); claimed benefits include about 30% lower material wastage and 40% lower workforce need.
Labour accommodation for about 500-plus workers under development at Rustomjee Balmoral, Chembur.
Cluster redevelopment projects: Seasons (about 168 members) and Elements, Andheri (about 480 members); GTB project is 11.5 acres, which may be developed in two phases.
Construction finance lines are in place; management says it has not needed to draw the full contracted amount in the past two years.
demand_pricing: Sales pattern: about 35% sold by plinth (first year), about 75% by sustenance stage, 15-20% during fit-out, 5-10% post OC. 66% of FY24 launches and 49% of FY25 launches already sold as of March 2026; 17% of FY26 launches sold in-year.
Unsold inventory about INR12,000 crore, of which about INR8,000 crore from FY25 launches; about 49% of total inventory sold.
Input costs up about 8-13% in certain items, roughly 5% overall; management says the 35%/40% sales pattern lets it reprice unsold stock.
Demand: no slowdown seen in premium and luxury; INR1-3 crore segment needs more push. Buying decisions taking longer.
Pipeline mix: about 94% of forthcoming pipeline in emerging premium to super premium. Large share of BD in INR1-3 crore and INR1-4 crore segments; affordable not targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sold receivables low versus cost to complete on the residential book (Slide 30)?
qa_highlights.answer: Sajal Gupta said about INR8,000 crore of the INR12,000 crore unsold inventory comes from FY25 launches; 49% of total inventory is sold and sales follow a 35/40/15-20/5-10 pattern that funds cost to complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial annuity income target and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Boman Irani targets about INR100 crore by 2030, recovering costs via pre-leasing and sales to larger funds or HNIs while retaining some assets; commercial projects are about 60-65% sold to recover development cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash outflow for cluster versus single redevelopment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity investment stays about 10-11% of project GDV for cluster projects, with phased investment possible on very large sites like GTB.

qa_highlights.question: When do legacy projects end and what margin profile follows?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy projects are 62% of FY26 revenue and 12% in FY27; FY28 onward is expected at about 35% blended gross margin and 20% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is collection efficiency declining and what is the expected range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the lower ratio to a higher share of newly launched projects in presales; collection efficiency is expected at 75-80% from this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 peak debt and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is expected to peak at INR1,300-1,400 crore in FY27 (excluding commercial), with average debt of about INR1,000 crore and finance cost of about INR95 crore at 9.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East crisis and cost inflation affecting demand and input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No slowdown in premium segment; INR1-3 crore segment needs more push. Input costs up about 5% overall, with supply shortages of imported materials creating delays.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition shift to POCM: FY27 mix is 60% POCM, so reported profit and cash flow may not track presales smoothly.
Collection efficiency guided lower at 75-80%, and sales pace in the INR1-3 crore segment needs more push.
Rising input costs (about 5% overall, 8-13% in some items) and import shortages could cause delays.

Target of INR10,000 crore presales by FY30 requires about 26% CAGR; ROE/ROCE guidance not yet provided.
Bandstand Cama (27 apartments, about 30% sold) and the super-luxury redevelopment deal (to be announced around Q3 FY27) are pending updates.

543686|2026-03.headline: Sirca Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin reached 20.08%, with management guiding 25-30% growth and 19-21% EBITDA margin for FY27.
543686|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore, EBITDA rose 35.69% to INR25.74 crore (margin 19.17% vs 18.8%), and PAT rose 25.07% to INR17.71 crore. Management flagged short-term raw material margin pressure from crude-linked inputs, offset by two price increases totalling about 10% on Sirca range, and a March NC raw material shortage that cost Wembley about INR4-5 crore of revenue. The company has shifted from pure trading to manufacturing, with about 95% of previously imported products now targeted for Indian production.

segments.name: Core Sirca wood coatings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of about INR372 crore, of which about INR124 crore came from Italy-imported products and about INR252 crore from products made in India. Sirca gross margins are higher than Wembley/Welcome by about 10-15 percentage points.

segments.commentary: Combined FY26 revenue of about INR120.5 crore: Welcome about INR46.5 crore and Wembley about INR74 crore. Wembley was roughly flat YoY after INR4-5 crore of orders were lost in March to an NC raw material shortage, and about INR5-6 crore was billed to distributors before the acquisition closed.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY25 exports were about INR9 crore, mainly Nepal plus one or two Sri Lanka customers. Wembley Valentino polyurethane exports are expected to start in Q1 FY27, with management targeting exports of about 3-4% of revenue.

segments.name: Acrylic coatings (Sirca brand)
segments.commentary: Acrylic sales contributed about INR120 crore in FY26 per management. Made-in-India production is expected to roll out in Q1 FY27 after the December 2025 know-how transfer from Sirca Italy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% CAGR, described as a minimum.
EBITDA margin guided to stay in the 19-21% range, with raw material pressure expected to be temporary after two price increases.
Management said the INR1,000 crore revenue vision is achievable in about three years (FY29) and that Sirca and Wembley capacities are broadly sufficient for that journey.
FY27 capex limited to about INR5-6 crore, mainly for acrylic production expansion.
Expects inventory to fall by about INR15-20 crore and debtors to decline in the coming quarters as import stock is consumed by June end.
Expects NC supply constraints from supplier Nitrex to ease from June with a new Nitrex unit starting operations.
Expects exports to Middle East including Dubai to begin in FY27, and export contribution of about 3-4% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Sirca core facility capacity raised by 1,750 tons per annum to about 17,750 tons; about 12,000 tons utilised in FY26, with full utilisation expected by year-end in single shift at Unit 1.

Wembley capacity consolidated from four old distributor units into one new integrated facility with about 3x earlier capacity; management expects a turnover of INR250-300 crore from this setup using nitrocellulose and polyurethane products.
Wembley manufacturing facility is fully operational, consolidating multiple production lines.
Formula transfers for acrylic and polyester systems are complete; commercial trials underway with production expected in Q1 FY27. UV technology transfer is on track for Q1.
FY27 capex of about INR5-6 crore planned for acrylic production; most FY26 capex went to consolidating Wembley and Welcome sites.
demand_pricing: Two price increases of about 5% each (April and May 2026) on the Sirca range, totalling about 10%; Wembley and Welcome prices raised by about INR35 per litre. Management said this is enough to offset RM inflation so far.
Polyurethane is replacing melamine; melamine is about INR230-240 per litre vs PU about INR450-460 per litre, with PU about 10% higher per square foot on coverage.

Premium segment competition from large players is seen as limited because specification is driven by architects and designers; mass segment competition is more intense and is addressed through retailer margins and exclusivity.
About 80% of revenue comes from North India (Delhi NCR, Punjab, Haryana, UP, UK, Rajasthan, MP) and about 20% from West and South; 5 of 20 depots opened last year in South and West.
Management said the Indian furniture industry is shifting to local manufacturing after BIS implementation, which supports OEM and institutional demand.

543829|2026-09.headline: Global Surfaces Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.7% YoY to Rs 60 crore, EBITDA margin 2.17% on cost pressures; PAT loss Rs 5.4 crore.
543829|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 60 crore, up 10.7% YoY but up only 8.4% sequentially per the call's wording (the transcript says "lower than 8.4%", which is ambiguous). EBITDA was Rs 1.3 crore (margin 2.17%) versus a Rs 3.6 crore loss a year ago and a 12.69% margin in Q1, as raw material costs rose 25-50% and imported-raw-material freight rose nearly fivefold. Loss after tax was Rs 5.4 crore against Rs 4.6 crore a year ago and near breakeven in Q1. H1 EBITDA doubled to Rs 9.6 crore with margin up 424 bps to 7.66%, but other income fell to Rs 1.8 crore from Rs 9.4 crore, leaving H1 loss after tax at Rs 5.3 crore.

543874|2026-03.headline: Maiden Forgings H2 FY26 revenue rose 17.46% YoY to INR122.60 crore, with net profit up 46.37% to INR2.93 crore.
543874|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 production of 35,546 metric tons and FY26 revenue of INR233.96 crore, EBITDA of INR17.22 crore and net profit of INR5.02 crore. H2 EBITDA grew only 3.52% YoY to INR10.49 crore, and management attributed the margin improvement in the last three months mainly to a shift toward pneumatic nails, stainless steel bars and alloy steel bars. A new 4-acre integrated facility at Modinagar is being commissioned, with unit shifting already under way, and two new product lines (GI wires and stainless steel machine components) are expected to start around September-October 2026. Management guided to EBITDA margin improvement of at least 1-2% within FY27 but gave few hard numbers, and deferred several questions (realisation, other income, order pipeline, product-mix split) to later email or disclosure.

Raw material costs expected to rise in FY27, which management expects to be passed through to customers; management expects volumes to be maintained.

Capex and growth in FY26 were funded entirely from internal accruals; no equity or institutional borrowing was raised.
Land acquired for expansion over the next five years, per management.
Overseas warehousing: a 100% owned UAE subsidiary was planned for Dubai; groundwork began February 2026 and was postponed due to the geopolitical conflict.
demand_pricing: Management said export order book is the highest in company history, and reoccurring orders are strong despite geopolitical volatility.

Volumes ran at about 3,000 tons per month until September 2025 and about 3,500-3,600 tons per month from November 2025; about 7,000 tons was reported for April-May 2026, with management saying the run rate was maintained.

Management said margin protection relies on back-to-back procurement against customer POs, with inventory held around a plus or minus 5% band; stainless steel carries longer-term, higher-value inventory.
Management said the steel market was falling until November 2025 (compressing margins) and has been two-way since December 2025.
Management is confident that raw material supply is secure via at least 5 vendors with about 10 years of relationships; management also said it expects no volume loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term EBITDA margin aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a 1-2 percentage point improvement in EBITDA margin within FY27 from current levels, and said H2 FY27 would see a further increase.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 20% of growth would come from the new products' volumes (9,000-10,000 tons), with most new sales coming from product mix; volumes grow 5-10% per year.

543904|2026-03.headline: Mankind Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to INR3,443 crores with adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.1%; FY27 guided to double-digit growth.
543904|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.8% YoY to INR3,443 crores, led by 13.4% domestic growth, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 400 bps to 27.1% on better gross margin, operating leverage and a lower Q4 base. Full-year FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR14,278 crores, but PAT fell 3.4% to INR1,938 crores as finance cost, depreciation and lower other income weighed. Management said acute therapies were muted during FY26 but recovered sequentially from Q2, and chronic share rose to about 39-40%. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of at least double digits and adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.5-26.5%, with an effective tax rate stepping up to 25-26%.

segments.name: Domestic formulations (ex-Consumer Healthcare)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 12.9% per management's first remark (13.4% on domestic revenue of INR2,886 crores), with organic ex-OTC growth of 10.1%, the highest since the BSV acquisition. FY26 domestic revenue INR12,217 crores, +14.4%.

segments.name: Chronic therapies
segments.commentary: Chronic share about 40% in Q4 (+120 bps YoY) and about 39% for FY26 (+190 bps). Outperformed IPM 1.1x in cardiac and 1.6x in anti-diabetes ex-GLP-1 in FY26, but Q4 was 0.9x IPM per analyst's question, which management did not dispute.

segments.name: Acute therapies
segments.commentary: Gastro outperformed IPM at 1.1x (Pantakind 1.4x); gynaecology +10.8% with Dydrogesterone +20%; vitamins and minerals +12.5%. Management expects acute to grow in line with IPM in FY27.

segments.name: BSV specialty (domestic)
segments.commentary: Strong double-digit growth led by Anti-D, Foligraf (+52%) and HMG (+40%). Management says secondary sales for the brand are growing in mid-teens.

segments.name: Consumer Healthcare / OTC
segments.commentary: Q4 OTC revenue INR213 crores (+20%), with modern trade and e-commerce +57%. Share of e-commerce and modern trade rose from about 9% in FY25 to 13% in FY26. FY26 OTC INR879 crores (+9%).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 exports INR557 crores (+4%), hit by geopolitical headwinds and BSV exposure in LATAM, RCIS and the Philippines. FY26 international INR2,061 crores (+35%). Management expects high double-digit growth in FY27 for both international business units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at double digits or better, with aspiration to outperform IPM (IQVIA).
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided at 25.5% to 26.5%, better than FY26's 25.4%, with caveats on geopolitics and market conditions.
FY27 effective tax rate expected at 25% to 26%, up from 15-16% in FY26, as the Sikkim tax exemption ends.
Capex guidance of 6% to 7% of FY27 revenue, driven by the new Vadodara biotech facility; board approved up to INR500 crores investment in Mankind Medicare for this.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA expected at 0.5x for FY27; acquisition-related debt to be repaid by FY28. Next repayment INR1,250 crores in October 2026, and INR2,500 crores due in FY27.
Employee cost targeted at around 22% of sales over the long term (plus/minus 0.5%).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR737 crores (5.2% of revenue); FY27 capex guided at 6-7% of revenue.
New best-in-class biotech facility under construction in Vadodara, aligned with R&D and specialty focus.
Udaipur and Ambernath facilities received EU GMP certification during FY26, supporting semi-regulated market entry.
Board approved investment of up to INR500 crores in subsidiary Mankind Medicare for the Vadodara biotech plant; spend phased into the coming year.
demand_pricing: Price increase for FY26 was 4.2% per IQVIA versus about 4.4% for the industry.
Q4 IQVIA secondary sales growth 8.7% vs IPM 10.7% ex-GLP-1; muted anti-infective, with recovery in gastro, gynae, vitamins and derma QoQ.
Prescription share 15.1% and prescriber penetration 84.1%; ranked number 1 in prescriptions for the ninth consecutive year.
GLP-1: pen launched about one month before the call, targeting endocrinologists first; management said it is not launching vials or cutting prices.

Management attributed the Q2 onward recovery to acute therapies after corrective actions, with Q2, Q3 and Q4 growing sequentially. Raw material, packaging and excipient costs are disrupted due to the Middle East conflict; management said precautions were taken but gave no quantified impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is the disruption in sales teams behind us and is domestic business back to normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Juneja said corrections are done and the company is on the path to recovery; chronic (38-40% of sales) was not hit, only acute was.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-line growth guided to double digits, with aspiration to outperform IQVIA; EBITDA margin guided at 25.5-26.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q4 chronic outperformance only 0.9x IPM, and what is driving the high Q4 margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Sheetal Arora said there is no chronic pressure. Ashutosh Dhawan attributed the margin to a 60 bps gross margin gain, operating leverage, a Q4 FY25 relaunch base effect and a commission waiver.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall sequentially and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost fell 9% QoQ: about 5-5.5% from lower revenue, incentives and true-up, and about 3.5% from waiver of director and commission fees. Normalised for BSV, annual employee cost rose about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will GLP-1 launch and base diabetes be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management launched a pen only, is not in a hurry for vials or price cuts, and is focusing on adjacent vitamins, minerals and protein. Sudipta Roy said there has been no direct impact yet on base anti-diabetic and cardiac therapies.

qa_highlights.question: How is the price hike and growth built into FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited recovery in acute, sustained chronic outperformance, and specialty and GLP-1 contribution. Price hikes were in line with industry at 4.2% vs 4.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BSV acquisition playing out as expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Juneja said BSV brought biologicals and complex products and that the domestic leadership change has worked, with the Philippines leadership also changed. He added that the company is 18-19 months into integration and that it took longer than planned.

Chronic outperformance slowed to 0.9x IPM in Q4 FY26 from 1.1x for the full year; an analyst challenged this and management attributed it to no chronic pressure, so track quarterly chronic share.

There is no pressure on chronic therapies because it's a long-term growth story.
Acute therapy would be in the line of IPM growth.

543904|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the recovery and FY27 outlook, citing the Q2-to-Q4 sequential improvement and a commitment to hold margins, but it was cautious and at times evasive on specifics. It gave no quantified raw-material impact, declined to split export growth between Mankind and BSV, and caveated the EBITDA guidance for geopolitics and market conditions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA guided at 25.5-26.5% vs FY26 25.4%, so only flat to modest expansion, while Q4 hit 27.1% on a 60 bps gross margin gain and a commission waiver that may not repeat; the ETR rise is a PAT drag.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 volume grew 2.3% (vs 0.5% in FY25), domestic grew 14.4% with organic ex-OTC 8.6%, and acute is expected to grow in line with IPM after the Q2-Q4 sequential recovery.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at 6-7% of revenue (FY26 was INR737 crores, 5.2%), with INR500 crores board-approved for Vadodara and spend phased into the coming year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management aspires to outperform IQVIA with double-digit FY27 growth after Q4 revenue +11.8% and FY26 +17%, but Q4 chronic outperformance was only 0.9x IPM and acute is still recovering.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA guided at 25.5-26.5% but caveated for geopolitics, and raw material, packaging and excipient costs are disrupted by the Middle East conflict with no quantified impact; ETR steps up to 25-26% from 15-16%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: GLP-1 pen already launched about one month before the call targeting endocrinologists, with management not launching vials; specialty brands (Foligraf +52%, HMG +40%) and biologicals from BSV are ramping.

rows.label: International high double-digit growth in FY27
rows.why: Management guided high double-digit growth in both international units after FY26 international +35% to INR2,061 crores, though Q4 exports grew only 4% to INR557 crores due to LATAM, RCIS and Philippines BSV exposure.

rows.label: Net debt to adjusted EBITDA to 0.5x in FY27
rows.why: Net debt was INR3,932 crores (1.1x adjusted EBITDA) at 31 Mar 2026, with INR1,250 crores due in October 2026 and INR2,500 crores in FY27, against capex of 6-7% of revenue.

rows.label: Price increases in line with industry
rows.why: FY26 price increase was 4.2% vs industry 4.4% per IQVIA, and management cited pricing as part of the FY27 growth build without quantifying a FY27 price increase.

tone.note: Management was confident on acute recovery, double-digit FY27 growth and the Vadodara capex, but was cautious and evasive on raw-material impact, export split with BSV and the Q4 chronic slowdown to 0.9x IPM; analysts pushed on chronic outperformance, the employee cost drop and margin sustainability

543904|2026-06.headline: Mankind Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.9% YoY to INR4,031 crore and reported EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps to 26.3%, with PAT up 29.1% to INR574 crore.
543904|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 12.9% YoY to INR4,031 crore, led by BSV specialty and a 29% rise in international business. Domestic formulations (ex-Consumer Healthcare) grew 11% to INR3,180 crore, with chronic up 15.8% and acute recovering to 10.9% versus IPM. Margin expansion came from a 230 bps gross margin gain, with lower finance cost offset by a higher tax rate (25.4%). Management guided that gross margin will likely compress in coming quarters on commodity and dollar pressures, but kept full-year EBITDA guidance of 25.5% to 26.5%.

segments.commentary: Revenue rose 10.5% YoY to INR3,426 crore, driven by chronic growth of 15.8%, acute recovery and double-digit BSV growth. Secondary sales per IQVIA grew 12.7% with volume growth of 4.7%.

segments.name: Domestic ex-Consumer Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR3,180 crore. Chronic share ex-BSV rose 80 bps YoY to 40%, with cardiac up 19.4% and anti-diabetes up 12.7%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 29% YoY to INR605 crore, with management citing US launches and currency tailwind of 12-13%.

segments.name: BSV (Bio Specialty Vertical)

segments.name: Consumer Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR246 crore, with growth of about 3.8%. Cash and carry sales were stopped, and modern trade and e-commerce share rose to 15% from 11%, growing 38%.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25.5% to 26.5%.
Gross margin guided to be upward of 71% for FY27, with compression expected in the next quarter or so from higher commodity and dollar prices (West Asia cost pressure).
Domestic business expected to return to double-digit growth for the full year, with sequential improvement and chronic and acute both contributing.
BSV growth guided at high-teens for FY27.
Consumer Healthcare guided to high single-digit to double-digit growth from Q2 FY27 onwards.
Net operating working capital days expected to fall by year-end as inventory is rationalised.

Acquisition-related debt expected to be fully repaid by FY28; chronic share target of 50% over the medium term (4 to 5 years).
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR198 crore (4.9% of revenue) vs INR127 crore in Q1 FY26; FY27 guidance 6% to 7% of revenue.

Prescription share 15.2%, number 1 in prescriptions.
Price increases taken contributed to gross margin expansion; management said the price benefit had not fully flowed through due to inventory levels.
New introductions contributed 2.8% of sales vs IPM 4.1% (IPM includes GLP-1s), indicating softer launch contribution.

GLP-1 (semaglutide) launched late in anti-diabetes and gynaecology amid price war with 20+ companies and 35-40 brands; management is avoiding a price war and pursuing a therapy-led approach with KOL promotion. No export strategy for it.

qa_highlights.question: How will the remaining nine months of India growth look, and will Mankind consistently outperform IPM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic has returned to double-digit growth with better quality (chronic 15.8%, acute 10.9%, volume 4.7%). It expects progressive outperformance from chronic mix, hospitals, new divisions and under-penetrated states, though it did not commit to a specific multiple of IPM.

qa_highlights.question: How will BSV grow this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 BSV grew about 21% (domestic about 17%, international about 25%). Guidance is high-teens growth for FY27. Last year's growth was early teens, not 5-6%.

qa_highlights.question: Why will working capital stay elevated and will gross margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is slightly above normal, and management expects days to fall by year-end. Gross margin may compress in the next quarter from commodity and dollar pressures, but the 71%+ gross margin and 25.5%-26.5% EBITDA guidance were kept.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Consumer Healthcare growth slow, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash and carry sales were stopped because they hurt general trade. The market was softer. Modern trade and e-commerce grew 38% and reached 15% share. Guidance is high single-digit to double-digit growth from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Mankind cautious on launching GLP-1 (semaglutide), and what is the anti-diabetes covered-market story?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a strategic decision to avoid a crowded launch (20+ companies, 35-40 brands) and to focus on a therapy approach. Covered market in anti-diabetes rose from 56% in FY21 to 74% in FY26, and rank improved from 10 to 7 with a 4.5% share.

qa_highlights.question: What metrics show the reorganisation is working (attrition, share gains)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said attrition and vacancies are back to normal after a sharp drop. Acute growth improved from 3.3% in Q2 FY26 to 10.9% in Q1 FY27, and chronic from 12.2% to 15.8% over the same period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rivotril (Roche) acquisition worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Rivotril's IQVIA sales are about INR20-30 crore. Management said growth depends on specialist access and that the CNS category takes time. It aspires to build a gold portfolio in CNS.

543904|2026-09.headline: Mankind Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.3% YoY to Rs 4,338 crore, with EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 27.1%.

Domestic revenue rose 14.8% to Rs 3,657 crore, with India Rx-type growth outperforming IPM at 1.1x, driven by chronic and a recovering acute portfolio. International revenue grew 33% to Rs 680 crore, led by BSV specialty and new US launches. Consumer healthcare was weak at Rs 229 crore, and management guided only single-digit growth for FY27 in that segment.

543918|2026-06.headline: GHCL Textiles Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to Rs.410 crores, with EBITDA of Rs.70 crores (~17% margin) helped by cotton inventory gains.
543918|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs.410 crores (up 52% YoY), EBITDA Rs.70 crores and PAT Rs.39 crores. Management said the spread widened to about Rs.155/kg (with packing) from Rs.138/kg in Q4 FY26, helped by cotton bought earlier at lower prices. Fabric reached 16% of sales (vs 9% a year ago) as the first 15 of 40 planned knitting machines ran. Management guided a normalised EBITDA margin of 14-15% for FY27 and 16-18% once ready-to-cut fabric capacity is in place, and set a target of Rs.2,000 crores revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin ~17% (vs ~12% last year, per management)

financial_highlights.value: ~10-12% of sales price increase attributed to inventory gain (sales prices up ~20-24%)

segments.commentary: 89% of yarn production sold as yarn; 11% converted to fabric. Spinning utilisation ~99% per management, and 98%+ per the CEO's answer on volume. No new yarn capacity planned beyond knitting.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric is ~16% of sales, split roughly 50:50 woven and knitted. The 15 knitting machines run at 80-85% utilisation, with Q1 the first full quarter. Greige fabric contributed about Rs.65 crores this quarter.

FY27 capex of about Rs.100-120 crores including modernisation; about Rs.350-400 crores earmarked for ready-to-cut fabric facilities, subject to shareholder approval.

First 50 knitting machines installed and commercial production stabilised; 15 knitting machines received so far and 25 more to follow in phases through Q3 FY27.

PM MITRA Park (Tamil Nadu): land allotted in Q4 FY26; park completion targeted December 2027; GHCL must complete within three years of allotment. Fabric/processing plant planned for CY28, with part work possibly earlier.
In-house knitting capacity expected to be about 12-15% of total yarn production once all 40 machines are running.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices (domestic): Rs.62,000/candy in April, Rs.67,000 in May, Rs.64,000 in June, and back to about Rs.68,000-70,000 by the call. NY futures reached 80 cents/lb at end-June.

Order book healthy with 1.5-2 months of forward booking maintained. Exports to Europe (Germany, Italy and others) were strong in Q1; GHCL has no direct US/UK exposure and sells through process houses and garmenters.
Chinese yarn demand from India has risen since December 2025 (partly on lower Chinese cotton output); GHCL itself exports little to China. Q1 saw some slowdown in that demand.
Management says domestic textile demand is growing 6-8% YoY. Cotton is now at parity with imported cotton, supporting export competitiveness.
Cotton stock is held till November-December; further inventory plans depend on the monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cotton inventory position and the current spread?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is covered until the new season (Nov-Dec). Current spread is ~Rs.160/kg before packing (~Rs.155 after), up from ~Rs.138/kg in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin sustainable, and what does fabric contribution look like over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads should stay better than last year and similar in Q2, then depend on the market. Fabric to reach 30-40% of revenue after about three years as a ready-to-cut supplier, up from 15-16% now.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 EBITDA came from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales prices rose ~20-24%, but inventory gain accounted for only ~10-12%. The rest came from better pricing, customer mix and strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Q1 spread given rising cotton prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread can be held at current cotton levels of Rs.68,000-69,000/candy, but may compress if yarn prices lag. Q2 expected slightly below Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any capacity expansion on the yarn side besides knitting?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Only knitting machines are in the pipeline, plus about Rs.350 crores of capex for ready-to-cut fabric.

qa_highlights.question: How is the order book for H2 FY27, and are there US/UK/EU orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book healthy at 1.5-2 months forward. Strong European demand in Q1; no direct US/UK orders since GHCL supplies yarn and greige fabric as a tier-two vendor.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected once ready-to-cut is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised margin 14-15% for FY27; 16-18% after vertical integration (ready-to-cut fabric).

qa_highlights.question: What incentives come with the PM MITRA Park project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capital subsidy of about Rs.100-125 crores on a ~Rs.1,000 crore total investment under TN incentive schemes. The first inspection is done and the file is moving. The CEO said debt concessions were not a main factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the roadmap to double revenue to Rs.2,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue grows about 14% a year from ~Rs.1,350 crores in FY26 to reach Rs.2,000 crores by FY29. Growth comes from greige fabric and ready-to-cut fabric (Rs.350-400 crores of turnover at 1:1 or 1:0.8 asset turnover).

543918|2026-09.headline: GHCL Textiles Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR446 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 20.6%, with management guiding Q3 margins between Q1 and Q2 levels.
543918|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR446 crores (up 31% YoY, up 9% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR92 crores (up 141% YoY) at a 20.6% margin versus 11.2% a year earlier. Adjusted PAT was INR56 crores after excluding a one-time INR27 crore exceptional loss from a fire at a rented Tuticorin warehouse; reported PAT was INR36 crores. Cotton prices rose sharply late in the quarter, prompting buyers to restrict purchases to immediate needs, and management expects Q3 spreads and margins to fall between Q1 and Q2 levels. Management reiterated the INR2,500 crore revenue and 15–18% EBITDA margin goal for FY30 and announced a new INR410 crore spindle and rooftop solar project.

Management does not currently plan a share buyback; capital will go into growth.

11 MW ground solar expected to be commissioned by end Q3 (December 2026), taking total green energy to 76 MW; capex about INR32 crores.

Buyers limited purchases to immediate needs when cotton and yarn prices spiked late in Q2; management said domestic demand remains steady with strong order flow.
Government removed import duty on cotton, extended to December 2026; management says imported inventory build in the next three months will be limited.
UK and New Zealand FTAs are in force (benefits expected in about a year); India-EU agreement expected to be operational in early 2027; Oman FTA also mentioned.
Lower cotton inventory provided a gain that management described as not sizable. Working capital rise was mainly cotton advances, per CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further expansions beyond 58,000 spindles, and when will projects come on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Spindle project benefits expected full year FY29; PM MITRA processing unit around FY30; 11 MW solar in December 2026; 40 knitting machines by Q3 with results from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for spreads and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread rose from INR160/kg in Q1 to INR173/kg in Q2; Q3 expected between these levels. Demand described as robust across exports and domestic.

qa_highlights.question: What were the drivers of margin expansion and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers cited: higher fabric share, lower power costs from green energy, product optimisation with strategic customers, market tailwinds and some benefit from lower cotton inventory. Management believes Q1–Q2 margins are largely sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: How much was spent on the fire and is it insured?
qa_highlights.answer: Entire inventory was insured; investigation by police and forensics to conclude by Q3 end, with recovery expected by year end after deductible. Fire was at a rented godown away from factory premises; no prior such incident at factory.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,850 crore FY28 revenue figure guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not guidance but agreed that about INR1,800 crores in FY28 looks highly likely based on H1 run-rate.

qa_highlights.answer: Delay due to SIPCOT common infrastructure tenders and DPR redrafting; cushion built into timelines. Garmenting is being looked at favourably with nothing to announce; PM MITRA Park is settled and garmenting would be additional.

543923|2026-03.headline: IKIO Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to INR165 crores and FY26 revenue reached INR595 crores (+23%), with management guiding FY27 revenue growth of 20-22%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the ~90% YoY standalone revenue jump and margin expansion, but vague on other income, volume and value split, and value-added contribution, deferring several answers; only two individual investors asked questions and the Vietnam and Brazilian beef queries went unanswered.
